title: P1: Make SoilStateForecast ensemble-native and initialize it from the DA posterior

body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Split into a synthetic transition library and a probabilistic implementation.

**Audit verdict:** split

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #190` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Split into two issues. (190a, after #187 and #121): a member-wise synthetic transition library with process-specific laws (relaxation-mode bank for D, a lagged root-cohesion curve, an exponential for repellency) and parameter priors. AC: the prior predictive envelopes match the literature ranges cited in 03c, and member identity is preserved. (190b, after #198c, #162, #169 and #188): condition D/Φ on dv/v, with an identifiability gate. Update BLOCKED_BY to 190a:[187,121] and 190b:[198,162,169,188]. Remove the generic single-exponential formula.

### Problems found

- BLOCKED_BY encodes only #187 (gaia_group_issues.py:93); the body's prerequisites #198, #162, #169 and #121/#122/#124 are not enforced.
- It mixes synthetic transition research with real-data conditioning (roadmap-review R5 asks for this split).
- The transition law is wrong for coseismic healing and for root cohesion.
- The ACs 'recover jump/healing distributions … when identifiable' and 'burn perimeter gives distribution of reduced infiltration' depend on #121/#122/#132 deliverables that do not exist.

### Physics assessment

Making the states probabilistic is the right goal (distributions over the jump, τ, footprint and coupling), and the #145 firewall and member-identity requirements are right. The prescribed transition, z[t+dt] = z_eq + (z−z_eq)e^{−dt/τ} + J + η, is a single exponential and contradicts the log-linear healing of #121 and the chapter (03c:67-74). Use a log-spaced relaxation-mode bank (Snieder 2017) that stays Markov. Post-fire root cohesion is non-monotonic (lagged loss, then regrowth), not a relaxation toward equilibrium. Conditioning mechanical states on dv/v requires the #198 operator and the #169 identifiability check; the probabilistic roadmap's RBPF choice is not yet justified (science-review S3).

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #187, #121, #198.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

## Why this is needed

The memory/disturbance roadmap already defines coseismic damage, wildfire/tillage/landslide perturbations, event catalogs, hysteresis, and dv/v attribution (#119–#125). The proposed states are currently described mainly by nominal jumps and recovery times. Forecasting post-earthquake healing, landslide remolding, or post-fire soil recovery requires distributions over event magnitude, footprint, coupling, and relaxation time.

These states must remain separate from hydrologic storage while being able to modify hydraulic and strength parameters.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #187 for member/state conventions.
- Builds on #119/#120/#121/#122/#124/#125 and landslide parameters in #134.
- Dynamic conditioning/attribution depends on #162 and the identifiability checks in #169.
- Observation errors and petrophysical coupling use #164/#165/#168.
- Maintain the triggering firewall in #145: slow damage/healing is not a liquefaction pore-pressure trigger.
- Feeds the joint hazard-ensemble handoff after the hydrologic forecast issue.

## Proposed transition

For each mechanical/disturbance state `z`:

`z[t+dt] = z_eq + (z[t] - z_eq) exp(-dt/tau) + J_event + eta_z`

with member-level uncertainty in `J_event`, `tau`, spatial footprint, equilibrium, and coupling to Ks/cohesion/porosity/dv/v.

## Tasks

- [ ] Define distinct carried states for coseismic damage, surface disturbance, and post-fire/root-cohesion recovery.
- [ ] Define prior distributions and spatial correlation for event jumps, healing times, and coupling parameters.
- [ ] Sample event footprints from ShakeMap, fire severity, and landslide/event-location uncertainty.
- [ ] Apply parameter perturbations member-wise to hydraulic and mechanical models.
- [ ] Add observation operators enabling dv/v and other monitoring data to condition the mechanical ensemble.
- [ ] Quantify attribution conditioning over the actual record length before allowing joint state updates.
- [ ] Expose hydrologic and mechanical contributions separately in outputs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Synthetic ensembles recover known jump/healing distributions without confusing a seasonal hydrologic signal with damage when the problem is identifiable.
- Unknown or weakly identifiable components remain prior-dominated and are flagged.
- A burn perimeter produces a distribution of reduced infiltration/cohesion and multi-year recovery.
- Coseismic healing affects monitoring/mechanical state but is not passed as a liquefaction-triggering pore-pressure term.
- Member identity is preserved into downstream hazard calculations.

</details>

milestone.description:
[loop: Advance]

Soil state carries memory: capillary hysteresis (drying != wetting) and event-driven damage/recovery from earthquakes, liquefaction, landslides, wildfire, and farming (agroseismology). dv/v is the shared observable; attribution is the goal.

body:
**Amended 2026-11-09 by the soil-state review ladder (#296; record `docs/reviews/2026-11-07-fable-soil-state-review/`).** Issue-time freeze list.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Start with one documented error value per sensor type and a frozen list of held-back sensors; then the operators.

**Audit verdict:** split

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #189` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Split into three. (a) Agent-ready now: source one documented σ per non-dv/v sensor (instrument spec or validation paper, with citation), retire the two inconsistent placeholder sets (observability.py STREAMS; make_twin_gif.py:80-83), and pre-register station/time/domain holdouts as a versioned file. (b) Record schema plus point/probe-depth/satellite operators, after the #187 draft. (c) A gauge flux operator through the water-budget model's baseflow plus routing, and an aquifer-head operator. Acceptance should add: a gauge datum is never mapped linearly onto head; the probe-depth operator is tested against a known profile.

### Problems found

- Very broad: schema, eight operators, block R, holdouts, latency and provenance in one issue.
- Blocked by #187, which is stuck behind epic #171, although the per-sensor σ sourcing and the holdout pre-registration need no contract.
- The gauge operator as written is physically wrong.
- Holdouts must be frozen before the #192 tuning; this issue is where that happens, but the ordering is not stated.

### Physics assessment

A single time-aware observation record with datum age, native support, QC, R-block ID and a permanent role is the right missing layer. Part of it has landed: the measurement_target classifier, the water_table_observations() screen, and water_table_point_footprint, which refuses non-water-table wells (observability.py:945-978). Physics problems. 'Basin-integral gauge operators' as a linear average of head is wrong: discharge is a flux, related nonlinearly to storage and gradient. Yet STREAMS models USGS gauges as informing 'gwl' with kind='flux' and a flat noise of 0.05 (observability.py:899). The operator must be the model's own baseflow/runoff prediction, h(x) from the water-budget model, ideally routed (September audit S4). Soil probes at 5/20/50 cm need a depth operator onto the root-zone storage, not the identity. The aquifer-head operator for deep or confined wells remains open (2026-08-20 comment). The added task on per-sensor σ is correct: SMAP's ubRMSE target of 0.04 m³/m³ is unused, and the NWIS/SNOTEL placeholders are not traceable to instrument specs.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #187, #9.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

## Amendment 2026-11-09
Freeze at forecast issue time (manifest #305): forcing product and version, observation arrival times, calibration parameters and prior hyperparameters, dv/v reference window and epoch, well-centring baseline computed from pre-issue data only, code revision. Reliability claims use the blocked multi-event manifest of #305; a single event (#59) is illustrative.

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

## Why this is needed

The repository already fetches and/or models NWIS wells, SNOTEL/SCAN/USCRN soil moisture, SWE, USGS discharge, SMAP, and seismic dv/v; it also has point, satellite, channel, basin, and coda-footprint concepts. These are not yet exposed through one time-aware operational record consumed by a cycling filter.

The missing layer is not another downloader. It is a consistent observation object with actual datum age, native spatial/depth support, QC/bias state, covariance metadata, and a permanent assimilation-versus-validation designation.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #187 for the observation schema.
- Feeds #188's cycling nowcast.
- Builds on #28 (SNOTEL), #29 (native-scale satellite comparison), #30 (real dv/v), #6 (continuous-well validation), #9/#46 (aquifer screening), and existing USGS gauge/soil-station fetchers.
- Must implement #167 (datum age is not revisit cadence).
- Must respect #164/#165/#168 for correlated dv/v error, petrophysical gain, and coda-operator uncertainty.
- Coordinate with #156 for fixture-backed parser/assimilation tests.

## Tasks

- [ ] Define one observation-record table/dataset: value, units, time, arrival time, datum age, coordinates, depth/support, stream, QC, bias flag, operator ID, R block ID, and role.
- [ ] Adapt existing NWIS, AWDB/SNOTEL/SCAN, USCRN, gauge, SMAP, and seismic outputs without duplicating their fetch logic.
- [ ] Implement screened-well operators and soil-probe depth operators.
- [ ] Implement basin-integral gauge operators and retain satellite/coda native footprints.
- [ ] Construct block/non-diagonal R where observations share references, stations, retrieval errors, or processing choices.
- [ ] Assign stations/times to assimilation, calibration, or fully withheld validation before cycling.
- [ ] Handle late, missing, stale, and asynchronous observations explicitly.
- [ ] Persist operator and QC provenance with each analysis.

## Acceptance criteria

- A mixed fixture containing a well, soil probe, gauge, satellite pixel, and dv/v datum can be evaluated in one observation-space call.
- Actual timestamp/age, not nominal revisit interval, controls lag handling.
- Assimilation and validation records are mutually exclusive.
- Every residual is computed at the observation's native spatial and depth support.
- Correlated observations are not treated as independent diagonal-R replicates.
- Existing fetchers and deterministic native-scale validation remain usable.

---

**Added task (2026-07-21 review, [`docs/reviews/sensor-uncertainty-covariance-review.md`](../docs/reviews/sensor-uncertainty-covariance-review.md)):**

- [ ] Source one physical, documented sigma per non-dv/v sensor, and retire the two independently-invented, mutually inconsistent placeholder sets currently split across `src/models/observability.py`'s design catalog (e.g. `noise=0.02` for NWIS, `noise=0.03` for SNOTEL/SCAN) and `notebooks/make_twin_gif.py`'s demo constants (`WELL_VAR = 0.15**2`, `SM_VAR = 0.03**2`). Candidate sources: USGS reading precision / datum uncertainty for NWIS wells; the published SNOTEL/SCAN/USCRN probe accuracy spec; SMAP's published ubRMSE (~0.04 m³/m³, currently unused even though `fetch_smap.py` has no error assignment); USGS discharge/rating-curve error (currently a flat `noise=0.05` placeholder with no stage/discharge dependence). None of today's values traces to an instrument spec.


</details>

milestone.title: Applied math: DA estimator correctness
milestone.description:
[loop: Observe · Correct]

Make the assimilation theory sound: a real space-time treatment of time (not a scalar R inflation), an augmented estimator that can actually do the attribution the twin claims, a scalable and terrain-aware prior, correlated dv/v error, petrophysical gain in the operator, and the identifiability precondition for attribution. From the applied-mathematics review of the assimilation core.

title: P1: Operationalize ground-sensor observation records, operators, QC, and holdouts

body:
**Amended 2026-11-09 by the soil-state review ladder (#296; record `docs/reviews/2026-11-07-fable-soil-state-review/`).** Rescoped to the fixture slice (a); pilot and multi-sensor slices moved to #306 so production calibration gates deployment, not fixture verification.

**Rescoped 2026-10-18 for the MODFLOW 6 groundwater core.** Plan and design record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-modflow-groundwater-core/plan.md` (#273); epic #274.

## Purpose
Assimilate sensors into the coupled MODFLOW + land-surface state day by day, with an ensemble
that stays calibrated.

## Deliverable (one slice per PR, `Refs #188`)
**(a) Fixture.** (1) Linear-Gaussian exact case first: one confined layer (MF6 linear in h), AR(1)
Gaussian recharge noise, point heads; the EnKF at N = 500 matches the exact Kalman mean and
covariance within Monte Carlo error at every cycle (this also fixes the time convention).
(2) Fixture OSSE: nature run independent of the forecast ensemble, operator evaluated on nature;
Q from day one (AR(1)-perturbed precipitation, temperature and LSM drainage; parameter ensemble
from PEST++; RTPS or adaptive inflation); diagnostics from day one (spread/RMSE, Desroziers
consistency, standardized innovations, rank histograms, 90% coverage, lag-1 innovation
autocorrelation per stream with a stated threshold). (3) UZF test: truth differing only in the
last 60 days of infiltration; head-only vs head + UZF water content update; the transit-time
threshold above which UZF state is added is set from this. Ledger closure across water-table
movement.
**(b) and (c)** moved to #306 (pilot, wells only; multi-sensor), which waits for this issue, #285, #9 and #235.

Localization tapers with distance and hydrogeologic connectivity; no hard zeros across layers
or unconnected models (test: N = 1000 fixture with two unconnected models and correlated forcing).
No innovation-mean requirement.
The posterior object is the member set; marginal sigma is a derived export, never the analysis product.

## Hard blockers
Blocked by: #289, #187.

## Advisory follow-ups
#192 (B/Q/R), #239 (correlated observation errors), #194 (withheld-sensor value).

<details><summary>Scope before the 2026-11-09 review-ladder amendment (archived, not current)</summary>

## Purpose

**(b) Pilot, wells only.** Only well-years with the "assimilation" role in #235; no inner-loop
parameter augmentation; held-out coverage reported with and without data overlap.
**(c) Multi-sensor.** Gauges as total SFR outflow (#237), soil moisture (#290), dv/v from
non-overlapping stacks through #198 with an AR(1) bias state, GNSS (#226) if shown above noise.

Localization tapers with distance and hydrogeologic connectivity; no hard zeros across layers

<details><summary>Scope before the 2026-10-18 MODFLOW refactor (archived, not current)</summary>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** First a synthetic cycling test on a small fixture, then a real pilot basin assimilating continuous well records only.

**Audit verdict:** split

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #188` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Split into (a) a synthetic identical-twin OSSE cycling pilot on a small fixture: wells and probes only, BLOCKED_BY [187-schema-draft, 155, 156]. Acceptance: with no observations, reproduce the open loop bit-for-bit under fixed seeds; with a near-perfect observation, spread contracts only in the observed subspace; bounded-transform mass ledger closes to 1e-9; spread/RMSE ratio within 0.8-1.2 over 100 cycles on the truth run; no dense n×n matrix. (b) Real-observation cycling, blocked by #189. (c) dv/v assimilation, blocked by #164/#198.

### Problems found

- BLOCKED_BY [154, 187, 189]. #154 is closed, so it is effectively [187, 189], and #187 is stuck behind epic #171.
- The September follow-up review says a synthetic filter fixture may precede live-record integration, but the hard #189 dependency prevents an OSSE pilot.
- Its dv/v scope depends on #164/#165/#168/#198 (only stated in prose); it should be scoped out of the hydrology pilot.

### Physics assessment

LETKF/EnKF over storage states, with native-support operators and localization by hydrographic or hydrogeologic connectivity, is the right next estimator, and doing hydrology first is right. Physics gaps in the body. (1) 'Enforce state bounds' by clipping members creates or destroys water and biases the mean. Use a bounded transform (anamorphosis/logit) or book the clipped mass in the DA-increment ledger as a non-physical flux. (2) A bucket or water-budget model is strongly dissipative, so forcing perturbations alone will collapse the spread. Parameter perturbation and Q (from #192) are needed from day one, not later. (3) Temporally correlated observation errors (dv/v Cd with a 3-day correlation; satellite retrieval bias) violate the white-noise assumption. (4) 'Invariant to observation ordering' holds for LETKF but only approximately for a serial EnSRF with localization; state the tolerance. (5) The flagship notebook make_twin_gif.py:248-252 still updates frames independently and injects synthetic observations (science review :85).

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #187, #189, #155, #156, #232, #233.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

## Why this is needed

The repository now has a sound static observation-space BLUE, correct OU gain/drift treatment for lagged data, native-support operators, and a Matérn prior with hydrographic region masking. The wet-season twin still applies independent BLUE corrections to frames on a deterministic trajectory, discards posterior covariance, and restarts from a prescribed prior at the next frame.

That is not a Kalman nowcast. The analysis uncertainty never becomes the next forecast's initial uncertainty, and model/process uncertainty is not propagated.

## Dependencies

- Depends on #187 for the ensemble/state contract.
- Builds on the partial fixes in #161 (OU lag treatment is landed; dynamic propagation remains) and #163 (Matérn + region masking landed; scalable representation remains).
- Depends on #154 for a production-scale strategy; a localized ensemble pilot may proceed before a full SPDE/GMRF implementation.
- Uses #164/#165/#168 for defensible observation errors/operators.
- Uses #155 for deterministic ensemble random streams and #156 for fixture-backed assimilation tests.
- Can prototype on the current calibrated daily budget, but release depends on #171/#172/#137.
- Supersedes the independent-frame update pattern in `notebooks/make_twin_gif.py`; coordinate with #162 before augmenting with damage/disturbance states.

## Proposed method

Implement a localized EnKF/LETKF cycle over storage-based hydrologic states:

`x[t+1,f,e] = M(x[t,a,e], u[t,e], p[e]) + eta[t,e]`

followed by an observation-space analysis at each cycle. Start with hydrology only; add mechanical memory after stability and calibration are demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] Define forecast, observation, localization, inflation, constraint, and persistence interfaces.
- [ ] Propagate every ensemble member through the daily water-budget/snow model.
- [ ] Use observation operators at native spatial and depth support.
- [ ] Carry the analysis ensemble and covariance into the next forecast cycle.
- [ ] Localize by distance plus hydrographic/hydrogeologic connectivity; prevent leakage across divides.
- [ ] Enforce state bounds and recompute diagnostic variables from corrected storage.
- [ ] Record per-member and ensemble-mean DA storage increments separately from physical fluxes.
- [ ] Retain the static BLUE as a tested limiting/reference case.
- [ ] Add a small fixture-based cycling experiment before scaling to the 2.96 M-cell domain.

## Acceptance criteria

- Sequential observations affect later forecasts through the updated ensemble.
- Posterior covariance is not discarded between frames.
- With no observations, the cycle reproduces the open-loop ensemble forecast.
- With a near-perfect synthetic observation, spread contracts in the observed subspace without becoming negative or collapsing globally.
- Storage bounds hold and each analysis increment is auditable.
- Results are invariant to observation ordering within numerical tolerance.
- The implementation runs without materializing a dense full-domain cell-by-cell covariance.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** The format for state, uncertainty and sensors. Slice (a) schema draft can start now; release waits for the water-budget fixes.

**Audit verdict:** split

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #187` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Split into (a) a schema draft: xarray/Zarr ensemble_member contract, units/support/provenance, the DA-increment ledger, and the S/h_wt/D/H/u distinction with a ΔD = -Δh_wt round-trip test. BLOCKED_BY only #52. (b) A release qualification blocked by #186, #89, #137 and #172 (leaf issues, never #171). Relax E2S to 'an adapter maps the contract to E2S CoordSystem without data copies; native projected x/y retained'.

### Problems found

- BLOCKED_BY [186, 52, 89, 137, 171, 172] includes epic #171, which is human-closed, so this holds indefinitely. That in turn holds #189, #188, #192, #194, #205, #190, #191, #193, #195, #200-#203. The body itself allows a prototype on the current skeleton, with #171/#172/#137 as release dependencies only (roadmap-review R3).
- #52 (no milestone) is the real schema prerequisite and sorts late (batch 25 per the September audit).
- Acceptance mixes schema tests with release claims ('the same object initializes nowcast, forecast and hazard handoff').
- The E2S coordinate constraint is over-specified.

### Physics assessment

Storage as the primary state, with head/DTW/θ/pressure derived, is the right architecture, and the 2026-08-20 comment is right to separate S, h_wt, D, H (screened head) and u. src/models/hydro_state.py already implements the vocabulary and conversions; no ensemble schema exists anywhere in src. 'Bias states' in x need an identifiability caveat, because a bias state is only observable against an unbiased reference stream. The Earth2Studio addendum conflicts with the native EPSG:5070 90 m x/y grid: E2S models assume lat/lon coordinates, so 'round-trips without renaming or reordering dims' over-constrains the contract. An adapter should map the coordinates instead.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #52.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

## Why this is critical

The repository already has important probabilistic pieces: calibrated marginal coverage diagnostics, forcing-method ensembles, native-support operators, processing-ensemble dv/v covariance, a correct OU treatment for lagged observations, and a Matérn prior with hydrographic region masking. Those pieces currently live in separate objects, while the operational forecast and snapshot BLUE still exchange deterministic fields and marginal variances.

A fully probabilistic twin needs one contract that preserves dependence across hydrologic states, parameters, forcing, process error, observations, and later mechanical memory. Independently sampling GWL, soil moisture, and parameters can violate the water budget and destroy physically important covariance.

## Dependencies and relationship to existing work

- Depends on #52 for one unambiguous definition of the soil-moisture product.
- Incorporates the corrected Stage-3 uncertainty from #186.
- Can be prototyped against the currently calibrated daily water-budget skeleton, but operational release depends on the storage-account review in #171/#172 and specific-yield separation in #137.
- Builds on the existing native-support observation operators and the OU/Matérn work associated with #161/#163.
- Provides the interface for #162, #28/#29/#32, #71, #121/#122/#134, and hazard handoffs #127/#139.
- Coordinate with #64/#65 and the existing GAIA Zarr/STAC provenance conventions.

## Required state contract

Primary state should be storage based, for example:

`x = [S_root, S_vadose_or_transit, S_groundwater, SWE, S_interflow, bias states]`

The exact storage partition is finalized by #171/#172. Head, DTW, theta, saturation, recharge, and pore-pressure quantities should be derived consistently rather than updated as independent copies.

The schema must distinguish:

- state/initial-condition uncertainty;
- parameter uncertainty;
- meteorological forcing uncertainty;
- process/model-discrepancy uncertainty;
- observation and representativeness error;
- structural/method uncertainty;
- mechanical damage/disturbance uncertainty;
- native versus delivered resolution/support.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a canonical xarray/Zarr schema with an `ensemble_member` dimension.
- [ ] Define required coordinates, units, masks, hydrogeologic/basin IDs, timestamps, datum age, spatial/depth support, and provenance.
- [ ] Define parameter and forcing member tables and correlation/member-pairing rules.
- [ ] Define observation records, operators, R metadata, and assimilation/validation designation.
- [ ] Define deterministic summaries derived from members: mean, median, sigma, quantiles, and exceedance probability.
- [ ] Define a DA-increment ledger separate from physical fluxes.
- [ ] Add schema validation and round-trip tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- A synthetic coupled ensemble round-trips through Zarr without losing member identity or metadata.
- Soil moisture and GWL are not independently resampled from marginal sigma fields.
- All state variables and uncertainty components declare units and native support.
- Member-level water storage and DA increments can be audited.
- The same object initializes the nowcast, forecast, and downstream hazard handoff.
- Existing deterministic products remain derivable for backward compatibility.

---

**Added criterion (2026-07-21 Opus strategy review, [`docs/reviews/opus-digital-twin-evolution-review-2026-07-21.md`](../docs/reviews/opus-digital-twin-evolution-review-2026-07-21.md)):** design this contract to be Earth2Studio-shaped *from the start*, because it is the single artifact that decides whether interop is a cheap constraint or an expensive retrofit.

- [ ] The `ensemble_member` dimension and its companions (`lead_time`, `variable`, and the spatial coordinates) follow **Earth2Studio conventions** (coordinate names, ordering, and dims), so the model-structure/assimilation adapter (new Earth2Studio compatibility issue) is a thin wrapper over this contract rather than a schema translation on top of it.

**Acceptance addition:** the canonical object round-trips through an Earth2Studio-style `CoordSystem`/`OrderedDict` coords contract without renaming or reordering dimensions. Rationale: interop is cheapest as a constraint on the contract, most expensive as an adapter over a bespoke schema.

</details>

title: P0: Define the canonical probabilistic state, parameter, forcing, and observation contract

body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Uncertainty units fix for the statistical map; stays on hold until the PI releases it.

**Audit verdict:** hold-human

### Specification

Split into two issues. (a) Agent-ready once released: an 'NST-σ units guard'. Every σ array carries variable, units, transform space and support. All four producers either export back-transformed metres (Gauss-Hermite or Monte Carlo through the fitted anamorphosis, with a lognormal closed-form test and an identity/affine reduction test) or tag the output 'nst' and refuse quadrature. uncertainty_stack and landlab_export raise on mixed spaces or missing components instead of zero-filling. Tests are scale-equivariance (rescaling residuals 10× scales σ 10×) and the closed-form oracle. (b) Hold for a human: empirical coverage, declustering, tail model and per-domain recalibration, blocked by #153. Open a separate P0 for the sign bug (see gaps). Release the hold explicitly.

### Problems found

- Labelled needs-human-decision but dispatched alone as queue batch 2; the grouper does not honour the hold. Part of the park cause was a reviewer returning verdict None (an infrastructure failure).
- Acceptance treats coverage as validation of a units fix (monotone invariance), and needs processed rasters that are not in the repo (the panel noted data/processed has JSON only), so it cannot be tested in an agent environment without #153 fixtures.
- Scope lists only Stage 3, while three other producers have the same defect.
- The DTW sign bug found during planning has no issue of its own.

### Physics assessment

Confirmed, and wider than the title. The σ is computed in normal-score space but labelled as metres at four places: interpolate_residuals.py:78-100 (written as 'kriging_std_m', units m, at :200); baseline_regression.py:446-467 (written to baseline_kriging_std_m.tif at :508); climate_response.py:160-176 (β σ); and interpolate_anomalies.py:243-246 (a quantile shortcut). Downstream, landlab_export.py:205-208 adds it in quadrature with metre-valued RF σ, so the hazard export is affected. The asked-for method (sample the conditional Gaussian and push it through the anamorphosis) is right, with two caveats from the panel. First, coverage of a quantile interval does not change under a monotone back-transform, so acceptance item 4 cannot be satisfied by this fix and conflates two things. Second, QuantileTransformer's inverse clips to the observed range, so the far-field back-transformed variance is set by one or two extreme wells unless a tail model is added. The same panel also found a separate critical sign bug: interpolate_residuals.py:203-207 computes dtw_final = baseline_dtw + wte_anomaly + wte_residual. Both terms are water-table-ELEVATION anomalies, positive upward (interpolate_anomalies.py:114 defines anomaly = wte - median), so the DTW anomaly is sign-inverted. This is live through Makefile:185 and pixi.toml:97.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

## Why this is critical

Stage-3 residuals are normal-score transformed before PyKrige. The kriging mean is inverse-transformed, but the returned kriging variance remains in transformed, dimensionless space and is subsequently treated as if it were in `m²`. It is therefore not commensurate with metre-scale RF spread or response uncertainty.

A fully probabilistic state cannot be initialized from an uncertainty field with mixed units. This can produce misleading interval width and corrupt every downstream DA, forecast, and hazard probability.

## Dependencies

- Part of #1.
- Coordinate with #5 (coverage/PIT/CRPS; closed but its calibration tests must be rerun).
- Coordinate with #7 (domain-specific nugget/representativeness variance).
- Blocks the canonical probabilistic-state contract and ensemble initialization.
- Blocks trustworthy propagation into #64, #142, and #144.

## Tasks

- [ ] Identify and document the stochastic variable and units returned by each Stage-3 uncertainty component.
- [ ] Back-transform the full kriging predictive distribution by conditional sampling or numerical integration; do not apply a naive inverse transform to variance.
- [ ] Produce mean, variance, and requested quantiles in physical GWL/DTW units.
- [ ] Prevent missing uncertainty components from being silently replaced by zero.
- [ ] Recompute the total static uncertainty without adding variances of incompatible variables or supports.
- [ ] Rerun spatial-block coverage, PIT, and CRPS per hydrogeologic domain.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every uncertainty array carries variable name, units, spatial support, and provenance.
- No transformed-space/dimensionless variance is added to a variance in `m²`.
- Monte Carlo tests recover the analytical result for an identity transform and a known nonlinear transform.
- Empirical 90% coverage is within the #5 gate in cored domains, or an explicit recalibration is applied.
- Downstream exports contain no zero uncertainty caused solely by a missing component.

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Its pieces go to the valley (#233), snow (#234) and θ-product issues; the rest is closed out.

**Audit verdict:** split

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #177` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Split into: (a) m5 HAND<d0 ratchet as a P1 bug (or fold into #175); (b) m1 snow state + rain-on-snow/liquid retention (combine with the SWE-state gap); (c) m2 documented as a product statement, with retiring the monthly product as a needs-human-decision item tied to #89/#52; (d) m3 texture-dependent drainage via K(theta), folded into #131 (the same K(theta) sets celerity); (e) drop m4 as covered by #58 and fix the docstrings.

### Problems found

- It mixes a P1 bug (m5), a P1 flood mechanism (m1), a product-identity decision (m2), and a stale item (m4) under a P2 'minor' label, which the roadmap review (line 101) also flags.
- A single agent pass would Close #177 on a partial checklist.
- It is in batch 6, before the storage restructure.

### Physics assessment

m1, rain-on-snow: real. Degree-day melt (forecast.py:105-131) misses the turbulent fluxes that dominate melt in warm atmospheric rivers. It also passes rain straight through the pack with no liquid retention or refreezing (:130), which over-delivers on cold packs. So the bias goes both ways. m2, two inconsistent models: real. The shipped product is monthly TerraClimate with a drain-to-nowhere bucket (soil_moisture.py:162-187, 291-293, 330). m3, Ksat unused: real. drain_tau is 2 d regardless of texture (water_budget.py:73). m4, Hamon PET: partly stale. Calibration forcing uses daily Hargreaves-Samani (fetch_prism_daily.py:9-12,156), though forecast.py:12 and stage_mvp_window.py:9 still say Hamon, and #58 covers Penman-Monteith. m5, valley ratchet: a confirmed defect, not 'verify' (probe above).

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

From the ParFlow review:
- [ ] Rain-on-snow is absent — degree-day melt (`forecast.py:105-131`) has no energy balance; rain-on-snow (turbulent+advective) is the PNW extreme-antecedent flood mechanism and will under-melt during warm atmospheric rivers (m1).
- [ ] Two inconsistent ET/hydrology models coexist: hard ET cap `min(PET,S-Swp)` (`water_budget.py:238`, no stress function fc->wp) vs Thornthwaite-Mather (`soil_moisture.py:139-155`); and the SHIPPED 90 m soil-moisture product (`soil_moisture.py:292,452`) drains water out of the system — the exact #43/#44 gap the coupled budget fixed. The 'coupled twin' and the published SM product are not the same model; state it (m2).
- [ ] Ksat is computed (`soil_moisture.py:107-109`) and never used; unsaturated K(theta) is absent — gravity drainage is a fixed `drain_tau_days=2.0` identical for sand and clay (m3).
- [ ] PET is Hamon (temperature-only) — weak for summer drawdown that sets antecedent deficit (m4).
- [ ] Valley-floor cells (HAND~=0) are frozen: head0->0 disables discharge while VSA caps rise, so baseflow originates only mid-slope — verify it does not bias the spatial baseflow field (m5).

</details>

body:
**Addendum 2026-10-18 (MODFLOW 6 groundwater core; plan #273, epic #274):** #172 and #131 are superseded by MODFLOW UZF. Hysteresis now acts on the land-surface root zone; it waits on the ledger slice (a) in #232 and the operator in #198.

---

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Capillary hysteresis changes water fluxes, not only seismic velocity; blocked until the store and operator exist.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite (verifier corrected: The physics is correct: forecast.py:168-174 uses vadose_dvv_hysteretic only on the dv/v output, while theta comes from the single-valued budget. However, the issue has no acceptance criterion, bundles an unrelated SIGMA0/G_REF calibration (dvv_coupling.py:47-48), and sits in batch 6 [227,225,177,176], ahead of the #172 restructure. The audit itself lists these problems plus a missing blocker, so the verdict should be 'rewrite', not 'keep'. Physics caveat for the proposed acceptance: K(theta) is nearly non-hysteretic, so drainage hysteresis has to enter through the psi-dependent field-capacity threshold or gradient. Also, closed-loop invert_dvv equality (dvv_coupling.py:126) requires a path-aware inversion.)

### Specification

Move SIGMA0/G_REF calibration to the dv/v family. Acceptance: same final theta reached by wetting vs drying gives different drainage; ledger passes; invert_dvv theta equals budget theta on a closed loop. Add BLOCKED_BY 176:[172] and 198:[187,176].

### Problems found

- It is in batch 6, the first water-budget batch, before #172 restructures the same loop. That means rework and conflicts.
- It bundles an unrelated dv/v calibration (SIGMA0/G_REF) that needs data.
- It has no acceptance criterion.
- #198 depends on it (roadmap review line 43, dependency review line 27), but that is not in BLOCKED_BY.

### Physics assessment

Accurate: forecast.py:166-174 applies Kool-Parker hysteresis to the dv/v output only, so the theta trajectory is single-valued. In a theta-only bucket, hysteresis enters physically as a path-dependent drainage endpoint: a wetting-branch vs drying-branch effective theta_fc, with Delta-theta about 0.02-0.05. That is second-order next to the missing vadose store. The SIGMA0/G_REF magnitude calibration (dvv_coupling.py:47-48) is a separate dv/v petrophysics task that needs observed dv/v.

### Order and dependencies
Blocked by: #232, #198.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`forecast.py:168-174` swaps in `vadose_dvv_hysteretic` for dv/v while the theta trajectory comes from the SINGLE-VALUED `coupled_water_budget` (groundwater M5). Capillary hysteresis is fundamentally a STORAGE process — the retention curve sets held water, hence drainage/recharge fluxes and the soil-moisture memory #120 invokes. Implementing it only in the Hertz-Mindlin velocity map makes the loop cosmetic: it decorates the seismic output but changes no water flux, and `invert_dvv` would return a theta disagreeing with the budget's theta.

**Do:** route the hysteretic retention through the water-budget drainage/infiltration branch so the INTEGRATED state carries the memory (the remaining half of #120); also calibrate the SIGMA0/G_REF magnitude the loop uses.

</details>

body:
> **Superseded 2026-10-18** by SFR exchange, #284 and #286 under the PI's decision to make MODFLOW 6 the groundwater core (plan `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-modflow-groundwater-core/plan.md`, PR #273; epic #274). Held from the agent queue by the `superseded` label. Closing is the PI's call after reviewing the replacement.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Groundwater drains to streams at a per-cell rate from a spun-up run; model BFI from the simulated hydrograph; held-out gauges.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite (verifier corrected: The physics premise is right: the steady-state anchor is gw_recess=(R_ref/S_y)/head0 (water_budget.py:193-196), and R_ref is fitted to BFI (:56-61; calibrate_fluxes.py:6-10). But 'keep' contradicts the audit's own findings: two missing blockers, a missing ratchet fix and no validation design. Probe results: HAND<=d0 cells get zero baseflow and the table rises 5.0->2.05 m in year 1 and reaches the surface (wt -0.03 m) by year 3 under ~1570 mm/yr. That is much larger than the audit's +0.51 m/yr, which depends on the forcing. R_ref=3 mm/d (1095 mm/yr) is about 2.4x BFI*Q/P*P (~458 mm/yr) and about 2x the code's own comment of ~1.6 mm/d (:86-88). As a result, slope cells drain the observed baseline (5.0->8.55 m over 3 yr, baseflow 1023 mm/yr vs recharge 668 mm/yr), and the 10-month calibration counts storage depletion as baseflow. Per-cell Boussinesq b also risks double counting: the HAND-distributed linear tau (=100*head0 d) already gives a nonlinear aggregate recession (Harman et al. 2009). Recession tests must therefore be done on the basin aggregate.)

### Specification

Add: (1) anchor R_ref per cell to the long-term mean recharge from a spun-up multi-year daily run, and check that the domain mean is consistent with BFI*Q/P*P; (2) fix the HAND < d0 ratchet; (3) compute model BFI with Lyne-Hollick on the basin-aggregated model Q; (4) validate on held-out gauges and years. Add BLOCKED_BY 175:[172, 70 (rewritten multi-year forcing)].

### Problems found

- The valley-floor ratchet (#177 m5) belongs here, not under 'minor'. With HAND < d0 there is no discharge and head ratchets up (probe: +0.51 m/yr, zero baseflow).
- It needs basin masks, a multi-year spun-up record and a frozen holdout set, none of which exist (calibrate_fluxes.py:48,61).
- If b is fit from the same gauge recessions, a recession check is calibration, not validation.

### Physics assessment

Correct, and worse than stated. R_ref = 3 mm/d (:88), about 1095 mm/yr. The targets imply long-term baseflow of 0.47 x 0.65 x 1500, about 460 mm/yr or 1.25 mm/d. So at the 'observed baseline' the cells discharge about 2.4x their sustainable recharge and the table drains through the run (probe: HAND 6 and 30 m cells lose 1-3 m/yr). BFI is contaminated by storage depletion over a 10-month run with no spin-up. The recession timescale is S_y*head0/R_ref: 100 d at head0 = 1 m, 13.7 yr at 50 m. Ridges barely recede. A Boussinesq nonlinear recession (b about 1.5 late-time, Brutsaert & Nieber 1977) is appropriate. Model BFI must come from the same Lyne-Hollick filter applied to the modelled basin hydrograph, not from bf/Q flux bookkeeping (calibrate_fluxes.py:72-75).

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #232, #233.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`water_budget.py:188-197`: `gw_recess=(R_ref/S_y)/head0` with R_ref=3 mm/day a single DOMAIN-CONSTANT used to force 'observed baseline = steady state', then R_ref is itself calibrated to BFI (`:56-61`) and BFI is reported as validation of the sink — the sink is set to reproduce a baseflow fraction, then the fraction is presented as independent agreement (groundwater M4). Recharge is spatially variable, so the steady-state anchor is only self-consistent where cells get 3 mm/day. The legacy `drop=h*recess` (`:268`) is a LINEAR reservoir; Brutsaert (cited) recession is NONLINEAR (Boussinesq dQ/dt ~ -Q^b, b~1.5-2), so exponential recession systematically misfits observed limbs.

**Do:** spatially-consistent recharge anchor; a nonlinear (Boussinesq) recession; and BFI validated on data the sink was NOT fit to.

</details>

body:
**Rescoped 2026-10-18 for the MODFLOW 6 groundwater core.** Plan and design record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-modflow-groundwater-core/plan.md` (#273); epic #274.

## Purpose
Western-Cascades stormflow moves laterally in colluvium over bedrock, inside the root zone that
the land-surface model owns under the #265 partition. MODFLOW does not see it. It also carries
the pore pressure that slope stability consumes. (Kept open after review round 1, item H2.)

## Deliverable
A lateral root-zone flux in the LSM on sloping cells, routed downslope on the 90 m flow
directions with a documented transmissivity decay with depth, conserving water cell to cell
and handing what reaches a channel cell to SFR.

## Acceptance
- Cell-to-cell exchange sums to zero over the domain except at channel cells (ledger, #232).
- Quickflow fraction and recession at 12097500 and 12115000 with and without the lateral flux,
  reported.

## Hard blockers
Blocked by: #232.

## Advisory follow-ups
#133 (convergence in hollows).


<details><summary>Scope before the 2026-10-18 MODFLOW refactor (archived, not current)</summary>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** One perched-water store on the soil-bedrock/till contact that drains downslope (shared with #130 and #133).

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Rewrite the Do section as: a perched interflow store on the soil-bedrock/till contact, a kinematic outflow K_h*sin(b)*H/L, flux routed downslope via flow accumulation (or explicitly sent to the stream, stating which), and a slope from the 10 m DEM aggregated as mean tan(b) per 90 m cell. Ka is reported as an effective parameter, with the anisotropy formula corrected or relabelled. Acceptance: ledger passes; interflow recession timescale vs held-out storm hydrograph recessions at gauges; coordinate one state with #133. BLOCKED_BY 174:[172].

### Problems found

- 'Re-fit Ka within a physical range' cannot be satisfied with the current formula and will push an agent to tune.
- It does not depend on #172 but edits the same lines (:247-250).
- It overlaps #130/#133 (the roadmap review asks for one shared perched/interflow state).
- 'Report the residual' does not say against what. Q/P is a calibration target.

### Physics assessment

The issue is right that interflow is an instantaneous fixed fraction (:247-249) with no hillslope memory. It is wrong about why Ka looks too low. f_lat = Ka*tan(b)/(1+Ka*tan(b)) is the ratio of slope-parallel to slope-normal Darcy flux. For gravity drainage in an anisotropic slope, the lateral:vertical ratio is (Ka-1)*sin(b)*cos(b)/(Ka*sin^2(b) + cos^2(b)) (Zaslavsky & Sinai 1981), which is zero for isotropic soil. The code gives 19% lateral at Ka=1 and 13 deg. So the fitted Ka is a lumped coefficient, and 'refit within 10-100' is not a meaningful target. With 90 m slopes biased low (true slopes are steeper), correcting the slope at fixed Q/P drives Ka down further. Real subsurface stormflow comes from perching on the soil/till/bedrock contact and is threshold-driven: a kinematic perched store, q = K_h*sin(b)*H_perched (Sloan & Moore 1984), with soil thickness already available (baseline_wt_domain.py:62). Interflow also leaves at the cell with no downslope convergence, so hollows never get wetter. That matters for landslide pore pressure (#130/#133).

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #172, #265.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`water_budget.py:199-206,248-249`: `f_lat=Ka*tanb/(1+Ka*tanb)` skims a fixed drainage fraction downslope INSTANTANEOUSLY each step — no hillslope storage-discharge hydrograph. The team flags Ka=2 is 5-50x below the 10-100 forest-soil range and 'absorbs other processes' (groundwater M3). Part is real (90 m tanb underestimates hillslope gradient), but a term that is both the dominant runoff producer and a fudge factor 25x off range is not a validated parameterization.

**Do:** add a transient interflow store with hillslope memory; correct the 90 m slope bias; re-fit Ka within a physical range and report the residual.

</details>


</details>

body:
> **Superseded 2026-10-18** by partition option B in #265 and the seepage return in #280 under the PI's decision to make MODFLOW 6 the groundwater core (plan `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-modflow-groundwater-core/plan.md`, PR #273; epic #274). Held from the agent queue by the `superseded` label. Closing is the PI's call after reviewing the replacement.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Surface runoff only when the column is actually full; no double counting of root-zone pore space.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Replace '#...' with #172. Acceptance: (1) the deficit is computed from U and the root store with no double count, and the ledger test passes; (2) report runoff by mechanism (VSA, root-zone excess, interflow) per gauged basin; (3) an independent check: the modelled saturated-area fraction in wet-season storms vs NWI wetland/riparian area or TWI-saturation maps for Newaukum. Do not use Q/P, because that is a calibration target. Add BLOCKED_BY 173:[172] and the ratchet-fix gap issue.

### Problems found

- The body depends on '#...', a placeholder for the store issue (#172) that was never filled in. That dependency is not in BLOCKED_BY.
- It is batched before #172 in batch 7, so it would be implemented first.
- It has no testable acceptance criterion.
- There is no independent check of saturated-area extent.

### Physics assessment

The arithmetic is correct. deficit = S_y*dtw*1000 (:230), so at 5 m, 1500 mm, and at 0.5 m, 150 mm. VSA effectively never fires except where d0 is under about 0.5 m. The root-zone space is counted twice (:230 and :236). Runoff Q/P is therefore produced mostly by interflow (Ka), not VSA, which contradicts the docstring (:15-19). The physically right deficit is the unsaturated storage deficit, integral of (theta_s - theta) over the column, taken from the new store U. Additional bias: the valley-floor ratchet (HAND < d0, :195) pushes those cells up to the surface over time and makes VSA fire artificially there.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #172.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`water_budget.py:230-231`: `deficit=S_y*wt_depth*1000; sat_runoff=max(liquid-deficit,0)`. At the default 5 m table, S_y 0.30, the deficit is 1500 mm, so VSA runoff never fires except in a thin riparian strip — yet the docstring sells VSA as 'the dominant runoff mechanism' (groundwater M2). The arithmetic means Q/P is actually constraining the interflow K_aniso, not VSA. The formula also assumes the whole unsaturated column is instantaneously fillable (same teleport as #131) and double-counts the root-zone space already handled at `:235`.

**Do:** compute the fillable deficit from the actual unsaturated store (once #... storage exists), remove the double-count, and reconcile which mechanism truly produces Q/P.

</details>

body:
> **Superseded 2026-10-18** by UZF in #282 under the PI's decision to make MODFLOW 6 the groundwater core (plan `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-modflow-groundwater-core/plan.md`, PR #273; epic #274). Held from the agent queue by the `superseded` label. Closing is the PI's call after reviewing the replacement.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Becomes the deep unsaturated store between the root zone and the water table. The bookkeeping fix moved to #232.

**Audit verdict:** split

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #172` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Split into two issues. (a) 'Whole-system water ledger + capillary/recession conservation repair' (new, P0/P1, agent-ready): define the control volume (root S + vadose U + S_y*h above datum), debit capillary rise from groundwater, and account for signed recession. Test: the residual over all branches (legacy, HAND, slope on/off, wet/dry limits, multi-step) is below 1e-6 mm per step in float64, and dt=1 d vs 0.25 d agree. (b) Keep #172 as 'explicit unsaturated store U with moving-boundary S_y,eff', blocked by (a). Acceptance: the conservation suite passes, and a zero-store limit reproduces the current behaviour. Add BLOCKED_BY 172:[ledger].

### Problems found

- It bundles two deliverables: a conservation repair that is small and testable, and a new physics store that is a design task. GAIA closes the whole issue with 'Closes #N' (gaia-automation.md:82,119), so a capillary-debit PR would close #172 with the store unbuilt. The operational plan (line 44) warns about exactly this.
- There is no acceptance criterion in the body at all.
- The vadose store IS the #131 lag mechanism. Unless the two are coordinated they will become two competing implementations.
- In the queue it is the last of batch 7, after #175, #174 and #173, which all depend on it. Batches run in descending issue-number order (queue_sim batch 7: [175,174,173,172]).

### Physics assessment

Correct and confirmed. cap_eff is added to S (:218-219) and h is never debited (:266). The legacy recession clips signed baseflow (:268, :278), leaving a residual of 0.00404 mm even after a one-line debit (followup line 40). The existing test only checks the root store (test_water_budget.py:26-33), so it cannot catch this. An explicit unsaturated store between the root base and the table is the right fix, but it needs a moving-boundary rule: as the table rises into the vadose layer, that layer's water becomes saturated storage. The physically consistent form is an effective specific yield S_y,eff = theta_sat - theta_u(table-top), which shrinks for shallow tables because of the capillary fringe (Duke 1972). That also resolves part of #137's 'S_y does three jobs'.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #232, #265.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Recharge leaves the root-zone store S (`water_budget.py:247-250`) and independently lifts head via S_y (`:266`); capillary rise pulls from a shallow table into S (`:217-219`) but never debits head. The metres of unsaturated material between them are MASSLESS — mass is 'conserved by construction' only because each reservoir is internally closed, but the coupling flux is not conserved across the gap (groundwater M1). In an integrated model that column IS the storage that sets both recession shape and event lag; its absence is why the vadose-lag (#131) and specific-yield (#137) issues bite.

**Do:** add an explicit unsaturated store between the root base and the water table that conserves the coupling flux and carries recession/lag.

</details>

body:
> **Superseded 2026-10-18** by #274 under the PI's decision to make MODFLOW 6 the groundwater core (plan `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-modflow-groundwater-core/plan.md`, PR #273; epic #274). Held from the agent queue by the `superseded` label. Closing is the PI's call after reviewing the replacement.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Epic for the water-conserving soil column. Children now include the new ledger, valley, snow, holdout and design-record issues; the PI decided to keep the light model and make it modular.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

In BLOCKED_BY[187], replace 171 with the leaf evidence: the conservation harness (new) and #172. Add #89, the #100 residual, #225, #227 and the new gap issues to the sub-issue list, and mark #87 as superseded by #131. Add an explicit decision checkbox (needs-human-decision): 'GWL product scope: storm-scale (1-15 d) head forecast vs antecedent/seasonal state', with the lab lead as owner. State the order: ledger harness, then #172, then #131, then #173/#174/#175 (sequential), then #176, then #137 re-close.

### Problems found

- The grouper skips it as an epic (gaia_group_issues.py:178), which is fine. But it is listed as a hard blocker of #187 (gaia_group_issues.py:87). Epics are closed by humans, so this can hold the P0 contract indefinitely (system audit line 95; dependency review line 24).
- The sub-issue list omits #89 (timestep, also a #187 blocker), #87 (duplicate of #131), the #100 phase residual, the Rainier #225 (canopy interception) and #227 (glacier melt), which edit the same loop, and the missing continuous-well and conservation-harness work.
- The 'or narrow the GWL claim' branch is an unresolved scope decision that should carry needs-human-decision. The grouper ignores that label anyway (it only checks epic and BLOCKED_BY, gaia_group_issues.py:175-186).

### Physics assessment

The diagnosis is correct and confirmed on main. The unsaturated zone has no storage (water_budget.py:247-266). Capillary rise creates water (probe: 33.8 mm/yr at a 0.8 m table). S_y does three jobs (:230, :266, :278). The closure is a calibration fit, not validation (calibrate_fluxes.py:81-99). The alternative it offers, narrowing the GWL claim to antecedent/seasonal state, is a scope decision for the PI, not for an agent.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

The lumped bucket + linear-reservoir water table (`src/models/water_budget.py`) is a credible, self-aware regional skeleton, but judged against Richards/integrated-flow it **deletes the unsaturated zone**, and that single omission drives the review's three criticals: recharge teleports to the table (no transit/storage), specific yield is forced to ~0.30 (near porosity) to compensate, and the 'closure against gauges AND wells' is an exactly-determined 3-knob fit reported as validation. Make the vadose physics and the calibration defensible, or narrow the GWL claim to antecedent/seasonal state.

## Sub-issues
- [ ] #131 Vadose transit lag (recharge must not teleport) — the C1 fix
- [ ] #137 Defensible specific yield + held-out validation — the C2/C3 fix
- [ ] #172 Consistent storage account: close the massless vadose gap between the two reservoirs
- [ ] #173 Saturation-excess runoff: no one-step fill to the water table; stop double-counting root-zone space
- [ ] #174 Interflow: give it a store and a defensible coefficient
- [ ] #175 Baseflow sink: break the near-circular BFI anchor; nonlinear recession
- [ ] #176 Route hysteresis into the soil-water DYNAMICS, not only the dv/v observable
- [ ] #177 Minor fixes (groundwater / vadose review)


</details>

body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Small fixes folded into #164; the area-weight item stays.

**Audit verdict:** split

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #170` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Fold m1/m2 into the #164(a) full-R/Cholesky task. Acceptance: Cholesky with symmetrization; a non-PD M raises or jitters with a logged warning; the clip only triggers on a flagged path. Keep m4 as a small agent-ready item: fractional-area weights against a supplied product grid transform, tested for invariance to the grid origin. Close m3 with a docstring note. Move m5 to #189's per-sensor σ task.

### Problems found

- m1/m2 touch the same functions as #164's full-R support, so they should ship together.
- m3 is stale.
- m5 is really #165/#189 (physical σ per sensor).

### Physics assessment

m1 and m2 are valid. np.linalg.solve (LU) on M = GBGᵀ+R at observability.py:1116, 1258 and 1260 should be a symmetrized Cholesky with detect-and-jitter. The clip(reduction, 0, var_prior) at :1118 and :1261 hides non-PD M and can drive information_gain to its clip. m3 is stale: no code sums per-cell nats to a domain total (make_observability_figure.py:191-207 only maps or concatenates for the colour scale), so the item becomes a docstring warning at most. m4 is valid: floor((x-x.min())/pixel_km) at :1024-1025 is anchored to the grid origin rather than the product's real pixel grid (EASE-2 for SMAP), and assigns cells wholly to one pixel. m5 is valid: ObsStream.noise is 'in units of prior variance' (:874), which is ill-defined until G carries the gain.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

From the applied-math review:
- [ ] Use SPD Cholesky (`cho_factor` with jitter), not LU, for `M=GBG^T+R`; symmetrise `M=(M+M^T)/2` — it also DETECTS the non-PD conditions the clamp hides (m1).
- [ ] The posterior-variance clamp `clip(reduction,0,var_prior)` masks conditioning: hitting it means M was numerically non-PD; prefer detect-and-jitter over silent `var_post=0 -> res=1 -> info_gain=+inf` (m2).
- [ ] Summing per-cell information gain over cells overcounts — neighbours are correlated by the off-diagonal C; a domain-total 'nats' is an upper bound, not a total (`information_gain:321-330`) (m3).
- [ ] Satellite pixel binning `floor((x-x.min())/pixel_km)` assigns a boundary-straddling cell wholly to one pixel and shifts with grid origin (`satellite_footprints:215`) — partial-overlap weighting (m4).
- [ ] 'noise in units of prior variance' (`:121`) is ill-defined until the sensitivity gain is in G (see the gain issue) (m5).

</details>

title: Minor fixes (DA review)

body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Synthetic study of whether damage can be told apart from hydrology.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Rewrite as an agent-ready synthetic conditioning study. Acceptance: report the posterior correlation matrix, VIF and posterior/prior σ ratio for each process amplitude against record length (1-10 yr), event-time knowledge (known / ±30 d / unknown) and noise level, using the repo's kernels and Cd; define 'identifiable' as |post-corr| < 0.8 and σ_post/σ_prior < 0.5, and add a refusal guard to the docs. Add #169 to BLOCKED_BY for #162/#123.

### Problems found

- The 'Do' is prose; there is no test or threshold.
- Needs the event catalog #124 for any real-data claim; a synthetic study does not.
- It should block #162/#123, but that is not encoded.

### Physics assessment

Correct, and stronger than stated. My probe (wf/da/ident.py) uses daily sampling with a known event time and basis {1, log(1+Δt/1 d), 1-exp(-Δt/2 yr), annual sin/cos}. The posterior correlation between the healing and slow-exponential amplitudes has |ρ| from 0.88 to 0.97, and VIF from 6 to 27, for every record length from 1 to 10 yr. Longer records do not decorrelate them, because both curves are concave and monotone after the event. With an unknown or uncatalogued event time it is worse. Illien et al. 2022 worked because the event time was exogenous. So a partition is prior-dominated unless the relaxation-kernel priors are informative and independently justified (lab or other sites).

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`03c:100-111`: at a cell/time `dv/v = elastic(theta,h) + D + Phi`, one scalar and >=3 unknowns. Separation needs the temporal basis columns (seasonal harmonic, log-t healing, multi-year exponential) known, non-collinear over the record, and anchored by known event times/locations. Over a short window log-t, a slow exponential and a seasonal term are strongly COLLINEAR -> near-singular augmented normal equations -> the 'partition' is prior-dominated and CANNOT discover an uncatalogued disturbance (M7). Illien 2022 worked because the earthquake time was exogenously known.

**Do:** state the identifiability precondition explicitly (correct relaxation-kernel priors + a known event catalog #124); quantify the conditioning over the actual record length before claiming a partition.

</details>

body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Specified coda-footprint kernels with their bias in the error budget.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Rewrite with three acceptance items. (1) Padded-domain kernel with f_out reported per pair and its variance added to R; a test shows a pair straddling the boundary gives an unbiased innovation on a synthetic. (2) A kernel for each lapse window actually used, consistent with DEFAULT_CODA_WINDOWS. (3) A kernel ensemble over D, l* and the partition coefficient α within stated ranges, with the spread propagated into R. Use radiative-transfer kernels when t_lapse < ~3 l*/v, or state the regime of validity. Coordinate depth kernels with #198.

### Problems found

- 'Use a 3-D kernel' is not specified enough to implement, and it is not the right physics target for early coda.
- It overlaps #198's depth-kernel operator.
- No acceptance.

### Physics assessment

(i) The edge bias is real and still present: pair_kernel renormalises the in-grid part to 1 (dvv_sensitivity.py:134-137) and only documents it in the docstring. The fix is to compute the kernel on a padded domain, keep the out-of-domain mass f_out, and add roughly f_out²·σ_m² to R. Do not renormalise. (ii) The separability claim is overstated. For surface-wave-dominated coda, a lateral 2-D kernel times a Rayleigh depth sensitivity is the standard approximation (Obermann et al. 2013/2016). It fails at later lapse times, when the coda partitions toward body waves. The physically right target is Obermann's combined kernel α(t)K_2D·K_z + (1-α(t))K_3D, not a full 3-D kernel by itself. (iii) The constants are inconsistent. D=8 km²/s and v=1.5 km/s give a transport mean free path l* = 2D/v ≈ 10.7 km and a mean free time of about 7 s. At t_lapse = 10 s (≈1.4 mean free times) the diffusion approximation is not valid; radiative-transfer kernels (Paasschens 1997) are needed. Also, dvv.py:232 sweeps coda windows from 5 to 50 s, but the operator uses a single 10 s kernel. The diffusion radius √(4Dt) runs from 18 km at 10 s to 40 km at 50 s, so the operator does not match the datum. rainier3d cannot provide near-surface Vs(z) here, because it flags its top 300 m as unresolved (rainier leverage review row 6).

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

The Pacheco-Snieder kernels are reused as the assimilation operator G (`04-assimilation.qmd:137`), but carry biases not in R (M6): (i) a pair extending past the domain has its in-grid part renormalised to sum 1 (`dvv_sensitivity.py:124-128`), so EDGE rows are the wrong operator and bias the innovation; (ii) a 2-D map-view diffusion Green's function times a separate depth kernel assumes K(x,z)=K_xy K_z, which Pacheco-Snieder does not support — coda sensitivity is an inseparable 3-D volume kernel; (iii) a single hard-coded D and lapse time fix width to order-of-magnitude.

**Do:** propagate kernel/medium uncertainty into R, and either use a 3-D (or 2.5-D) kernel or state the separability assumption as an operator caveat (not just a map caveat).

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** One issue for using the actual age of each datum (#167 merged here).

**Audit verdict:** merge

### Specification

Merge #166 and #167 into 'Temporal observability through lagged_observation with actual or age-distributed datum age'. Acceptance: (1) effective_observability is replaced or deprecated by a function that builds lagged G/R rows and calls variance_reduction_ratio; a test confirms one perfect datum at lag Δt reproduces 1-ρ²; (2) the figure caption no longer calls the product a resolution; (3) design mode uses the expected ρ² over the age distribution (see #167).

### Problems found

- It shares the cause and fix with #167 (dt should be the datum age, not the revisit interval), so doing them separately duplicates the work.
- Acceptance is 'label or derive' with no test.

### Physics assessment

Correct. effective_observability (observability.py:912-920) multiplies the variance-reduction ratio by ρ(revisit)². That product is not a diagonal of any posterior covariance, because a temporal discount acts on precision, nonlinearly through M⁻¹. The rigorous route already exists: build the rows with lagged_observation(g, age, τ, σ_m², σ_ε²) and pass them to variance_reduction_ratio. The function has no code callers (an earlier GAIA run on issue-166, 2026-08-18, confirms this), but make_spacetime_figure.py:88 plots the spatial×temporal product.

That product is not the diagonal of any posterior covariance — a temporal weight scales PRECISION, nonlinearly through M^-1, not resolution (M4). Presented beside the rigorous BLUE diagonals it reads as if it were C_a/C.

title: effective_observability is not a covariance diagonal — label or derive it

body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Allow correlated observation errors (full error matrix) in every solver; absorbs #170 m1/m2.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Split into two. (a) Agent-ready now: accept a full or block R (n_obs×n_obs) in all four observation-space functions, with SPD Cholesky (absorbs #170 m1/m2). Test: N pairs with perfectly correlated error give the same posterior variance as one pair, to 1e-10, while the diagonal path gives a variance 1/N as large. (b) Build the cross-pair/band R block from a joint processing ensemble plus a shared-station term. Test on a synthetic with a known shared-receiver error: posterior coverage at nominal 90% falls within ±5% over 500 replicates, while the diagonal-R run under-covers. Note that the temporal Cd belongs to the cycling-filter error model (see gaps).

### Problems found

- The solver functions only accept a vector of noise variances. variance_reduction_ratio, averaging_kernel, degrees_of_freedom_for_signal and blue_update hard-code np.diag(nv), so even a correct R could not be passed in. That is infrastructure work shared with #170 m1/m2.
- The cross-pair covariance has no estimation method. Options: apply the same processing-ensemble member to all pairs jointly, so the methodological covariance spans pairs; add a shared-station term; check against an empirical residual covariance.
- Cited line numbers are stale (observability.py:265,306-311,397,441 are now ~1115/1256; make_twin_gif.py call sites are now :225-244).
- The 'Blocks #188/#192' claim should be limited to dv/v-informed scopes; it does not block a well/probe pilot (follow-up review).

### Physics assessment

The core claim is right. Pairs that share a receiver, or that share a reference stack and processing choices, have correlated errors, and diagonal R (observability.py:1115, 1256) overcounts information where dv/v is densest. The 'sharpened finding' is partly wrong, though. The Cd in dvv.py:276-280 is a per-pair, per-band TIME×TIME covariance: 3-day temporal correlation plus a common mode plus methodological spread, with n_epoch×n_epoch shape. It is not the cross-pair, cross-band covariance at one epoch that a snapshot BLUE needs. That snapshot block is not built anywhere. Cd's temporal correlation matters for a different reason: in cycling DA (#188), errors correlated over 3 days break the EnKF white-noise assumption.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`observability.py:265,306-311` uses `np.diag(nv)` with a scalar `noise=0.12`, yet the doc itself calls dv/v error a 'processing-ensemble covariance (codameter)' (`04-assimilation.qmd:22`). Pairs sharing a receiver and lapse-windows of the same pair have strongly correlated error; a diagonal R treats them as independent replicates and double-counts information — posterior variance too small exactly where dv/v is densest (M1).

**Do:** use the dense/block ensemble covariance from codameter for the dv/v R; the scalar-per-stream noise cannot express it.

---

**Sharpened finding (2026-07-21 review, [`docs/reviews/sensor-uncertainty-covariance-review.md`](../docs/reviews/sensor-uncertainty-covariance-review.md)):** this is not merely "unmodeled" — the dense covariance is already *built* and then discarded before every current use. `dvv.py:222-281` computes a genuine ensemble-derived `Cd = temporal_error_covariance(corr_length_days=3.0) + methodological_covariance()`, combining a Weaver/Clarke coherence bound with a swept processing ensemble via the law of total variance. But `blue_update`/`resolution` both build `R` as `np.diag(nv)` (`observability.py:397,441`), and all five current call sites (`notebooks/make_twin_gif.py:197,213`; `notebooks/make_checkerboard_test.py:138`; `tests/test_observability.py:273,282`) pass a scalar or per-observation diagonal `noise_var` — none passes `Cd`. dv/v's own structured covariance never reaches the estimator.

**Blocks:** any trustworthy posterior variance involving dv/v in #192 (B/Q/R diagnosis) and #188 (cycling nowcast) — fix this before trusting either for dv/v-informed cells.


</details>
