body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Narrowed to recording the barrier approximation in metadata; P2; hold remains until the PI releases it.

**Audit verdict:** split

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #163` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Retitle to 'Record barrier-mask approximation status in prior/analysis metadata' and drop to P2. Acceptance: write_artifact() and any analysis output record barrier_source (none/hydrographic/hydrogeologic_domain), mask_type (hard_0_1/soft) and status='approximation', and a test asserts the fields. That piece is agent-ready once a human releases the hold. Move the terrain anisotropy, soft barriers and domain labels into a new research issue gated on an estimability study (see gaps). Remove the needs-human-decision label only after a person records the release.

### Problems found

- Labelled needs-human-decision, yet gaia_group_issues.py has no needs-human check, so it is dispatched again in batch 1. The park cause in the gaia-park payload is 'unrecognised verdict None', a reviewer-infrastructure failure, not a scientific block (audit A5).
- Title and P0 are stale: scalability is done (#154/#216). The remaining item is a small metadata task.
- The open-ended 'soft connectivity weight' and 'hydrogeologic-domain labels' items have no acceptance criteria. Agents read them as permission for an anisotropy SPDE build.

### Physics assessment

The revised body is physically right. It puts the prior on the baseline residual δh, not absolute DTW. It keeps ν separate for groundwater and soil moisture. It treats region_id as a localization/barrier approximation rather than a groundwater divide (a surface divide is not necessarily a groundwater divide, per Haitjema & Mitchell-Bruker 2005). And it separates the choice of statistical model from the scalable backend. Three of the four boxes have landed (issue comment 2026-08-20). The fourth box, barrier-approximation status in analysis metadata, is not done: neither prior_calibration.py nor calibrate_spatial_prior.py mentions barriers. The parked August plan grew into a terrain-anisotropy GMRF research program. That program is the wrong next step, because estimability at ~121-863 wells is unproven and a terrain-following H(x) forfeits the exact FFT backend.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Two faults were originally identified in one object (`GaussianPrior`): (i) the dense `(n,n)` `C` is
infeasible at 90 m; (ii) a single isotropic length leaks constraint across drainage divides, and the
$C^\infty$ squared-exponential imposes implausibly smooth fields.

The Matérn switch and the `region_id` masking have **landed**. What remains needs restating, because
the original framing fused two decisions that must stay separate.

**Objective (revised):** a **residual/anomaly** Matérn prior with **state-specific smoothness**,
**configurable barriers**, and a numerical representation that **does not dictate ν**.

Three corrections to the original text:

1. **The prior is on the residual, not the field.** Absolute DTW is $D = z_s - h_{wt}$ and carries the
   whole deterministic landscape; it is not a stationary Gaussian Matérn field over Puget Sound. The
   prior belongs on $\delta h$ about the baseline (the standard drift-plus-residual construction —
   Varouchakis et al. 2019, 2022).
2. **Groundwater and soil moisture must not share ν.** One `GaussianPrior` default governed both.
   ν=3/2 is a *working hypothesis* for the water-table-head anomaly (the log-K→head filtering argument
   is directional only, and does not select 3/2 over 1 or 2) and is *unsupported* for soil moisture,
   which the literature describes as rougher and strongly state/scale/support/depth/season dependent
   (Vereecken et al. 2014). Minasny & McBratney (2005)'s low smoothness is for measured **soil
   properties**, not monthly soil moisture.
3. **"Simultaneously the scalable representation and the physically right correlation structure" is
   the coupling to reject.** The classical *local* GMRF/SPDE construction exists only for integer α,
   hence integer ν, so adopting it as the scalability fix silently changes the statistical model —
   and the prototype benchmarked in `docs/reviews/prior-operator-benchmark.md` does exactly that
   (ν=1.5→1). Rational SPDE methods reach general smoothness (Bolin & Kirchner 2020), so this is a
   *choice*, not a constraint. The statistical model is selected on physical/statistical grounds;
   the backend then serves it. Scalability is #154.

**Also:** `region_id` is a **hydrographic localization / barrier approximation**, not an exact
physical covariance boundary — a surface drainage divide is not necessarily a groundwater divide
(Haitjema & Mitchell-Bruker 2005). Prefer hydrogeologic-domain labels
(`src/features/hydrogeologic_domains.py`); consider a soft connectivity weight instead of a 0/1 mask.
`barrier_id` now exists as an alias; a full rename is proposed, not done.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Groundwater and soil moisture carry independently configurable ν (asserted by test). *(landed)*
- [ ] The prior is documented as being on the baseline residual. *(landed)*
- [ ] Any sparse/SPDE representation adopted for scalability **reports whether it changes ν**, and
      any benchmark against it treats a changed ν as a confound, not a rounding.
- [ ] The barrier mask's approximate status is recorded in analysis metadata.

Context: `docs/reviews/hydrology-geostatistics-prior-audit-2026-08.md` §3, §7.

---

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Merged in spirit with #123 (attribution); on hold, P2.

**Audit verdict:** hold-human

### Specification

Merge with #123 into one issue in v0.6, dropped to P2. Add BLOCKED_BY [169, 188, 198, 124] and label needs-human-decision for the architecture choice. Split off one agent-ready docs task now: a status box in 03c/04-assimilation.qmd saying attribution is not implemented and the current estimator is a static BLUE. Acceptance once released: on a low-dimensional synthetic with known truth, the augmented smoother recovers D and Φ amplitudes within their posterior intervals. It must report the posterior correlation matrix and refuse to report a partition when |corr| > 0.8.

### Problems found

- It duplicates #123 ('augment the BLUE to separate hydrology / damage / disturbance').
- It is P0 and dispatched in batch 1 with no BLOCKED_BY entry, although it needs #169, #187, #188, #198 and the event catalog #124.
- The architecture (Kalman/RTS vs RBPF) is unresolved across #162, #190 and the roadmap. Deciding that needs a person, not an agent.
- No testable acceptance. 'Until then, state in the docs that attribution is unbuilt' is the only immediately actionable item.

### Physics assessment

The diagnosis is correct. Separating hydrology, damage D and disturbance Φ by temporal signature needs an estimator that sees time; blue_update (observability.py:1217-1263) is a single snapshot. But prescribing a Kalman/RTS smoother over [hydrology, D, Φ] is premature. (1) Identifiability (#169) is unproven, and my probe says it is badly conditioned even with known event times: |post-corr| ≥ 0.88 between log-t healing and a slow exponential for 1-10 yr records. (2) The roadmap specifies an RBPF instead, and the September science review (science-review.md:39-45) shows that the RBPF's 'exact conditional linear likelihood' claim is false. That is a real architecture conflict (roadmap-review R5). (3) #123 is the same task in v0.6.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #188, #169.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`observability.py:276-318` solves one snapshot with no state-transition operator, no temporal propagation, and no augmentation of D (damage) or Phi (disturbance). The attribution plan (`03c:100-111`, #123) separates hydrology/damage/fire by their temporal SIGNATURES — but a temporal discriminant can only act inside an estimator that sees the time axis (a Kalman/RTS smoother over the augmented state with per-process transition kernels). As coded the object is a static BLUE; the method described is a space-time smoother (C2).

**Do:** build the augmented-state Kalman/RTS smoother (state = [hydrology, D, Phi] with per-process transition/relaxation kernels) that #123 requires; until then, state in the docs that attribution is unbuilt.

</details>

The 'dense stationary-isotropic squared-exponential' sentence is stale: the prior is Matérn with per-state ν (observability.py:184-244, 653-700), and #160's own comment from 2026-08-20 says so. body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Move the assimilation closure into src and test it.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Move the inner `assimilate` into a src function.

Acceptance:
1. A mocked-response parser test for the NWIS or PRISM daily fetcher, covering units and missing-value handling.
2. An end-to-end synthetic-grid test asserting that the well-cell increment is preserved after upsampling (tolerance stated).
3. A test documenting the edge-band behaviour.

Add #153 to BLOCKED_BY (it needs the fixtures).

### Problems found

- `assimilate` is a closure inside notebooks/make_twin_gif.py:204, so it cannot be tested until it is moved into src.
- Has no acceptance criterion.
- `blue_update` already has a synthetic test (tests/test_observability.py:268); what is missing is the end-to-end grid path and fetcher parsers (no tests/test_fetch_*).

### Physics assessment

The 'upsample mass invariant' is the wrong invariant. `upsample` in make_twin_gif.py:198-202 linearly interpolates a correction and sets edges to zero (`nan_to_num`), and linear interpolation does not conserve mass. Two checks are meaningful: (i) at well cells the upsampled fine analysis reproduces the coarse analysis increment to within interpolation error; (ii) the zero-correction edge band is quantified, since cells outside the coarse hull get no update even next to a well, which may itself be a defect.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

**Do:** add fixture-backed tests for one fetcher parser and for the `assimilate()` inner function on a tiny synthetic grid; assert the upsample mass/consistency invariant.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** One seeded random-number stream helper.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Specify `src.utils.rng.stream(seed, *keys)` built on `SeedSequence` `spawn_key`.

Acceptance: `assimilate(k)` gives identical outputs for any shared frame k under CADENCE=1 and CADENCE=3, and the same helper supports a member key for #191.

### Problems found

- Mostly done already: src uses seeded generators (attribution.py:42, dvv.py:406/448, domain_gates.py:60, pilot_temporal.py:376), and only old/notebooks/make_digital_twin.py lacks a seed.
- The real remaining defect is make_twin_gif.py:196-241: one RNG consumed inside `assimilate(k)` in frame order.
- No acceptance criterion.

### Physics assessment

The prescribed fix does not achieve its own goal. Spawning `len(idx)` children assigns streams by position, so changing CADENCE changes `len(idx)` and frame k gets a different child stream. Streams must be keyed by absolute identity, for example `SeedSequence(seed, spawn_key=(frame_index_or_time, member))`. That keying is also what #191 needs for member streams.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Only 2 of ~15 notebook scripts seed (M2). `make_twin_gif.py` seeds but consumes `rng.standard_normal` inside `assimilate(k)` in frame order, so the 'reproducible' figure depends on CADENCE/loop order.

**Do:** a `src`-level `get_rng(seed)`, seed every script that draws randomness, and derive per-frame streams via `rng.spawn(len(idx))` so realisations are independent of loop structure.

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Warn or fail when the slope-based Vs30 proxy is used on flat soft ground.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Do: (1) write the actually-used source to raster tags/attrs and the log line; (2) fail, or require an explicit flag, when Wald-Allen would be used inside liquefiable units (needs the geology mask from #84 or the hydrogeologic domains); (3) add the 1e-4 E edge and use bin geometric centres, after verifying against Wald & Allen 2007 Table 1 (absorb #149 m1); (4) document the 30-arcsec calibration. Acceptance: tests for the provenance tag on fallback, the presence of the E bin, and the flat-cell value not equal to 180.

### Problems found

- Stale line refs (:367-373 is now :371-399)
- Misses the lower-edge bias, the missing E bin, resolution dependence and the provenance mislabel

### Physics assessment

Correct and confirmed: a gradient below 2.2e-3 (about 0.126 deg) maps to a single bin of 180 m/s (fetch_vs30.py:44-45, 51-63), so there is no discrimination within the liquefiable population. More defects than the issue lists: (a) values are bin lower edges (180/240/300/... per range), a systematic low bias of about 10-15% per bin; (b) the Wald & Allen 2007 active table's E-class edge at gradient 1e-4 (Vs30 < 180) is missing, so true E sites cannot be identified (edges from memory; verify against the paper's Table 1); (c) the proxy was calibrated on 30-arcsec slopes and is applied to 90 m 3DEP slope, which is steeper, so upland Vs30 is biased stiff; (d) main() logs 'Wrote Vs30 (svm)' using args.source even when get_vs30 fell back to Wald-Allen (fetch_vs30.py:449-451), a provenance mislabel of the kind ROADMAP.md:180-181 warns about. The fallback is no longer silent (warning at :365), but it is not recorded in the output.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`fetch_vs30.py:44-63`: active-tectonic bins assign 180 m/s to everything below a 2.2e-3 gradient. Liquefiable terrain (Holocene alluvium, fill, tideflats) is flat, so the proxy saturates in one bin — zero discrimination within the liquefiable population; `get_vs30` silently falls back to it (`:367-373`) (C3).

**Do:** require SVM (or a better low-relief model) for liquefiable units; make the flat-ground fallback a loud warning; document Wald-Allen's poor performance on young low-relief deposits.

</details>

body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Code and docs firewall: dv/v damage state is not a liquefaction-triggering input.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Extend Do: edit the soil_mechanics.py docstring/contract to say dv/v is not a pore-pressure or triggering input; add a guard so any liquefaction consumer rejects time-varying Vs30 (Vs30 is a static site covariate). State explicitly that dv/v may constrain the water table via the hydromechanical operator (#198). Acceptance: docs and code comments updated; a unit test that the liquefaction entry point raises on a time-varying vs30.

### Problems found

- Docs-only scope misses the code contract in soil_mechanics.py and Vs30(t) in forecast.py
- No acceptance criteria
- Could over-firewall the legitimate dv/v -> water-table assimilation path

### Physics assessment

Correct. Coseismic dv/v drop is nonlinear damage with log-time healing (03c:65-83). Triggering is excess pore pressure reaching r_u = 1 within seconds, a different mechanism, depth and timescale. The category error also sits in code: soil_mechanics.py:11-14 calls dv/v 'a time-varying proxy for effective stress / pore pressure' and :61-62 asks for a liquefaction susceptibility term from it. forecast.py:181-183 produces Vs30(t) from dv/v, which as a GLM input is both conceptually wrong and numerically negligible (0.2% Vs30 gives dX of about 0.004). The issue must also preserve the legitimate path: seasonal hydrologic dv/v constraining the water table (03b:95-102), which then feeds DTW. The firewall applies to the damage state and to Vs30(t) entering the hazard model, not to the use of dv/v in hydrology.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`03c-memory-disturbance.qmd:65-83` and #121 propose a velocity-deficit D healing log-linearly. The coseismic dv/v drop is nonlinear near-surface DAMAGE recovering over days-years; triggering is excess-pore-pressure to r_u->1 in SECONDS — different physics/depths/timescales; velocity change is NOT pore-pressure generation (C5). Illien 2022 (cited) had to SEPARATE damage from drainage.

**Do:** docs state the dv/v/healing state is a post-event MONITORING/attribution variable, NOT a pore-pressure/triggering quantity; keep it as a research track (Milestone 4 #123), firewalled from triggering.

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Vs30 uncertainty map per cell.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Do: write vs30_sigma_ln_90m.tif with a source-specific sigma: Wald-Allen a documented constant from the literature (cite the value and table); SVM from per-province residuals (cite, or mark pending #81). Write a per-cell source-provenance band. Assign Wald-Allen the bin geometric mid-value, not the lower edge, so flat cells do not sit exactly on 180. Acceptance: a test that P(class) for flat Wald-Allen cells is not pinned at 0.5; the sigma raster co-registers with vs30_90m.tif; documented sigma values with citations.

### Problems found

- Cited lines are stale (Wald-Allen is now fetch_vs30.py:51-63)
- No acceptance criteria
- SVM sigma may need the #81 profiles

### Physics assessment

Still accurate: nehrp_class_probabilities requires vs30_std (fetch_vs30.py:73-107) and no producer of a sigma raster exists (only tests/test_vs30.py calls it). sigma_lnVs30 of about 0.3-0.5 for slope proxies is in the right range. There is a further problem the issue misses. Wald-Allen assigns exactly 180 m/s to all flat cells, which sits on the E/D boundary, so every flat cell gets P(E) = 0.50 regardless of sigma (probe: slope 0.001-0.12 deg gives P = [0.50, 0.46, 0.04, 0, 0]). That is decorative in the same sense the issue complains about. For the GLM, sigma should be propagated in ln Vs30 directly, not via P(class). For the SVM, sigma should come from the province profile residuals in Grant, Wirth & Stone 2025, which need #81's data if not published.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`fetch_vs30.py:73-107` differences a CDF but REQUIRES `vs30_std`, and nothing produces a spatial sigma — Wald-Allen is a deterministic step (`:57-63`), SVM returns a mean with no sigma (M2). So sigma is a guessed constant and P(class) is decorative.

**Do:** carry a real per-cell sigma — Wald-Allen dispersion (sigma_lnVs30 ~ 0.3-0.5) and SVM province scatter — as a field alongside the mean.

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Split: lowland accuracy check; coastal/confined method; pass the water-table uncertainty to liquefaction.

**Audit verdict:** split

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #142` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Split into: (142a) restrict the truth set to measurement_target == water_table inside young alluvium/fill, report exclusion counts and lowland-only block-CV RMSE/bias plus PIT coverage of the P10 tail (agent-ready on existing code). (142b) Coastal/tidal/confined head prior to replace TOPMODEL there, needing a human hydrogeologist decision (hold). (142c) Set the accuracy target from the consumer: about 1.5-2 m for the #141 screen, sub-metre only for #146, and reconcile domain_gates.py coastal 1.0/2.0. Add BLOCKED_BY 142:[137].

### Problems found

- Bundles four deliverables: truth-set restriction, lowland-specific scoring, a coastal/confined non-TOPMODEL prior, and DTW pdf propagation
- Contradictory accuracy target (title vs body), noted in roadmap-review:89
- Depends on #137 (specific yield/held-out validation) and a DTW time series, neither encoded
- P10 over a short pilot series is not a return-period quantity (also #149 m2)

### Physics assessment

The truth-set fix in the Aug 20 comment (measurement_target == water_table, tail-coverage scoring) is correct, and the classifier now exists (src/features/well_hydrostratigraphy.py:53,129). The accuracy target is not derived from the consuming model. For the GLM screen, 1 m of DTW error is about 0.008 in P under Zhu 2017, so sub-metre accuracy is not needed for #141. Sub-metre accuracy matters only for depth-resolved LPI (#146), where the saturated thickness above 20 m with weight w(z) = 10 - 0.5z dominates. The title says sub-1.5 m, the body sub-metre, and domain_gates.py:31,33 sets the valley-fill threshold at 1.5 m and coastal at 2.0 m. Replacing TOPMODEL (water_budget.py:287) in tidal/confined fill is physically right: tidal fill heads follow sea level plus tidal damping, not TWI. It is, however, a model-development project, not an issue.

### Order and dependencies
Blocked by: #286, #9.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

**Amended 2026-11-09 by the soil-state review ladder (#296; record `docs/reviews/2026-11-07-fable-soil-state-review/`).** Forecast wording removed until the gate passes.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Build only after the model is pinned and the value-of-information gate (#270) shows the water table matters.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Pin 'Zhu et al. 2017 Model 2 with Rashidian & Baise 2020 caps; coefficients transcribed with a table citation and unit test against the paper's worked values'. Inputs: ln Vs30 with sigma from #144, ShakeMap PGV with sigma_lnPGV from #143, and DTW from a product that does NOT use Vs30 as a predictor (or quantify the collinearity). Monte Carlo over all three. Acceptance: (a) a probability map plus LSE with sigma; (b) a variance decomposition of P into Vs30, PGV and DTW shares, with the pre-registered statement that if the DTW share is under 10% the 'dynamic' claim is dropped from the docs; (c) a hit-rate/ROC against the observed 2001 Nisqually liquefaction sites using the 2001 ShakeMap, stating whether Nisqually is in Zhu's training set; (d) agreement with WA DNR/Palmer reported as a contingency table, labelled a sanity check. Add BLOCKED_BY 141:[143,144].

### Problems found

- The model and coefficients are not pinned
- The acceptance criteria are trivially satisfiable and contain no event validation
- The required time-varying DTW series does not exist (landlab_export.py:333-335)
- Blockers #143 (PGV) and #144 (Vs30 sigma) are not in BLOCKED_BY; the queue runs #141 in batch 25, right after them in batch 24, likely before they merge
- The probability semantics (Zhu probability vs areal extent LSE; PGV < 3 cm/s and Vs30 > 620 m/s cutoffs) are unstated

### Physics assessment

A published logistic screen is the right MVP, but four physics problems need fixing first. (1) The acceptance test 'dynamic DTW changes the map vs static' passes trivially for any nonzero change; under Zhu 2017 the change is at most about 0.03 in P for a 4 m swing, well inside the Vs30-driven sigma_P of about 0.3. (2) ShakeMap PGV already contains a site term computed with the USGS Vs30, and Zhu 2017 was fitted that way. Pairing ShakeMap PGV with the twin's SVM Vs30 applies two inconsistent site models; either use ShakeMap's own Vs30 grid in the GLM or regenerate the ground motion with the SVM Vs30. (3) The DTW product the twin would supply is regressed on Vs30 itself (baseline_regression.py:70; fetch_gaia.py:374-377), so entering both double-counts Vs30. (4) Zhu wtd was fitted on Fan 2013 mean water-table depth; a P10 seasonal high is outside the calibration domain unless refitted or bounded. Benchmarking against WA DNR/Palmer compares an event-conditioned probability with a static geologic susceptibility class (roadmap-review:89); it can serve as a sanity check, not validation.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #260, #270.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---
Wording: until #270 passes, the product is a static susceptibility with seasonal-high DTW as a documented sensitivity, not a dynamic groundwater-conditioned forecast.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** One documentation fix: Vs30 is site amplification/class, not a triggering variable (#147 merged here).

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Retarget: (a) 07-hazard-integration.qmd:85-95: the GLM consumes ln Vs30 with its sigma, and the NEHRP P(class) is a separate design-engineering product; (b) stop calling Sanger & Maurer 2025 a GLM (03b:31, 07:89); (c) 01-input-data.qmd:54: SVM preferred, Wald-Allen fallback; (d) soil_mechanics.py:1-14 and :61-62 docstrings. Acceptance: grep shows no 'GLM' attached to sanger2025liquefaction and no P(class) described as a liquefaction-model input; the book builds. Merge #147 into this as one docs PR.

### Problems found

- Cited lines (fetch_vs30.py:175-218) are stale; the profile integrators are now at fetch_vs30.py:188-298
- The 'remove CSR/CRR-from-Vs30 implication' task has no current target; the real defect is NEHRP-probability-as-GLM-input
- There is no testable acceptance

### Physics assessment

The physics is correct: Vs30 is a 30 m harmonic average and a site-amplification proxy, while triggering lives in a 1-10 m critical layer (Andrus-Stokoe and Kayen use the overburden-corrected Vs1 of that layer). It is largely already true on main. No doc derives CSR/CRR from Vs30 (grep finds only 07b-resolution-requirements.qmd:41-42, which already tiers screening against CPT triggering). The remaining errors are elsewhere. 07-hazard-integration.qmd:89-95 says 'For the Sanger liquefaction GLM the stiffness is delivered as NEHRP site-class probability', but every geospatial liquefaction model takes continuous ln Vs30, not P(class). 03b:31 and 07:89 call the Sanger & Maurer AI model a 'GLM'. 01-input-data.qmd:54 still lists Wald-Allen as the Vs30 source.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`07-hazard-integration.qmd:36-45`, `fetch_vs30.py:175-218`: Vs30 = travel-time average over the top 30 m — a ShakeMap amplification proxy. Liquefaction triggers in a 1-10 m loose saturated low-fines layer a 30 m harmonic average buries (C1). Vs-based triggering (Andrus-Stokoe, Kayen) uses overburden-corrected Vs1 of the CRITICAL layer.

**Do:** docs state Vs30 is an amplification/site-class covariate — fine as a GLM predictor, NOT a triggering measure; remove any CSR/CRR-from-Vs30 implication.

</details>

body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** PI pins the liquefaction model (#260).

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Add a 'Decision required (human)' section that picks one model and version with its coefficient/weights source: Zhu 2017 Model 2 (BSSA 107:1365, plus Rashidian & Baise 2020 caps), or Sanger & Maurer 2025 if its weights are obtainable. State the probability semantics (Zhu P is converted to areal extent, LSE, not a point probability). Replace 'genuine contribution' with a hypothesis gated on the sensitivity study (new gap issue). Add order: 140/147 (docs) -> 144, 143 -> sensitivity gate -> 141 -> 142 (only if the gate passes) -> 146 deferred. Add the needs-human-decision label until the model is chosen. Add an event-validation sub-issue (Nisqually 2001).

### Problems found

- The model is not pinned: Zhu 2017 GLM and Sanger & Maurer 2025 geospatial AI are conflated (roadmap-review:89 demands pinning)
- The premise that the dynamic water table adds value is unquantified and, under Zhu 2017, an order of magnitude below Vs30/PGV uncertainty
- Sub-issue order and blockers are not encoded; the grouper skips the epic (gaia_group_issues.py:176-177) and has no BLOCKED_BY entries for 140-149
- It depends on a depth-to-water time series that does not exist (landlab_export.py:333-335)
- There is no event-based validation (WA DNR/Palmer are susceptibility maps, not event outcomes)

### Physics assessment

Framing it as a regional susceptibility screen rather than an LPI is right, and the Sept 10 audit agrees (soil-twin-system-audit:137; roadmap-review:20). The value proposition is wrong as stated: 'the twin's genuine contribution' is the modeled seasonal-high depth-to-water, but in Zhu 2017 wtd carries -0.0333 per metre, so a 1 to 5 m change gives dP of about 0.03, against about 0.3 for 1-sigma Vs30 and 0.1 for PGV (wf/liq/zhu_sens.py). Zhu's wtd was also fitted on an equilibrium mean water-table model (Fan et al. 2013), so substituting a P10 seasonal high is a covariate shift outside the fitted model. The 'Sanger-Maurer framework' named in the title is a geospatial-AI model (references.bib:338-346), not the published logistic model the MVP text describes.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

The twin is pitched as a liquefaction feed, but there is **no triggering code** anywhere (`grep LPI|CSR|CRR|Boulanger|Idriss` returns only prose), and the one join module `src/models/soil_mechanics.py:64` raises `NotImplementedError`. What is delivered is Vs30 -> NEHRP site-class probability (`docs/twin/07-hazard-integration.qmd:36-45`), a site-AMPLIFICATION quantity, not triggering.

## MVP (quick, physically grounded, uses the twin's value-add)
Drive a **published geospatial liquefaction GLM** (Zhu et al. 2017; Maurer et al. — the Sanger-Maurer framework) with **Vs30** (have it), the twin's **modeled seasonal-high depth-to-water** (the term static GLMs only approximate — the twin's genuine contribution), and **PGV** from a scenario USGS ShakeMap. Output a liquefaction probability/susceptibility screen benchmarked against WA DNR / Palmer. No CPT needed; respects the resolution (a screen, not a CPT-based LPI) while delivering the dynamic-water-table advance.

## Sub-issues
- [ ] #140 Reframe Vs30 as site amplification / class, NOT a liquefaction triggering variable
- [ ] #141 MVP: geospatial liquefaction GLM driven by the dynamic seasonal-high water table + scenario ShakeMap PGV
- [ ] #142 Seasonal-high depth-to-water in liquefiable units: sub-1.5 m accuracy, uncertainty, non-TOPMODEL prior
- [ ] #143 Ingest USGS ShakeMap ground motion (PGA / PGV / Mw) with epistemic uncertainty
- [ ] #144 Per-cell Vs30 sigma field so P(NEHRP class) is not decorative
- [ ] #145 Firewall the coseismic dv/v damage/healing state from liquefaction TRIGGERING (category error)
- [ ] #146 Future: depth-resolved triggering (CPT/SPT + Vs(z) critical layer + CSR/CRR)
- [ ] #147 Scope honestly: a susceptibility screen, not an LPI — 90 m from a 200 m SVM cannot resolve facies
- [ ] #148 Wald-Allen Vs30 proxy is near-degenerate on flat liquefiable ground — document and guard
- [ ] #149 Minor fixes (liquefaction review)

Depth-to-water accuracy is shared with Milestone 1.


</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Items redistributed, then closed.

**Audit verdict:** split

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #138` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Close #138 after redistributing its items:
- m1: defer into #19/#30 as a research question, with a footprint-mismatch caveat.
- m2: fold into #64 as 'seasonal-high = annual-minimum DTW with a GEV return level (e.g. 2-yr, 10-yr), requires a >=10 yr daily/monthly DTW series'.
- m3: fold into #133.
- m4: close as documentation-already-present.

### Problems found

- The roadmap review lists #138 as containing substantive operator requirements under a 'minor/P2' label.
- Mixed-scope bullets, so no single PR is possible.
- m4 touches the paused Vs30 lane.

### Physics assessment

m1 (dv/v -> FS operator): physically weak as stated. Ambient-noise dv/v at 1-10 Hz samples effective stress over a coda footprint of hundreds of metres laterally and tens to hundreds of metres in depth. It cannot resolve failure-plane pore pressure at 1-3 m in a 10-50 m hollow. At best it is a regional wetness covariate, and measured dv/v is not ingested yet (#30). m2: P10 of a monthly DTW series is exceeded in about 10% of months (about 1.2 months/yr). That is a sub-annual typical wet-season state, not a return-period event. Tying it to a return period needs annual-minimum DTW and an extreme-value fit (GEV/Gumbel). m3 is correct and duplicates #133. m4 is a true statement by construction (forecast.py:26-29; root zone d/30 of the Vs30 averaging depth), not a task, and Vs30 is paused (ROADMAP:129-132).

From the DOT landslide review, minor items:
- [ ] dv/v is synthetic and unlinked to stability — add a dv/v -> FS / failure-plane-pressure operator once measured dv/v is ingested (m1).
- [ ] `seasonal_high_water_table` (P10 DTW, `landlab_export.py:58-67`) is the right reduction but needs an operational monthly DTW series to be produced (m2); tie the quantile to a return period.
- [ ] Saturated-area runoff fires at HAND~=0 (valley floors) where slides do NOT start; hillslope source areas for shallow failure are unmodeled (m3).
- [ ] Vs30 (200 m upsampled) barely moves with moisture by construction (`forecast.py:26-29`) — carries little dynamic landslide info (m4).

body:
> **Superseded 2026-10-18** by #284, #285, #286 under the PI's decision to make MODFLOW 6 the groundwater core (plan `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-modflow-groundwater-core/plan.md`, PR #273; epic #274). Held from the agent queue by the `superseded` label. Closing is the PI's call after reviewing the replacement.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Recalibrate after the fixes, with S_y bounded per geologic unit and scoring on wells and basins kept out of the fit.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Acceptance: (1) S_y bounded per hydrogeologic unit with cited ranges, e.g. till 0.02-0.10, outwash 0.15-0.30, volcanic below 0.05; (2) a frozen holdout manifest (wells by site, whole basins, one water year) committed BEFORE fitting, owned here and adopted by #189; (3) model fluxes basin-masked, model BFI from Lyne-Hollick on model Q, wells sampled at their cells; (4) report held-out metrics that are NOT in the objective: daily KGE at held-out gauges, recession constant, held-out well amplitude/phase, storm lag. Peak month and amplitude stop being called validation. Run on a multi-year spun-up daily record. Add these to BLOCKED_BY.

### Problems found

- 'S_y in a defensible range' gives no numbers or source, so the criterion cannot be tested.
- 'Skill on data NOT used' does not say which partition, metric or threshold.
- Every physics change (#172, #131, #173, #174, #175) shifts the fit, so this must come last. It also needs multi-year daily forcing (#70/#89), basin masks and frozen holdouts, none of which exist.
- It is a #187 blocker, but #189 (holdouts) is itself downstream of #187. If #137 waits for #189's holdout machinery, the dependencies form a cycle.
- The #100 phase residual should be judged here, but peak month is itself in the objective (calibrate_fluxes.py:81-86).

### Physics assessment

Correct: S_y = 0.30 (:62) was picked from the grid {0.05...0.40} (calibrate_fluxes.py:96). 0.30 is the top of the coarse sand/gravel range (Johnson 1967: sand about 0.27-0.30). It is implausible for the till and volcanic rocks that dominate the Cascades: Vashon till about 0.02-0.10, fractured volcanics below 0.05. The amplitude it is fit to (1.06 m) comes from monthly medians of discrete well visits, but the model side is a domain-mean over all land cells, not the well cells (calibrate_fluxes.py:76-79). S_y absorbs the missing vadose attenuation. 'Exactly-determined' is slightly inaccurate: it is 4 targets (BFI, Q/P, amplitude, peak month) on a coarse 120-point grid, but the conclusion holds. The right structure is S_y by hydrogeologic unit, with a depth-dependent S_y,eff for shallow tables, which matters for liquefaction (M2).

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #172, #173, #174, #175, #131, #100, #89, #235, #236.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`S_y = 0.30` (`water_budget.py:62`) is near total porosity and does three inconsistent jobs — WT rise per recharge (`:266`), fillable VSA deficit (`:230`), baseflow release (`:278`) (groundwater C3). The 'closure against gauges AND wells' is an exactly-determined 3-knob fit (S_y, K_aniso, R_ref -> amplitude, Q/P, BFI) with no held-out basin or leave-one-well-out (groundwater C2). This foundation feeds BOTH the landslide FS and the liquefaction water table (Milestone 2).

**Do:** separate drainable porosity (with rising/falling hysteresis) from near-surface fillable space; bound S_y to a physical range; re-close; add leave-one-well-out and held-out-basin validation reporting an independent scalar the calibration did not target.
**Acceptance:** S_y in a defensible range, and skill on data NOT used in calibration.

</details>

**In plain words:** FuXi GPU run: waits for the PI and compute.

**Audit verdict:** hold-human

### Specification

Merge into #71, move to the v0.7 milestone, and add a needs-compute/needs-human-decision label.

Acceptance:
- Hindcast of at least 10 AR events.
- Elevation-band quantile-mapped totals vs held-out SNOTEL/COOP gauges (not PRISM).
- CRPS/skill vs climatology by lead day.
- Keep the 6-hourly accumulations in the forcing object.

### Problems found

- It needs a GPU (9.4 GB weights; Hyak Tillicum H200 via deploy/tillicum-fuxi.yaml per ROADMAP:209-210), which an autonomous agent cannot obtain.
- It duplicates #71 (bias-correct AI QPF against PRISM; orographic downscaler) and #32. Roadmap review recommends unifying #71/#136/#32.
- Mis-milestoned: it is forcing/forecast (v0.7) work, not landslide handoff. In the queue it is batched with #224/#138/#135, an incoherent batch.
- The acceptance 'a real forecast run feeding the twin' is not a skill test, and fetch_earth2studio.py:155 aggregates FuXi to daily, discarding the 6-hourly steps #132 wants.

### Physics assessment

FuXi at 0.25 degrees (about 25 km) cannot resolve Cascade ridge-scale orographic enhancement (ROADMAP:126; 07b:23). Bias-correcting TOTALS against PRISM climatology (quantile mapping by elevation band) fixes the mean-climate bias but cannot recover event-scale spatial structure, which requires the orographic downscaler task in #71. PRISM is itself an interpolated product (gauge-anchored, climatology-aided), and it serves as the bias target, so it cannot also be the independent validation. Deterministic AI precipitation skill beyond about 7-10 days is near climatology for event totals, so '+1..15 d' needs probabilistic lead-time scoring (#195), not just 'a run'.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

The FuXi adapter is written but 'never run on a GPU' (`ROADMAP.md:23`); its 0.25 deg grid cannot resolve the Cascade crest where orographic enhancement dominates (`06-forecast.qmd:97-102`) (landslide M5). The advertised +1..15 d product has no demonstrated skill.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Waits for the PI's choice of corridors and lidar source.

**Audit verdict:** hold-human

### Specification

Human decides the corridors (e.g. I-90 Snoqualmie, US-2, SR-410 for the Rainier box) and the lidar source.

Agent-ready part:
- Write native 10 m slope/curvature/TWI rasters for named corridors.
- Add sub-grid slope quantiles (p50/p90/max) to the 90 m outputs.
- Acceptance: on the S24 inventory, the slope distribution at initiation points from 10 m vs 90 m is shifted by a reported amount (e.g. median delta in degrees).

Move cut-slope stability to a separate issue that uses a planar/wedge method on 1-3 m lidar.

### Problems found

- Corridor definition, road-cut source (WSDOT inventory vs lidar-derived) and lidar acquisition are human/data decisions.
- The acceptance is qualitative and untestable as written.
- It mixes a 90 m pore-pressure state with 10 m geometry without a downscaling rule (this ties to #133).
- Easy partial step not mentioned: slope is already computed at 10 m (compute_terrain_domain.py:151) and could be written out before coarsening, or summarized as sub-grid p90 slope per 90 m cell.

### Physics assessment

The diagnosis is correct. compute_terrain_domain.py:170-176 average-resamples 10 m slope/HAND/TWI to 90 m. Shallow failures need 1-10 m (07b-resolution-requirements.qmd:33). Two corrections. (1) A road cut is typically 3-15 m high and 5-20 m wide in plan, so a 10 m DEM still smooths it; cut faces need 1-3 m lidar (WA DNR lidar / 3DEP 1 m). (2) Cut slopes are height-limited, steep (often >45 degrees) faces where infinite-slope FS is not valid; Culmann/planar-wedge or rock-slope methods apply. So 'FS resolves cut-slope facets' asks infinite slope to do something it physically cannot. Cost: the roughly 100,000 km2 domain at 10 m is about 1e9 cells per layer, so restricting to corridors is necessary, and the corridors are a human choice.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`compute_terrain_domain.py:172-178` average-resamples slope/HAND/TWI from 10 m to 90 m; a 90 m cell averages the road-cut face into the hillslope and understates the steep facets that fail (landslide C4). Shallow slides initiate at 10-30 m scales, often on the cut itself.

**Do:** compute FS on <=10 m slope/curvature at corridors and add an explicit cut-slope layer; keep 90 m only for deep-seated (10^2-10^3 m) features.
**Acceptance:** FS resolves cut-slope facets that the 90 m field smooths away.

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Split: soil strength and soil thickness maps now; post-fire later.

**Audit verdict:** split

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #134` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Split it in two.

(A) 'FS strength/geometry parameter fields', agent-ready:
- c_r from NLCD/LANDFIRE with literature ranges and a sigma.
- H from a published slope-dependent soil-depth model, cross-checked against SOLUS, with the 2 m cap flagged.
- Acceptance: fields on grid with priors cited and sigma; values within literature ranges.

(B) 'Post-fire hazard pathway', after #121's body is fixed:
- Ks multiplier with 2-4 yr recovery feeding #132's infiltration capacity.
- c_r decay/regrowth curve with its minimum around 5-10 yr.
- The post-fire debris-flow probability via the Staley 2017 M1 logistic, not FS.
- Acceptance: year-1 runoff increase inside the perimeter; c_r minimum timing matches the decay/regrowth model.

### Problems found

- The c_r/H lookup duplicates #128's 'root cohesion c_r (land-cover lookup) ... colluvium thickness z (slope-dependent soil-depth model)'.
- The post-fire part duplicates #121/#122. Their bodies are shifted (2026-09-10 roadmap review: #121 holds the disturbance body, #124/#125 duplicate), so 'coordinate with #122' points at the wrong body.
- No MTBS/burn-perimeter fetcher exists in src.
- The acceptance encodes wrong recovery physics.

### Physics assessment

c_r and colluvium thickness H are necessary FS inputs. Literature priors exist: c_r about 2-25 kPa in PNW conifer forests and about 1-7 kPa in clearcuts (Schmidt et al. 2001); H from soil-production/slope models, or SOLUS depth. Note that SOLUS is capped at 2 m (#224 caveat), which matters for anything deeper. The post-fire acceptance is physically wrong on timing and mechanism. (1) Root reinforcement does not drop at the fire and recover over 3 yr. Roots of killed trees decay over years while regrowth lags, so c_r reaches its MINIMUM about 3-10+ years after stand death (Sidle 1992 decay/regrowth model). (2) The 1-3 yr post-fire debris-flow hazard is dominantly RUNOFF-generated (reduced infiltration, sediment bulking; USGS Staley et al. 2017 M1 model with I15, dNBR and soil erodibility), not infinite-slope shallow failure. Reduced Ks actually lowers infiltration and pore pressure, which can RAISE FS in year 1. So 'a burn perimeter lowers FS and recovers over ~3 yr' tests the wrong hazard model.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Root cohesion `c_r`, colluvium thickness `H`, and post-fire hydrophobicity/cohesion-loss appear nowhere in the state (landslide M4); post-fire debris flow is the highest-consequence corridor hazard and is exactly the reduced-Ks + lost-cohesion + intensity regime the product cannot represent. These overlap the v0.6 disturbance epic (#119, #122).

**Do:** add `c_r` (land-cover), `H` (soil-depth model), and a post-fire perturbation (Ks-multiplier down, `c_r` down) with multi-year recovery, feeding FS. Coordinate with #122.
**Acceptance:** a burn perimeter lowers FS inside it and recovers over ~3 yr.

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Phase 2 of the perched store: route perched water to downslope/convergent cells to build pore pressure in hollows.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Keep it as phase 2 of the #130 store with BLOCKED_BY {133: [130]}.

Specify: a steady-state or kinematic lateral delivery on the 90 m D8 graph, plus a 10 m TOPMODEL wetness downscaler for FS on #135 corridors.

Acceptance:
- Basin ledger closes (interflow delivered + exfiltrated = interflow generated).
- Q/P re-closed.
- Synthetic convergent hollow shows higher h_w/z than the planar slope for the same storm.
- The 90 m vs 10 m limitation is documented.

Fold in #138 m3.

### Problems found

- It depends on #130's perched store (it converts convergence into 'a perched head') but is batched simultaneously with #130 (batch 21).
- Double-counting risk: once interflow is delivered downslope, the exported Q/interflow source term (#200) and the Q/P 0.71 calibration both change (roadmap review R7: 'the same transferred water is not also counted as outlet discharge').
- Acceptance has no conservation check, no resolution statement, and no observational check (it is synthetic only).
- Overlap with #174 and with #138 m3 (hillslope source areas).

### Physics assessment

The physics diagnosis is correct and is the central shallow-landslide mechanism (Montgomery & Dietrich 1994; Iverson 2000). water_budget.py:248-249 removes interflow from the column, and it never loads a downslope cell. However, convergent hollows are 10-50 m wide (07b-resolution-requirements.qmd:33), so 90 m D8 accumulation largely smooths them out. The perched head that matters lives at <=10 m and needs a downscaling step such as TOPMODEL/SHALSTAB wetness from 10 m specific contributing area. The column model is also vectorized per cell with no lateral graph, so this is an architectural change: a topologically ordered cell loop or a steady-state wetness approximation.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #130, #174.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`water_budget.py:248-249` sends interflow 'downslope' straight into streamflow Q; it is never delivered to a downslope cell or accumulated in convergence hollows (landslide M2). For shallow failures the trigger is transient POSITIVE pore pressure from lateral stormflow convergence — here that water is accounted as gauge discharge, i.e. a loss, not a stress.

**Do:** route interflow to downslope/convergent cells (topographic accumulation) and convert convergence to a perched head that feeds FS.
**Acceptance:** convergence hollows show elevated perched head and reduced FS after a storm.

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Post-fire infiltration excess only (Green-Ampt), after #134.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Merge into #57 or rewrite.

Scope:
- Add a Green-Ampt infiltration capacity using the existing Ksat (and the post-fire Ks multiplier from #134/#122).
- Run dt_days <= 1/24 on the triggering path, with MRMS hourly for hindcast.

Acceptance:
(a) Unburned forest cells produce no infiltration excess for the Dec 2025 AR (consistent with the rainier3d Richards result).
(b) A burned cell with Ks x 0.1-0.3 does produce it.
(c) The ledger closes.

State explicitly that I15 is out of reach of the forcing products.

### Problems found

- It duplicates #57 (daily/hourly bucket re-derivation; notes FuXi 6-hourly is discarded).
- It is mis-milestoned: this is water-budget/forcing physics, not landslide handoff.
- The acceptance test is satisfiable trivially by any intensity-dependent runoff rule and says nothing about PNW realism.
- It does not specify a sub-daily hindcast source: MRMS 1 h exists in rainier3d S29 (#224), while FuXi sub-daily is forecast-only and unrun (#136).

### Physics assessment

The motivating arithmetic is right: 68 mm/day = 2.8 mm/h. But the requested remedy is physically insufficient on three counts. (1) The budget has no infiltration-capacity term at all. Runoff is only saturation-area and root-zone excess (water_budget.py:229-237), and Ksat is computed but unused (#177 m3). Sub-daily forcing alone cannot produce Hortonian runoff; a Green-Ampt/Philip capacity is needed. (2) In unburned PNW forest soils Ksat (roughly 10-100+ mm/h) exceeds even hourly AR intensities (about 5-20 mm/h). The rainier3d 1-D Richards run with MRMS 1 h QPE produced no runoff for the Dec 2025 AR (rainier3d_map.md:5). Hortonian triggering is relevant mainly on burned, compacted or road surfaces. (3) Post-fire debris-flow thresholds use 15-30 min peak intensity (I15/I30). FuXi 6-hourly accumulations smooth those peaks by about 24x in time, so '>=6-hourly' does not reach the regime the issue names.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #134.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

At a daily mean, a 68 mm/day storm is 2.8 mm/hr and never exceeds Ksat, so the model structurally cannot fire infiltration-excess/burst triggering (landslide M3-fall; ROADMAP #57). FuXi's native 6-hourly steps are currently discarded to run daily.

**Do:** ingest sub-daily (>=6-hourly) intensity for the triggering path so Hortonian and post-fire debris-flow regimes can exist; keep the daily budget for the seasonal state.
**Acceptance:** an intense sub-daily burst generates infiltration-excess runoff where a daily-mean equivalent does not.

</details>

> **Superseded 2026-10-18** by UZF kinematic wave in #282, scored in #286 under the PI's decision to make MODFLOW 6 the groundwater core (plan `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-modflow-groundwater-core/plan.md`, PR #273; epic #274). Held from the agent queue by the `superseded` label. Closing is the PI's call after reviewing the replacement.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** How long recharge takes to cross the deep unsaturated store (kinematic celerity, not particle travel time). #87 is closed into this.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Make it the timescale parameterization of #172's store: outflow from U with tau = (d0-h-z_root)/c(theta, K(theta)), using a texture-specific K(theta) (folds in #177 m3). Acceptance: (1) ledger passes; (2) storm-to-peak lag vs at least N continuous wells (new gap issue) at held-out sites; (3) seasonal peak month on held-out wells is no worse than before. Carry over #87's Nash-cascade option and comment history. Move the scope decision to #171. BLOCKED_BY 131:[172, continuous-wells gap].

### Problems found

- Acceptance requires 'a continuous well hydrograph'. The repo only ingests discrete field measurements aggregated to site-month medians (download_nwis_domain.py:6-15), so the acceptance cannot be tested.
- It is the same mechanism as #172's store. As written, two issues would each add a store.
- It duplicates #87.
- The 'or narrow the GWL claim' branch is a human scope decision.
- In batch 8 it runs after #137, so the lag would be added after the calibration.

### Physics assessment

The diagnosis is right: there is zero delay (:266, forecast.py:31-34). Two parts of the prescription are physically off. (1) Unsaturated thickness should be depth-to-water minus root depth (d0 - h - z_root), not HAND. (2) Head responds to the kinematic celerity c = dK/dtheta, not the particle velocity, and Ksat-based or Green-Ampt estimates (#87) are far too fast. For Brooks-Corey K ~ theta^n with n about 8-12 at about 3 mm/d flux, c is roughly 0.1-0.3 m/d. That gives about 15-40 d through 4 m, and months through the roughly 20 m Puget-lowland vadose zones (#87 comment). Macropore preferential flow can be much faster. A 3-30 d sensitivity is reasonable only for shallow tables. Note the tension with #100: the calibrated model already peaks a month late (#100 comment). That evidence comes from a 10-month unspun run and is weak, but any lag must not degrade seasonal phase.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #172.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`water_budget.py:266` applies root-base drainage to head in the same step it leaves the 1 m root zone; the tens-of-metres unsaturated column (HAND-deep) has zero storage and zero delay. `forecast.py:31-34` admits GWL timing is 'early'. Issue #87 was demoted on a SEASONAL-phase argument, but the advertised product is a +1..15 day forecast where metres of unsaturated transit (days-weeks) is first-order (raised by groundwater C1 and landslide M3).

**Do:** add a linear-reservoir/convolution lag between root-base drainage and head, scaled by unsaturated-zone thickness (HAND / depth-to-water) and unsaturated K; publish a sensitivity of the 1-15 day WT response to a 3-30 day lag. Or narrow the GWL claim to antecedent/seasonal state.
**Acceptance:** the storm-scale WT response shows a physically-scaled delay, validated against a continuous well hydrograph.

</details>

**Rescoped 2026-10-18 for the MODFLOW 6 groundwater core.** Plan and design record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-modflow-groundwater-core/plan.md` (#273); epic #274.

## Purpose
Fall-shallow vs spring-deep water-table regimes come from perched water above a low-K cap over a
deeper table. In MODFLOW this is layering, not a separate bucket.

## Deliverable
In the pilot (#282): the cap as its own layer with NPF `VARIABLECV DEWATERED` and `PERCHED`,
UZF linking below the cap, and a comparison against the pilot without the perched treatment.
A 1-D column (perched mound, cap, 20 m vadose zone, deep table) checked against the Richards
reference (#267) for perched head and leakage.

## Acceptance
- Column test: perched head and leakage within a stated tolerance of the Richards reference.
- At recorder wells above and below the cap: timing of the fall response and the spring peak,
  with and without the perched treatment, reported.

## Hard blockers
Blocked by: #282, #235.

## Advisory follow-ups
#133 (convergent hollows at 10 m for landslides) consumes the perched head.


<details><summary>Scope before the 2026-10-18 MODFLOW refactor (archived, not current)</summary>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Moves to the water-budget milestone: the shared perched store gives a fast fall response while the deep table lags.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Move it to milestone 'Water budget: vadose-zone physics & calibration' and make it THE shared perched/interflow store, absorbing #174's store task.

Acceptance:
- Ledger closes to 1e-6 mm.
- Synthetic fall storm: perched head peaks within days while the regional table lags by weeks.
- Q/P and BFI re-closed on held-out basins (#137).
- The issue records that the perched store is unconstrained by NWIS.
- Name the store in the #187 contract.

Encode BLOCKED_BY {130: [174]} or merge #174 into it.

### Problems found

- It overlaps #174 (interflow store), #173 (fillable deficit) and #131 (vadose lag), all in the Water budget milestone (batches 6-8). This issue sits in the landslide milestone (batch 21), so two agents will build competing perched/interflow stores in coupled_water_budget.
- Batch 21 = [134,133,132,130] puts four agents in the same function, coupled_water_budget, at once, which guarantees conflicts.
- It changes the state vector while the #187 canonical contract is still held; the contract should name the store.
- Acceptance does not require mass-balance closure, Q/P/BFI re-closure, or a statement of which observation constrains the shallow store.

### Physics assessment

Correct and important. water_budget.py carries one head with HAND recession (:266-279) and drains interflow instantaneously (:248-249), so it has no perched water body. The 2026-08-20 comment correctly calls for three distinct water bodies (perched/transient, regional phreatic, confined head) with different observation semantics. The perched store is essentially unobserved by NWIS wells, so its parameters are prior-dominated, and the acceptance test can only be synthetic behavioral plus mass balance. Any added store changes Q/P and BFI, so it forces re-calibration against #98/#137.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #172, #174.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

`src/models/water_budget.py:157,266-279` carries ONE head anomaly on a linear reservoir with one recession (`RECESSION_MONTHS=6`). The two failure regimes are defined by different water bodies at different depths and timescales; a single store collapses them (raised independently by the landslide and groundwater reviewers).

**Do:** add a transient shallow interflow/perched store (flashy, fall shallow control) distinct from the deep GWL store (lagged/persistent, spring deep-seated control). 
**Acceptance:** a fall storm produces a flashy shallow response while the deep table lags; both drive FS separately.

</details>


</details>

**Amended 2026-11-09 by the soil-state review ladder (#296; record `docs/reviews/2026-11-07-fable-soil-state-review/`).** Integration acceptance made causal.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Waits for the PI's choice of corridor, landslide inventory and LandLab adapter path.

**Audit verdict:** hold-human

### Specification

Hold for human decisions: pilot corridor, inventory (S24 Rainier vs WA DNR lidar inventory), and the LandLab-vs-own-FS adapter path.

Then rewrite:
- Shallow-only event hindcast (Jan 2009 S24, merging #224's landslide part into this issue or making #224 the vehicle).
- Report AUC/POD/FAR against two baselines (slope-only; rainfall threshold), plus a time-shifted-forcing control.
- If LandLab is used, R = rech + interflow (the adapter documented).
- Add landlab pinned to an exact version.
- Encode BLOCKED_BY {129: [128, 135]}.

### Problems found

- No BLOCKED_BY on #128 (roadmap review: '#129's end-to-end landslide score needs #128 and suitable terrain/head inputs'), so it is dispatched in the same run as #128.
- landlab is not in pixi.toml; no inventory fetcher exists; no corridor is chosen.
- It duplicates #224's landslide part (S24, 351 dated Jan-2009 slides in the Rainier box), which is the one dated inventory available.
- It has no negative control or baseline (slope-only, rainfall-threshold such as the USGS Seattle cumulative-precip threshold), so AUC alone is uninformative.
- It runs on the 90 m grid unless #135 lands first. The review says #135's fine-slope contract must precede shallow-failure validation.

### Physics assessment

Scoring against an inventory is the right validation, and POD/FAR/AUC is appropriate. LandslideProbability is a steady-state, recharge-driven Monte Carlo model; it does not ingest the twin's transient head (followup review lines 60-67). Feeding it the exported recharge_mm is physically inconsistent: that flux excludes interflow (water_budget.py:248-249), while LandLab's R is recharge to the perched layer, so R is underestimated by about (1 - f_lat), roughly 2x at tanB=0.5. A slope-only baseline is mandatory, because event slides sit at median 27.9 degrees vs 18.5 degrees for the box (#224), so slope alone gives a high AUC.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Factor of safety for shallow slides in a new slope-stability module, with suction and named pore-pressure conventions.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Retitle it 'Infinite-slope FS kernel + named pore-pressure closures (shallow only)'.

Scope:
- New function infinite_slope_fs(slope, z_or_h, c_eff, phi, gamma_moist, gamma_sat, h_w, closure={'hydrostatic','slope_parallel'}) in a new src/models/slope_stability.py.
- Leave estimate_mechanics untouched.
- Parameters are injected; #134 owns the fields.

Acceptance:
- Unit tests: dry FS = c/(gamma z sinB cosB) + tanphi/tanB; flat-slope limit; saturated limit; monotone decrease in h_w.
- The two closures differ by a factor cos^2B in u, tested at 30 degrees.
- Numeric agreement with LandLab's normal-thickness form to 1e-6.
- The closure is recorded in output metadata.
- Analytic first-order sigma_FS from input sigmas.

Move the corridor run to #129.

### Problems found

- The target function is wrong: estimate_mechanics (soil_mechanics.py:56-71) is a Vs30/dv/v stiffness contract for liquefaction twins. Implementing FS inside it breaks or overloads that contract. FS belongs in a new function or module.
- Parameter ownership duplicates #134: both ask for a c_r land-cover lookup and a soil-depth model.
- 'FS field on the pilot corridor' has no corridor named, no h_w source, and no data; agents will invent them.
- The 'per-cell uncertainty companion' is undefined (first-order delta method? MC from which input sigmas?). #193 will later replace it with member evaluation.
- The 2026-08-20 closure-metadata acceptance comment is not in the body (roadmap review R7 flags this).
- P0 puts it alone in batch 3, ahead of the water-budget foundations. That is fine only if scope is algebra plus closures.

### Physics assessment

The algebra is textbook and correct for shallow translational failures. The pore-pressure closure matters: slope-parallel u = gamma_w h_w cos^2B is 25% below hydrostatic at 30 degrees, and hydro_state.py:209/229 already gives both closures as named functions. Several things are physically underspecified. (a) 'Saturation -> h_w' for fall failures has no physical conversion: root-zone theta/theta_s says nothing about positive pressure head. The budget has no perched head until #130/#133, so the MVP can only use h_w = max(z - DTW, 0) from the regional table, and that is near zero on most hillslopes (median DTW metres to tens of metres). The FS 'response to wetting' will therefore be weak, and the run must report that as a result, not hide it. (b) The z-vs-h convention must be pinned: LandLab uses slope-normal thickness h = z cosB. A unit test should show agreement with LandLab's dimensionless form FS = [C/(h rho_s g) + cosB(1 - r R_w)tanphi]/sinB.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

**Do:** implement the infinite-slope FS of the epic, with pore pressure `u = gamma_w * h_w` from the modeled saturation/perched head (fall) and seasonal-high table (spring), root cohesion `c_r` (land-cover lookup), effective friction `phi'` and colluvium thickness `z` (slope-dependent soil-depth model). Return FS and a per-cell uncertainty companion. Re-scope the docs from 'delivered' to this MVP.
**Acceptance:** FS field on the pilot corridor; monotone response to wetting; unit tests on the FS algebra (dry vs saturated, flat vs steep).

</details>

Rewrite the body:

- State the adapter decision as an explicit fork: twin-computed FS from twin h_w (#128), versus LandLab LandslideProbability fed R = total root-zone drainage (rech+interflow) with its own TOPMODEL wetness. Mark this needs-human-decision.
- Update the child list: remove #126/#131/#137, add #224 and the new gap issues.
- Fold in the closure comment.

### Problems found

- Body is stale: it says landlab_export.py:265 calls coupled_water_budget without slope_tan/hand_m/dt_days, but #126 is closed and src/io/landlab_export.py:260-307 now runs the calibrated configuration.
- Sub-issue list still includes closed #126 and the moved #131/#137, and omits #224 (the S24 Rainier ROC/AUC that is the most concrete validation available).
- The MVP covers deep-seated failures with an infinite-slope model, which the 2026-09-10 roadmap review R7 explicitly says to separate.
- It conflates its own FS (#128) with LandLab LandslideProbability (#129). LandLab derives wetness from recharge/T/a/sinB (followup review lines 60-67), so the twin's h_w cannot drive it without an adapter or bypass decision.
- Pore-pressure-closure comment (2026-08-20) is not yet folded into the body/children.

### Physics assessment

The FS expression is the standard infinite-slope form with slope-parallel seepage when z and h_w are vertical heights: [c'+c_r+(gamma_sat z - gamma_w h_w)cos^2B tanphi']/(gamma_sat z sinB cosB). Using gamma_sat for the whole column overweights the unsaturated part (moist unit weight is about 10-15% lower). This is a minor, conservative-ish approximation; it should be stated. The serious error is applying infinite slope to SPRING DEEP-SEATED failures driven by a seasonal-high table. Infinite slope needs z/L << 1. Deep-seated slides (S24 median depth 14.6 m, #224; 10^2-10^3 m per #135) need limit-equilibrium/3-D analysis or an explicit exclusion. The claim that it 'needs no new field data' is false: inventory scoring (#129) needs an inventory, and c_r/z need literature priors.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

Executed fact (official Landlab source; #300): `LandslideProbability` computes relative wetness from sampled recharge, transmissivity, contributing area and slope; it has no water-table or pore-pressure input. The adapter fork is therefore (i) recharge-driven screening with the stock component, or (ii) the twin's own FS kernel (#128) fed by h_w. #300's positive control and invariance test are the integration acceptance for (i).

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Restored body: dv/v attribution.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Move the attribution text from #122 here. Retarget to the augmented space-time estimator (#162), with the state vector hydrology (via #198) + D + Φ + a temperature/loading confounder. AC: on a synthetic run with known components and realistic correlated Cd (#164), the #169 rank/identifiability diagnostic is computed first; for identifiable cases the recovered components fall within posterior 90% intervals at nominal coverage; non-identifiable cases are flagged as prior-dominated. Remove the dvv_proxy reference. BLOCKED_BY 123:[162,169,121,122,164].

### Problems found

- Wrong body (shifted).
- It names the static BLUE (observability.blue_update, observability.py:1217) as the estimator, contradicting #162.
- The AC extends a demo that no longer exists.
- No confounder states are included.
- Queue batch 18 places it before #121 (batch 19), which supplies D, and outside the encoded blockers.

### Physics assessment

The body holds the event-catalog text from #124; the attribution text sits in #122. The intended approach, augmenting the static BLUE with D and Φ, cannot separate processes by their temporal signatures, because a static snapshot BLUE has no time dimension. That needs the space-time estimator (#162) and the rank test (#169). Attribution also omits the dominant non-hydrologic dv/v drivers: thermoelastic and temperature terms, snow and atmospheric loading (1 m SWE ≈ 10 kPa total-stress load, comparable to a ~1 m water-table change at shallow depth) and tides. Their omission biases the hydrology/damage split. The cited target demo dvv_proxy was removed (pixi.toml:187). Illien 2022 shows damage and drainage covary after large events, so separability is conditional, not guaranteed.

body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Restored body: wildfire, tillage and landslide disturbance.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Move the surface-disturbance text from #121 here and amend it as follows. Φ becomes separate states: repellency/Ks multiplier (recovery τ ~1-4 yr), root-cohesion deficit (lagged decline, peak ~5-10 yr, owned by #134), tillage porosity/ρ_b (seasonal), and landslide remolding (cohesion step). ACs: with #132 sub-daily forcing, the burned cell's runoff ratio rises by the prior-specified factor and relaxes with τ; tillage changes drainage recession time; the predicted dv/v perturbation at each band is reported via #198a with an explicit 'below detection' flag where it is invisible. BLOCKED_BY 122:[132,198].

### Problems found

- Wrong body (shifted).
- Its central mechanism depends on Hortonian infiltration (#132), which is not encoded as a dependency.
- It conflates hydrophobicity recovery with root-cohesion loss.
- The dv/v-signature AC is not falsifiable at 0.1-4 Hz for a 0.3 m tillage layer.

### Physics assessment

The body holds #123's attribution text. The correct body is currently in #121, and its physics needs three fixes. (1) Fire mainly reduces infiltration through water repellency and sealing, which matters for infiltration-excess (Hortonian) runoff. water_budget.py has saturation-excess only and states that Hortonian runoff is not represented and needs sub-daily rain (water_budget.py:41-44; #132). A Ks multiplier on this bucket would therefore not produce 'more runoff inside the perimeter', and the AC is untestable on main. (2) Root cohesion after fire declines over roughly 3-10 years as roots decay, while repellency recovers over 1-4 years. These are opposite trajectories on different clocks, so a single relaxing Φ state is wrong; #134 owns the root-cohesion part. (3) 'Both leave a dv/v signature' must be quantified through the #198 operator; tillage loosening lowers ρ_b and breaks capillary connectivity (Shi et al. 2026), and the effect is confined to the top ~0.3 m, which these bands cannot see (probe).

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #134.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Part of #119.

**Attribution is the point.** dv/v sees hydrology, damage, and disturbance at once; because they carry **different space-time signatures**, the BLUE can separate them.

**Approach:** augment the observability control vector (src/models/observability.py) with the memory states `D` and `Phi`; the coda kernels (src/models/dvv_sensitivity.py) supply the **spatial** footprint and the distinct relaxation timescales supply the **temporal** discriminant; the dv/v innovation partitions among hydrology / damage / disturbance. Generalizes Illien et al. (2022, doi:10.1029/2021JB023402) damage-vs-drainage decomposition.

**Acceptance:** a synthetic dv/v containing a seasonal-hydrology signal + a coseismic drop-and-heal is separated by the augmented BLUE into its components (extends the `dvv_proxy` demo).


</details>

### Specification

Replace the body with a coseismic specification. Carried state D as K log-spaced relaxation modes; jump J = f(PGV; a, PGV_sat) with an uncertain prior; τmin and τmax priors; a ΔVs/Vs(z) depth profile with an e-folding depth parameter; output through #198a. AC: (i) the K-mode Markov recursion reproduces the analytic Snieder curve to within 5% over [10τmin, 0.1τmax]; (ii) dv/v versus log t has constant slope over that range; (iii) a synthetic scenario ShakeMap (e.g. a Nisqually-2001-like M6.8) produces a spatially varying drop and recovery through the band kernels; (iv) a #145 firewall test shows D is not passed to triggering. Move the current body to #122. Add BLOCKED_BY 121:[198]; use synthetic ShakeMap fixtures so that #124 gates only the real-event run.

### Problems found

- The body describes wildfire, tillage and landslide (shifted from #122); an agent would build the wrong thing.
- There are no acceptance criteria for coseismic damage.
- Queue batch 19 runs it alone, after attribution (#123) and the chapter in batch 18, which inverts the dependency order.
- There is no code yet: grep finds no damage or healing in src/.

### Physics assessment

The title's physics is right: coseismic dv/v drops followed by log-linear 'slow dynamics' healing, with a substrate-controlled rate (Illien 2025; Wang 2021; chapter 03c:67-74). The body is the surface-disturbance text that belongs to #122, so no coseismic specification exists anywhere. A correct specification is as follows. The damage state D(x,z,t) enters ΔVs(z,t) in the #198 operator, concentrated in the top tens of metres. The jump size is a saturating function of PGV or dynamic strain from ShakeMap; observed drops are ~0.1-1% at 1-2 Hz for regional M6-7 shaking and much larger very near the surface, so this is an order-of-magnitude prior. Healing should follow the Snieder et al. 2017 relaxation spectrum, dv/v ∝ ∫_{τmin}^{τmax} e^{-t/τ} dτ/τ, which is log-linear for τmin ≪ t ≪ τmax. To keep the state Markov, represent it as a Prony series of 4-6 carried exponentials with log-spaced τ. The single exponential in #190 is the wrong law (roadmap-review R5). Healing must not feed liquefaction triggering (#145).

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #124.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Part of #119.

Event-driven perturbations to **hydraulic + mechanical parameters** that recover over months-years, for the surface disturbance classes:

- **wildfire** — hydrophobicity up, infiltration/Ks down; recovery 2-4 (up to ~6) yr;
- **agricultural (agroseismology)** — tillage/compaction disrupts capillary connectivity -> slower drainage, more evaporation, crusting (Shi et al. 2026, doi:10.1126/science.aec0970);
- **landslide / ground failure** — remolding, cohesion down.

**Model:** a per-cell perturbation state `Phi` (Ks-multiplier, hydrophobicity offset, cohesion) set by an event and relaxed on that process's timescale; multiplies the infiltration/envelope terms in src/models/water_budget.py and the Saxton-Rawls envelope.

**Acceptance:** a fire perimeter reduces infiltration inside it (more runoff), recovering over ~3 yr; a tillage event slows drainage; both leave a dv/v signature.


</details>
