## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Narrowed DataSource scope.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Narrow the scope.
- PRISM daily wrapped as a `DataSource`, with tp converted from mm/day to metres over the accumulation interval as declared.
- The FuXi store wrapped as a forecast source keyed by (init time, lead time).
- Drop in-situ observations, or defer them to a dataframe source if one exists.
- Round-trip tests run without earth2studio by duck-typing the protocol; earth2studio import stays lazy.

Acceptance: a slice read through the adapter equals the Zarr slice, and the lead-time coordinates are preserved. Once rewritten, an agent can do it.

### Problems found

- Registers the FuXi store under the wrong protocol.
- Puts in-situ point streams in scope without a suitable interface.
- No milestone; queued alone in batch 35.

### Physics assessment

This is a semantic error, not a physics one. The FuXi store is a forecast, indexed by initialization time and lead time. Wrapping it as a `DataSource` with `__call__(time, variable)` conflates valid time with lead time and loses initialization identity; earth2studio's forecast-source protocol (`__call__(time, lead_time, variable)`) is the correct fit. Point well and probe observations are not gridded and do not fit `DataSource`. Unit and convention mapping is non-trivial: earth2studio 'tp' is in metres per accumulation interval, while the repo stores mm/day.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Every stream is already staged as Zarr with a time-and-variable layout, which is one thin adapter from earth2studio's `DataSource` contract:

    __call__(time, variable) -> xr.DataArray  with dims [time, variable, ...]

Wrapping our Kopah stores as DataSources makes the FuXi forcing, the PRISM hindcast forcing, and the in-situ observation streams consumable by the same tooling that drives the AI weather models — the twin's data plane usable from the AI-weather ecosystem rather than siloed.

## Do
- [ ] A small `earth2studio`-shaped adapter: `KopahZarrSource(uri, var_map)` implementing `__call__(time, variable)` (and the async `fetch`) over a staged Zarr, mapping our variable names to Earth2Studio variable ids.
- [ ] Register the FuXi forcing store and the PRISM daily store as DataSources.
- [ ] Round-trip test: a DataSource read reproduces the Zarr slice it wraps.
- [ ] Keep it optional (earth2studio is a GPU-extra dependency) — import lazily, so the adapter is only needed where earth2studio is installed.

## Done when
The staged forcing/observation Zarrs are readable through the earth2studio DataSource interface, with a round-trip test, and documented in Appendix A.

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Split: static channel mask check now; dynamic surface water later.

**Audit verdict:** split (verifier corrected: The substance is right, but the verdict label is inconsistent with the proposed edit, which is a split: an agent-ready static HAND channel mask vs JRC GSW, plus a deferred dynamic VSA. 'Defer' would also defer the defensible static half. The title says Sentinel-2 optical while the body prefers SAR. Optical and C-band SAR cannot see saturation under the closed conifer canopy that dominates the domain, which supports deferring the dynamic part.)

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #109` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Split: (a) agent-ready static task, validating the HAND-derived channel/perennial-water mask against JRC GSW occurrence, with precision and recall by stream order; (b) defer the dynamic VSA work to the flood milestone (#199-#202), with a classification-likelihood operator. Fix the title.

### Problems found

- Dynamic VSA scoring is not defensible physics for this domain.
- The static HAND channel-mask check against JRC GSW is defensible and small.
- No milestone.

### Physics assessment

Physically overstated. Optical and SAR water masks detect OPEN water. Saturated variable-source-area soils under a closed conifer canopy are not open water and are largely invisible to S2 and to C-band S1. Storm-time inundation in channels and floodplains is dominated by routed streamflow and overbank flow, not groundwater outcrop. The score 'water table within S_y·d of surface' is dimensionally muddled: Sy·d is a storage deficit, not a depth. Binary inundation needs a classification likelihood, not a footprint average (science-review.md:59). The title says Sentinel-2 while the body prefers SAR, and the wet-season cloud cover makes the S2 premise weak.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

The observing-system design (`src/models/observability.py`, evaluation chapter) treats surface-water extent as a **spatial flux constraint** — it observes the **variable source area**, the valley floors and riparian corridors (HAND ≈ 0) where the water table outcrops and quickflow is generated. That is exactly the saturated-area runoff mechanism the water budget already models, and it is the *spatial* complement to the gauges: a gauge sees the basin-**integrated** discharge, surface-water extent shows **where** it is generated.

The observation **operator** is implemented (`channel_footprints`) and tested; the **data** is not yet fetched.

## Do
- [ ] Fetch a surface-water / inundation time series over the domain. Options: Sentinel-2 NDWI/MNDWI optical differencing (10 m, cloud-limited); the JRC Global Surface Water occurrence layer for the static channel mask; Sentinel-1 SAR water (all-weather, better in the PNW winter). Prefer SAR or a fused product for the cloudy wet season.
- [ ] Reduce to a per-date inundation mask on the analysis grid, with a cloud/valid mask.
- [ ] Two uses: (a) **static** — verify the HAND-derived channel network against observed perennial water; (b) **dynamic** — where the inundated area *expands* during a storm marks the saturated source area, a direct check on the saturated-area runoff term.
- [ ] Score: does modelled saturation (water table within `S_y·d` of the surface) coincide with observed surface water?

## Done when
An inundation product on the grid, the HAND channel mask validated against it, and the modelled variable source area scored against observed storm-time expansion.

</details>
title: Surface-water extent (Sentinel-2 optical) as a distributed flux / variable-source-area constraint

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Test whether snowmelt really sets the April water-table peak, without making it a calibration target.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite (blocker should be #70, not #137) (verifier corrected: The rewrite content is sound. v0.4 is DONE in ROADMAP.md:87 while #100 is open. Snow is SNOTEL-calibrated per the comments, so a leave-stations-out test is a fair new requirement. liquid_input starts SWE at zero on every run (forecast.py, swe=np.zeros), so SWE state is a real gap. But adding BLOCKED_BY 100:[137] inverts the issue's own ordering ('do D8 before or alongside D7, not after') and would delay the snow fix until after calibration. The phase residual depends on multi-year spin-up (#70), per the last comment.)

### Specification

Narrow it to snow: (1) a falsification test: stratify wells by elevation and snow fraction. If snow is the clock, rain-dominated low wells should peak earlier than snow-affected wells; (2) leave-stations-out SNOTEL validation of melt-out; (3) carry SWE as model state and initial condition. Move the WT-phase criterion to #137's held-out metrics.

### Problems found

- The acceptance criterion is a calibration target.
- Its milestone (v0.4) is declared done in ROADMAP (audit R4).
- The mechanism is untested.

### Physics assessment

The snow calibration is done (forecast.py:53-61, 28-30 SNOTEL stations, melt-out objective). The acceptance criterion (April well peak emerges) is not met (model peaks in month 5), and it cannot serve as validation, because peak month is inside the D7 objective (calibrate_fluxes.py:81-86). The 'snow is the clock' hypothesis is physically questionable for the observed wells. The 863 NWIS wells are largely lowland, below the seasonal snow zone, so their April peak is more plausibly aquifer and vadose response to winter rain. Domain-mean melt timing matching the well-ensemble peak month is a phase coincidence, not a mechanism test. The snow calibration was also evaluated on the stations it was fit to. Gap: SWE is not a carried state. liquid_input starts SWE = 0 on every call (forecast.py:123), so a forecast initialized mid-winter melts nothing.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #70, #234.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

**This is why the domain extension matters for the physics, not just for gauge coverage.**

## The finding
TerraClimate SWE over the Cascade-inclusive domain (2005–2024):

| | month |
|---|---|
| precipitation peaks | **November** |
| snowpack (SWE) peaks | February |
| **snowmelt release peaks** | **April** (141 mm) |
| **observed water-table peak** | **April** ✔ (26,816 shallow-well obs) |

**The snowpack — not the unsaturated zone — is what lags the water table.** It stores the November rain as snow and releases it in April. Snowmelt delivers **312 mm/yr, 20% of annual precipitation**, and it arrives in spring when rainfall is low and ET is still low, so an unusually large fraction becomes **recharge** rather than ET or quickflow.

This corrects my earlier diagnosis in #87 (which blamed unsaturated travel time — now demoted).

## Why the model cannot currently produce it
The degree-day snow module (`src.models.forecast.liquid_input` / `soil_moisture.snowmelt_liquid_input`) **exists and is never exercised**: the Puget-lowland domain is rain-dominated (Dec-2025 hindcast domain-mean T ≈ 7 °C → all rain). There is no snow reservoir to lag anything.

## Do (after D2 gives us Cascade terrain + elevation)
- [ ] Verify the snow module actually accumulates a pack over the extended domain (SWE seasonality vs TerraClimate/SNOTEL).
- [ ] **Calibrate the degree-day parameters** — `ddf` (3.0 mm/°C/day), `t_snow_hi/lo`, `t_melt` are all nominal and have never been fitted. Melt *timing* sets the water-table phase, so these now matter a great deal.
- [ ] Calibrate against **SNOTEL SWE** — we already ingest SNOTEL soil moisture; SWE is the gap (and was flagged as a roadmap item long ago).
- [ ] **Acceptance: the April water-table peak must emerge from snowmelt**, without inventing a vadose lag.
- [ ] Check the elevation dependence: PRISM is 4 km, and the rain/snow line is sharp. A 4 km cell straddling the snow line will smear the partition.

## Watch for
Snowmelt recharge is efficient (low ET, low rainfall competition), so getting melt timing wrong shifts the water-table peak **and** the magnitude. This directly interacts with D7's flux calibration — **do D8 before or alongside D7**, not after, or D7 will fit `Ka` and the river sink to compensate for missing snow.

</details>

milestone.title: v0.4 — Domain extension: western Cascades (gauged-basin coverage)
milestone.description:
[loop: Represent]

Extend the 90 m static domain to CONTAIN the gauged headwater basins, so the water-budget flux partition can be calibrated against river gauges across real terrain instead of one lowland creek.

WHY (measured, not assumed): the current static footprint is a Puget-lowland strip. Basin overlap:
  Nisqually 0% | Puyallup 0% | Green 0% | Skykomish 0% | Cedar 1.8% | Snoqualmie 17.3%
  Newaukum Ck 100% (79 km2) <- the ONLY fully-contained gauged basin
Running the budget on the lowland and comparing it to mountain discharge is meaningless (#91).
Worse, interflow (f_lat = Ka*tanB/(1+Ka*tanB)) is MOST active on steep ground -- exactly what a
lowland creek cannot constrain. So the one basin we can model is the one least able to calibrate
the parameter that matters.

TARGET GRID (measured as the union of the gauged basins + the current footprint, plus padding):
  bbox (EPSG:4326): -123.0, 46.6, -121.0, 48.2
  CRS EPSG:5070, 90 m  ->  ~1670 x 1980 = ~3.3 M cells (~2.8-3.6x current 0.92 M). Tractable.

Includes the Puyallup and Nisqually headwaters (Mt Rainier), Green, Cedar, Snoqualmie, Skykomish.

PHASE 2 (separate milestone): Stehekin / eastern Cascades -- across the crest, so rain-shadow and
snow-dominated. Different hydrology, not a bbox change; do not fold it in here.

BLOCKS: #88 (water table 8-26x too high), #90 (model BFI 0.00 vs observed 0.55). Both are flux-
partition errors and neither can be calibrated honestly until the gauged basins are in the domain.

title: D8: Snow is the water-table clock — calibrate the snow module and verify the April peak emerges

**In plain words:** After #100; scoping memo first.

**Audit verdict:** defer

### Specification

Add BLOCKED_BY 99:[100]. Update the body to reflect the existing SWE fetcher and calibration, and add the MRMS/PRISM orographic test. Rewrite acceptance as a scoping memo before any code.

### Problems found

- Its own gate says not before v0.4 closes; #100 is still open (roadmap-review.md:61-63), yet the queue dispatches #99 in batch 17.
- It is a scoping placeholder with no testable acceptance.

### Physics assessment

The physics framing is right: a 0.25° FuXi grid cannot resolve the crest rain shadow, and a snowmelt-dominated regime makes the degree-day module first-order. Partly stale: a SNOTEL SWE fetcher and SWE calibration now exist (src/data/fetch_snotel_swe.py, notebooks/calibrate_snow_swe.py). rainier3d S29 offers a PRISM-versus-MRMS orographic check (MRMS 169 mm below 500 m versus 547 mm above 3000 m; leverage README:39). Hydrogeologically the Stehekin basin is crystalline bedrock plus valley fill with very few wells, so the GWL side has nothing to validate against.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #100.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Placeholder to hold the scope. **Do not start before v0.4 is closed.**

Stehekin R at Stehekin (USGS **12451000**, ~321 km²) drains into Lake Chelan from the east side of the crest.

## Why this is not just a bigger bbox
- **Rain shadow.** Precipitation falls several-fold across ~50 km. FuXi's 0.25° (~28 km) grid **cannot see the crest**, so the AI forcing will be badly wrong here without orographic downscaling. PRISM (4 km) resolves it; the forecast does not. This turns the "orographic downscaling" item from a nicety into a blocker.
- **Snowmelt-driven.** The hydrograph peaks in **spring/summer melt**, not the western autumn/winter rain peak. The degree-day snow module becomes **first-order**, not a correction — and `ddf`, `t_snow`, and the melt timing have never been calibrated.
- The MVP window framing (Sep–Mar wet season) describes the *western* regime. For Stehekin the interesting window is the **melt season**.

## Do (when it starts)
- [ ] Confirm the flux partition calibrated on western basins (D7) and **re-validate** it here — do not assume it transfers from a rain-dominated to a snowmelt-dominated basin.
- [ ] Calibrate the snow module against SNOTEL SWE (we have SNOTEL soil moisture already; SWE is the gap).
- [ ] Quantify how badly the 0.25° forecast misses the rain shadow, against PRISM.

## Done when
Stehekin's snowmelt hydrograph is reproduced, and the western-calibrated parameters are shown either to transfer or (more likely) to need a regime-dependent treatment.

</details>

milestone.title: v0.5 — Eastern Cascades: Stehekin (rain shadow, snow-dominated)
milestone.description:
[loop: Represent]

Extend across the Cascade crest to Stehekin (Lake Chelan). DELIBERATELY A SEPARATE MILESTONE from v0.4: this is not a bigger bounding box, it is DIFFERENT HYDROLOGY, and folding it into the western extension would hide that.

What changes east of the crest:
  - RAIN SHADOW: precipitation drops several-fold over ~50 km. The 0.25 deg FuXi grid (~28 km) cannot
    resolve the crest at all, so the AI forcing will be badly wrong there without orographic
    downscaling. PRISM (4 km) captures it; the forecast does not.
  - SNOW-DOMINATED: Stehekin runoff is snowmelt-driven, with a spring/summer peak, not the western
    autumn-winter rain peak. The degree-day snow module becomes FIRST-ORDER rather than a correction,
    and the water-table seasonal phase (western: April peak) will differ.
  - The wet-season framing of the MVP window (Sep-Mar) does not describe this basin; the melt season
    does.

Prerequisites: v0.4 done and the flux partition calibrated on the western basins first. Calibrating
on a rain-dominated basin and applying to a snowmelt basin without re-validating is precisely the
class of error this project keeps catching.

> **Superseded 2026-10-18** by MODFLOW runs daily only; the monthly groundwater path is retired under the PI's decision to make MODFLOW 6 the groundwater core (plan `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-modflow-groundwater-core/plan.md`, PR #273; epic #274). Held from the agent queue by the `superseded` label. Closing is the PI's call after reviewing the replacement.

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Daily and monthly runs must agree (monthly = daily sub-steps) or the monthly path is retired.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Move to the 'Water budget' milestone. Scope: make dt_days required (no implicit monthly); implement monthly as daily sub-steps; add a timestep-convergence test (dt = 1, 0.25 d, and 30 d via sub-stepping) with recharge totals agreeing within 2%. Move the multi-year calibration to #137/#70, and the monthly SM product retirement to a needs-human-decision checkbox.

### Problems found

- It has no milestone, so it lands in queue batch 36 although it is a hard blocker of #187 (gaia_group_issues.py:87), as the system audit (line 93) notes.
- Mixed scope: the code-consistency work, data acquisition (now just a run), calibration (belongs in #137) and the product-retirement decision.
- 'Agree within a defensible tolerance' gives no number.

### Physics assessment

Reproduced: 455 mm in one month gives 90 mm of monthly recharge vs 432 mm daily (4.8x). Part of the issue is already done: D7 calibrated in daily mode (calibrate_fluxes.py:1-4, :68 dt_days=1.0), and fetch_prism_daily has a PRISM-service fallback covering any window (fetch_prism_daily.py:59-139). What remains: dt_days=None (monthly) is still the DEFAULT (water_budget.py:122,161-164), the tests run monthly (test_water_budget.py:28), and the shipped SM product uses monthly drain_frac (soil_moisture.py:158-187). The physically consistent fix is a single process timestep, with monthly output produced by daily sub-stepping. Exact agreement between lumped-monthly and daily is not the right target.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #70.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Uncovered while calibrating interflow (#88).

## The inconsistency
Same rain (455 mm), same parameters — **only the timestep differs**:

| | drainage out of root zone | water-table rise |
|---|---|---|
| monthly step | 87.6 mm | +0.46 m |
| **daily step** | **409.6 mm** | +1.97 m |

**The daily mode drains 4.7× more.**

Cause: monthly drains `drain_frac = 60%` of the **month-end** excess **once**; daily drains `1 - exp(-1/DRAIN_TAU_DAYS) ≈ 39%` **per day**, compounding, and re-evaluates the state every day.

## Why it matters
The **daily mode is the physically correct one** — gravity drainage above field capacity is a 1–3 day process, so over a month essentially all of it should leave. The monthly `drain_frac` is a lumped parameterisation that severely under-drains.

But the monthly mode is the one that **reproduces the observed well seasonal cycle** (amplitude 1.06 m, April peak). So the monthly fit is matching the wells **for the wrong reason**: it under-drains, accidentally compensating for missing attenuation (#87).

Consequence: **any calibration done in monthly mode is invalid for the daily mode we actually forecast in** — and we currently forecast daily.

## What is needed
1. **Calibrate in the mode we run** (daily). That needs multi-year *daily* forcing — the `gaia-hazlab/prism-stac` catalog currently holds only 2025-12-01..12-31. Extend `src/data/fetch_prism_daily.py` to pull multi-year daily PRISM directly from the PRISM service (as `fetch_prism_monthly` already does), so there is a real daily calibration record.
2. Decide whether the monthly path should be **retired** rather than kept as a second, inconsistent physics. Keeping two timesteps that disagree by 4.7× invites exactly this class of error.

## Done when
Daily and monthly runs of the same forcing agree within a defensible tolerance, or the monthly path is removed; and the reservoir parameters are calibrated in the daily mode against multi-year daily forcing.

</details>

Add a minimum held-out count per fold, decided from the #81 count. BLOCKED_BY 86:[81,84]; needs-human-decision until the pause lifts.

- Constraint space (slowness vs velocity) unspecified
- Internal contradiction with the bias-correcting siblings
- Depends on #81 and #84; the queue runs it in batch 14 before #81
- Under the user pause

### Physics assessment

The architecture is sound: predict profile parameters rather than Vs30, residuals from the prior, no lat/lon, block CV against measured profiles, a negative result allowed. Three physics gaps. (1) Vs30 is a harmonic (travel-time) quantity, so the block constraint must preserve the mean slowness (1/Vs30, or equivalently 200 m block travel time), not arithmetic Vs30; an arithmetic mean-preserving redistribution biases the block high. (2) Strict SVM block-mean preservation contradicts #83/#85 and the issue's own (b): if the SVM is biased (e.g., ignores shallow stiff units), the constraint forbids the correction measured profiles would justify. Split into a mean-preserving redistribution step and a separately validated block-bias correction. (3) With 649 profiles PNW-wide and probably tens in the pilot, block-CV skill estimates will be very noisy; a power analysis is needed before (b) is meaningful.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #81, #84.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

The machinery that ties the milestone together — and the guardrail that keeps it honest.

## The non-negotiable constraint
**Downscaling cannot create information.** The 200 m block mean of the densified field MUST reproduce the SVM (area-to-point / dissever style). We only redistribute *within* a block; we never contradict the source. Where the covariates say nothing, the result must fall back to the SVM **exactly**.

## Architecture
- Predict the **Vs(z) profile parameters** (surface velocity, depth-gradient exponent) from the covariates, stratified by geologic unit (#84), then integrate with `vs30_surface_referenced` — **do not regress Vs30 directly** (that breaks the travel-time definition).
- Predict the **residual from the SVM prior**, not the absolute value.
- Terrain (10 m 3DEP slope, curvature, HAND, TWI, geomorphons, distance-to-channel) enters only as a **residual** predictor — it is a proxy, it does not *cause* Vs.

## Guardrails
- [ ] **No lat/lon predictors** (Stage-1 critique: the model just memorizes location).
- [ ] Spatial **block CV** (`src/evaluation/cross_validate.py`), scored against held-out measured profiles (#81) — never against the SVM raster.
- [ ] Regularise: 649 profiles PNW-wide is sparse relative to the covariate count. Overfitting is the default outcome unless actively prevented.
- [ ] Emit a **downscaling uncertainty** term into the existing uncertainty budget; the densified Vs30 must not claim tighter sigma than the data support.
- [ ] Keep delivering **NEHRP site-class probability**, not a point Vs30 — the 200 m native resolution is a real limit and the product should say so.

## Done when
The densified 90 m Vs30 (a) reproduces the SVM under 200 m block averaging to within tolerance, (b) beats the plain upsampled SVM against held-out measured profiles under block CV, and (c) ships a defensible downscaling sigma. **If (b) fails, we report that and keep the SVM** — a negative result is a valid outcome here.

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Paused; geology classes by age and genesis.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Do: a separate vs_geology_crosswalk.json keyed on age and genesis (artificial fill, Holocene alluvium, peat/organic, tideflat/estuarine, Vashon recessional outwash, Vashon till, advance outwash, pre-Fraser, bedrock), from 1:24K where available and otherwise 1:100K, with a fractional-cover raster at 90 m rather than a majority class. Acceptance as written (per-unit counts, explicit SVM-prior fallback). BLOCKED_BY [81]; keep paused.

### Problems found

- Relies on a crosswalk that destroys the needed classes
- Overstates map scale
- Depends on #81 counts per unit; under the pause

### Physics assessment

The best-founded issue in the milestone. Glacial overconsolidation (Vashon till/outwash about 400-600+ m/s vs Holocene alluvium/fill/peat about 150-250 m/s) is the first-order Puget Vs control, and stratifying by unit rather than regressing is correct. Two factual errors. (1) The 'existing lithology crosswalk' maps to 4 hydrogeologic classes (0 unconsolidated / 1 fractured bedrock / 2 young volcanic / 3 CRBG; rasterize_geology.py:10-12), which merges Holocene and Vashon units, the exact distinction needed. A new age-plus-genesis crosswalk is required. (2) The shipped source is DNR 1:100K (rasterize_geology.py:7), not 1:24,000, and rasterizing to 90 m discards the 10-30 m signal the issue values.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #81.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

**The covariate with the most unused fine-scale information.**

## Why
In the Puget Lowland the dominant Vs control is not texture — it is **glacial overconsolidation**. Vashon till and outwash were loaded under ~1 km of ice, so they are overconsolidated and stiff (Vs30 ~400–600+), while Holocene alluvium, tideflat deposits, peat, and artificial fill are normally consolidated and soft (~150–250).

The SVM collapses this into **four Holocene provinces**. WA DNR 1:24,000 surficial geology resolves it at effectively 10–30 m — far finer than the SVM's 200 m grid. This is where the real sub-200 m signal lives.

## Do
- [ ] Rasterise WA DNR surficial geology through the existing lithology crosswalk (a local rasterizer already shipped).
- [ ] Treat the geologic unit as a **stratifying factor** — a distinct Vs(z) profile per unit — **not** a continuous predictor.
- [ ] Key on *age + genesis* (Holocene alluvium / fill / peat / tideflat vs Vashon till / outwash vs pre-Fraser vs bedrock), since that is what encodes consolidation history.
- [ ] Fit each unit's profile against the measured profiles (#81), with the SVM province profile as the prior for units with too few observations.

## Done when
Per-unit Vs(z) profiles are fitted with observation counts reported per unit, and units with insufficient data fall back to the SVM prior explicitly (never a fabricated profile).

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Paused; use soft-sediment thickness, not soil restrictive depth.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Restate h as soft-sediment (Holocene + soft Pleistocene) thickness over the stiff unit, from geology/boring compilations or the SVM/CVM layer interface, never SOLUS restrictive depth. Restrict scope to thin-regolith terrain. Add a regression test that h >= 30 gives the identical result, and a test rejecting h taken from a variable capped at about 2 m. Keep under the pause; BLOCKED_BY [81].

### Problems found

- Wrong thickness variable (pedologic restriction ≠ soft-sediment thickness)
- No-op in the liquefaction region
- Acceptance 'beats plain SVM against #81' depends on #81, which is paused
- The CVM below the SVM may already encode the soil/rock transition, risking double-counting

### Physics assessment

The formula is correct (harmonic travel time, exact reduction for h >= 30), but the proposed h is wrong. SOLUS resdept/anylithicdpt is a pedologic restrictive depth of about 2 m or less (often dense Vashon lodgement till, about 400-600 m/s, not rock). Using it as h with CVM rock Vs below would put about 28 m of 'rock' under most columns and bias Vs30 strongly high. In the Puget Lowland, glacial/Quaternary sediment is tens to over 1000 m thick, so h >= 30 almost everywhere liquefaction matters; the model is a no-op there and helps only in thin-regolith Cascade uplands (site amplification, not liquefaction). The 'single biggest structural win' claim is unsupported for the hazard this family targets. GAIA dtb (fetch_gaia.py:415-425) is of unknown provenance and accuracy in deep basins.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #81.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

**The single biggest structural win, and it needs no new statistics.**

## Why
Vs30 is a travel-time average over *exactly* 30 m. If the soil column is only 8 m thick over rock, the average is dominated by rock and Vs30 jumps. This is a **geometric** control that explains a large share of Vs30 residuals — and it should be encoded as physics, not fitted as a regression term.

$$V_{S30} = 30 \Big/ \left(\frac{h}{V_{S,\text{soil}}} + \frac{30-h}{V_{S,\text{rock}}}\right), \qquad h < 30$$

## Do
- [ ] Use SOLUS depth-to-restrictive-layer (100 m) + our depth-to-bedrock layer for $h$ (both finer than the SVM's 200 m).
- [ ] Reconcile the two thickness sources; they will disagree — document which wins where, and carry the disagreement as uncertainty.
- [ ] Apply the two-layer travel time through the existing integrator rather than a new one.
- [ ] Sanity-check: where $h \ge 30$ the model must reduce **exactly** to the plain soil profile (regression test).

## Watch for
Rock Vs is itself uncertain and lithology-dependent — take it from the CVM below the soil, not a constant.

## Done when
A thickness-aware Vs30 exists, reduces exactly to the soil-only case for $h\ge30$, and its residual against measured profiles (#81) beats the plain SVM.

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Paused; after #81.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Retitle 'Assess SOLUS bulk density/SOC as Vs residual covariates'. Do: void ratio from dbovendry with a theta_sat cross-check; explanatory power for measured-profile residuals (#81) under block CV, not the SVM residual; state the 2 m sampling-depth limit up front. Keep under the pause; BLOCKED_BY [81].

### Problems found

- Fetch already done
- Scoring target is circular (residual vs SVM)
- Under the v0.3 pause

### Physics assessment

The fetch is done: dbovendry, soc, resdept_all_cm and anylithicdpt_cm are in src/data/fetch_solus_domain.py:16-58 (via the closed #94; roadmap-review:79 calls #82 stale). The physics claim is overstated. SOLUS samples only the top ~1-2 m (point depths 0-100 cm, fetch_solus_domain.py:27-28). A 2 m cap at 120 m/s over 250 m/s lowers Vs30 by only about 7% (30/(2/120+28/250) = 233 vs 250 m/s). The thick (5-15 m) Duwamish/Kent-valley peat and organic tideflat deposits that produce the NEHRP E tail are invisible to SOLUS and come from geology (#84). 'Residual variance vs the SVM' is the circular target #81/#86 forbid.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #81.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

We currently fetch only `clay_pct` and `sand_pct` from SOLUS100 (see `data/processed/solus100_wa.zarr`). **Texture is a weak, second-order handle on Vs.** The properties that actually drive stiffness are unfetched.

## Physics
$V_S=\sqrt{\mu/\rho}$, and Hertz-Mindlin gives $\mu \propto \sigma'^{1/3}$ modulated by **void ratio**. So:

- **Dry bulk density** → enters $\rho$ directly *and* enters $\mu$ steeply via void ratio $e=\phi/(1-\phi)$. (We already derive `theta_sat` ≈ porosity in the hydraulic envelope but never use it for stiffness.)
- **Organic carbon / peat** → peat and organic tideflat soils run below ~120–150 m/s. Because travel-time averaging is harmonic-like, a *thin* slow cap disproportionately drags Vs30 down. This is what generates the NEHRP **E tail** (2% of the pilot) and the worst settlement/liquefaction — and it is currently invisible to us.
- **Depth to restrictive layer (soil thickness)** → feeds the two-layer model (separate issue).

## Do
- [ ] Extend the SOLUS fetcher with bulk density, organic carbon/SOM, and depth-to-restrictive-layer (verify the exact SOLUS variable names from the product docs — do not guess).
- [ ] Derive void ratio from bulk density (and cross-check against the `theta_sat` already in the envelope).
- [ ] Quantify: how much of the **Vs30 residual variance vs the SVM** do these explain? Report honestly if the answer is "little" — that is a real result and would redirect effort to geology/thickness.

## Done when
The new covariates are on the 90 m grid with provenance, and their explanatory power for the SVM Vs30 residual is reported.

</details>

**In plain words:** Paused (v0.3). When resumed, measured Vs profiles go first.

**Audit verdict:** hold-human

### Specification

Add the needs-human-decision label (pause). Add: a profile-independence flag (in SVM training set: yes/no); a depth_max < 30 m extrapolation rule with sigma; report the in-pilot count split by geologic unit (feeds #84). In the grouper, BLOCKED_BY 82/83/84/86:[81].

- The queue runs it LAST in the milestone (batch 15) after #83-#86 (batch 14), the inversion flagged in soil-twin-system-audit:92
- Data acquisition needs human contact/agreements

### Physics assessment

This is the right gate: scoring against the SVM is circular. It has gaps. (1) The 649 profiles are the SVM's own training data (fetch_vs30.py:5-8), so comparing 'SVM vs densified' on them flatters the SVM, though only a little since it is province-averaged; independent profiles not used by Grant et al., or SVM refits with blocks left out, are needed. (2) Many MASW/ReMi profiles end shallower than 30 m; vs30_from_vs_profile returns NaN when not covered, so the issue must specify a Vs30-from-Vsz extrapolation (Boore 2004 / Boore et al. 2011) with its added sigma, or most profiles drop. (3) Obtaining data from authors/WSDOT is a human task.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

**This gates every other issue in the milestone.** Without independent point Vs data we cannot claim improved resolution — only a physically-plausible redistribution, and the report must say exactly that.

## Why
Scoring a densified Vs30 against the SVM raster is **circular**: it measures how well we memorized the thing we are trying to refine. The only honest target is measured Vs(z) profiles.

## Do
- [ ] Obtain the **649 measured profiles** behind the SVM (Grant, Wirth & Stone 2025, doi:10.26443/seismica.v4i2.1672) — ask the authors / check the Seismica supplement and the USGS release.
- [ ] Add other PNW point Vs: USGS shallow-seismic profile compilations (OFR series), NGA-West2 site database, WSDOT borings, university MASW/ReMi campaigns.
- [ ] Normalise to a single table: `lat, lon, vs30_measured, method, depth_max, profile_id, source, quality`.
- [ ] Compute Vs30 from each profile with `src.data.fetch_vs30.vs30_from_vs_profile` (do NOT trust a published Vs30 column — recompute the travel-time average, and record where they disagree).
- [ ] Hold out a spatial block test set (reuse `src/evaluation/cross_validate.py` block CV).

## Caution
649 profiles across the whole PNW is **sparse**. Report how many fall inside the Puget pilot footprint before committing to a covariate-heavy model — this number decides how ambitious the statistics can be.

## Done when
A `data/processed/vs_profiles.parquet` exists with recomputed Vs30, provenance, and a documented block-CV split; the count inside the pilot footprint is reported.

</details>

The principle is sound: PRISM for forcing, ERA5-Land only for validation, forecast the antecedent state not the hydrograph. The roster is stale. It names GraphCast/ACE2 (#71) although the code makes FuXi the only viable precipitation model (src/data/fetch_earth2studio.py:54-63). It omits #136 (actually running FuXi), #191/#195 (ensemble forecast and verification) and #200 (flood source terms).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

The coupled reanalysis (GWL + soil moisture + stiffness, closed water budget, dv/v) is built. The next phase drives it from **rainfall forcing** and completes the **downstream handoff** so it feeds flood/landslide/liquefaction models. This epic sequences the concrete issues.

## 1. Rainfall forcing (the headline next step)
- **#70** — Hindcast forcing from **PRISM rainfall** (preferred, gauge-anchored source).
- **#71** — Forward forcing from **GraphCast / ACE2** QPF (earth2studio) with **90 m precipitation downscaling** → antecedent-state ensemble.
- Supporting: #56 (forcing-interface table), #57 (daily/hourly bucket), #58 (Penman-Monteith PET), #55 (antecedent-state reframe), #39 (Earth2Studio scope), #31 (model-driven downscaler), #32 (forcing ensemble).

## 2. Independent cross-validation
- **#72** — **ERA5-Land** cross-check (upscale-then-compare; optional/secondary).
- Supporting: #29 (SMAP/NISAR/NLDAS/GRACE native-scale), #59 (AR-event hindcast).

## 3. Downstream handoff
- **#64** — LandLab dynamic export wired to real products (+ σ + mask) — *done in principle; operationalize*.
- **#65** — Publish the LandLab bundle as COG/Zarr + STAC.
- **#12** — LandLab / geotech bridge coordination.

## Principle
PRISM is the preferred **forcing** rainfall; ERA5-Land is **validation only**. Forecasts produce the **antecedent state**, not the flood hydrograph (surface routing is a separate model). Every downscaled field records native-vs-delivered resolution (footprint-leakage guard).

See the technical report's Roadmap and the July-2026 status update in the audit framework.

---

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Becomes the meteorological ensemble source (with #241).

**Audit verdict:** rewrite (repurpose #71 in place as the meteorological member-source / FuXi-ensemble issue, BLOCKED_BY 187 and 136) (verifier corrected: Partly wrong premise. The code does not exclude all the prescribed models: GraphCastSmall is still an allowed --model choice (fetch_earth2studio.py:54,185); only GraphCastOperational and ACE2 are excluded (lines 61-63). The ACE2 exclusion rests on a code comment claiming ACE2 emits no precipitation, which is questionable and unverified (ACE2 has a surface precipitation-rate output). No open issue covers the residual scope: an ensemble, by-lead QPF member source and a 90 m orographic downscaler. #136 only bias-corrects totals against PRISM climatology. The audit itself has to invent two new issues to cover it. #187 ('Provides the interface for ... #71'), #191 ('Builds on #71/#73') and #203 all link to #71, so closing it orphans those links. Rewriting #71 as the R8 member-source task (how members are obtained, P/T dependence, the reforecast archive for calibration, ensemble size and compute) is cheaper and keeps the graph intact. Either way it must leave queue batch 19 until #187 and #136 land.)

### Specification

Close as superseded by #136 (FuXi execution and bias correction), #191 (ensemble propagation) and two new gap issues: the meteorological member source, and a mass-conserving orographic precipitation downscaler. Move the honest-scope sentence (antecedent state, not hydrograph) into #73.

### Problems found

- The prescribed models are already excluded by the code.
- Its remaining real content duplicates #136 (run plus bias correction) and #191 (ensemble propagation); roadmap-review R9 lists the #71/#136 overlap.
- The queue dispatches it in batch 19, before #136 (batch 20) and #70 (batch 39), and before the #187 contract it is meant to feed (#187 body: 'Provides the interface for ... #71').

### Physics assessment

The model choice is wrong. GraphCastOperational emits tp06 as zeros (fetch_earth2studio.py:9-13, 63). GraphCastSmall runs at 1 degree, which removes orographic enhancement entirely. ACE2 is a climate emulator with no deterministic skill at days 1-15. The repo's own note that ACE2 emits no precipitation (line 61) is itself doubtful, since ACE2-ERA5 predicts a precipitation rate; this should be verified.

Filing the precipitation downscaler under the #31 registry is a category error. That registry (src/models/downscale.py:102-226) downscales state fields using soil/terrain covariates. Precipitation downscaling must conserve the coarse-cell total and use PRISM climatology or orographic physics.

Bias-correcting against PRISM 'climatology' needs a multi-year reforecast archive stratified by lead time. One season of FuXi runs cannot calibrate quantile mapping.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Drive the same water budget **forward** with AI weather forecasts to produce a forecast antecedent hydrologic state (water table / soil moisture / saturation) for the liquefaction and landslide chains.

## Tasks
- [ ] Ingest quantitative precip forecast (QPF) from **GraphCast** and/or **ACE2** via [earth2studio](https://github.com/NVIDIA/earth2studio) (ensemble lead times).
- [ ] **Downscale precipitation to the 90 m analysis grid** with orographic physics (the ~25 km → 90 m step; bilinear loses the Cascade AR enhancement) — register as a downscaler in the modular registry (#31).
- [ ] Bias-correct the AI-model QPF against PRISM climatology.
- [ ] Run `coupled_water_budget` forward over the ensemble → forecast GWL/θ/saturation/recharge with spread; hand off via `landlab_export` (#64).
- [ ] Keep scope honest: this forecasts the **antecedent state**, not the flood hydrograph — surface routing is a separate model (#55).

Relates: #39 (Earth2Studio scope), #55 (antecedent-state reframe), #56 (forcing interface), #31 (downscaler), #64 (LandLab export).

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Twenty years of daily PRISM rainfall and a spin-up test for the model.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Retitle: 'Multi-year daily PRISM forcing record + spin-up protocol for the coupled budget'. Acceptance: a versioned Zarr for WY2005-2025 on the domain grid with checksums; a documented PRISM day convention; a spin-up test where the table's state at the end of each repeated spin-up cycle changes by less than 1 cm/yr; a TerraClimate-vs-PRISM comparison kept as the forcing-spread item (#32). Move to the 'Water budget' milestone so it runs first.

### Problems found

- As written it is the old monthly/TerraClimate framing.
- It is unmilestoned and sits last in the queue (batch 39), although it is upstream of #137.

### Physics assessment

Mostly done. Daily PRISM with Hargreaves-Samani PET exists (fetch_prism_daily.py), and D7 is forced by it (calibrate_fluxes.py:48). The real missing deliverable, and the one the whole family needs, is a MULTI-YEAR daily record (e.g. WY2005-2025) with a spin-up protocol. #89, #100 (the phase residual is attributed to spin-up), #131, #137 and #175 all need it. Physics notes: PRISM 'days' end at 12 UTC, so a half-day offset matters for daily lag validation. PRISM is 4 km and undercatches mountain snow.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Force the closed pixel-wise water budget (`src/models/water_budget.py`) with **observed rainfall from PRISM** — the preferred rainfall source over reanalysis (ERA5-Land) for the PNW because it is gauge-anchored. `src/data/fetch_prism_monthly.py` already stages monthly PRISM; extend to the cadence the budget needs.

## Tasks
- [ ] Fetch PRISM precipitation (monthly now; daily where the event/AR resolution needs it) over the pilot, aligned to the analysis grid.
- [ ] Wire PRISM P (+ PET) as the `liquid_in`/`pet` forcing to `coupled_water_budget`, replacing/augmenting the TerraClimate driver in the hindcast path.
- [ ] Produce a hindcast GWL/θ/saturation/recharge time series and compare against the TerraClimate-forced run (forcing-ensemble spread, ties to #32).
- [ ] Document PRISM as the preferred rainfall source; ERA5-Land is cross-validation only (#ERA5).

Relates: #56 (forcing-interface table), #57 (daily bucket), #58 (PET), #59 (AR-event hindcast), #32 (forcing ensemble).

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Named atmospheric-river event outside the calibration window.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Milestone v0.7, priority P1.

Specify:
- A named AR event outside the calibration period.
- Daily PRISM forcing.
- Continuous well recorders plus SNOTEL/USCRN probes at their sensor depths.
- Metrics: onset and peak lag (days), peak magnitude bias, and recession tau, against an open-loop baseline.
- Report the instantaneous-recharge timing bias explicitly.

Add #89, #172 and #70 to BLOCKED_BY.

### Problems found

- No event is named, no metric (peak-timing error, peak-rise bias, recession time constant) and no pass threshold.
- No holdout rule.
- Unmilestoned P2 although it gates forecast claims (roadmap-review R9).
- Queued in batch 31, after #71/#58 (batch 19), which it is supposed to gate.
- Should be driven by daily PRISM (#70), which runs in batch 39.

### Physics assessment

This is the right gate: monthly correlations say nothing about how fast storms register in wells and probes. But the current model applies recharge to the water table instantly (forecast.py docstring, 'Known limitation'), so modeled well timing is early by design.

Without the daily storage fixes (#89, a 4.7x drainage difference between daily and monthly; #172, capillary-rise conservation), the hindcast would score known bugs. The event must not be inside the D7/daily calibration window, or the result is calibration posing as validation. The Nov 11-15 2021 Skagit/Nooksack AR sequence is a natural candidate if it is outside that window.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

All skill numbers are monthly correlation. Add a hindcast of one named PNW AR sequence showing modeled vs observed well/theta response and timing error, as the gating deliverable for any forecast-forcing claim. See `docs/peer_review.md` for the full reviews.

body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Deferred; on hold.

**Audit verdict:** defer

### Specification

Remove it from the v0.7 milestone; label P2/deferred.

Rewrite:
- Hindcast PM from ERA5-Land Rn, u10 (converted to u2 with the FAO-56 log profile, Eq. 47) and d2m.
- Forecast PM only if a radiation source is chosen; otherwise Hargreaves-Samani with daily Tmax/Tmin taken from 6-hourly t2m. Four samples per day bias the diurnal range low, so report that bias.
- A canopy coefficient for forest.
- Mandatory recalibration of the bucket.

Acceptance: a lead-0 continuity test, so that hindcast and forecast PET agree within X% on overlapping days.

### Problems found

- Queued in batch 19 as if ready, although the body calls it a later-stage enhancement and roadmap-review R8 calls it optional.
- Has no test of lead-0 continuity and no recalibration requirement.
- The forecast path has no PET at all yet: FuXi supplies only tmean (fetch_earth2studio.py:154-163), so even Hargreaves-Samani (which needs Tmax/Tmin) is undefined in forecast mode.
- Stale 'PET (Hamon)' text remains in src/models/forecast.py:12 and src/data/stage_mvp_window.py:9.

### Physics assessment

FAO-56 Penman-Monteith reference ET is the right formula, but the plan to source it does not work.
- FuXi (the preferred model) and GraphCast output t2m, u10/v10, msl and tp. They output no surface shortwave or longwave radiation, and FuXi gives humidity only on pressure levels.
- So 'use AI-model radiation/humidity/wind' is not possible for the forecast path. Rn would come from ERA5-Land (ssrd/strd, d2m), which works for hindcasts only, or from a radiation diagnostic.
- Reference ET0 is for a short-grass reference. Forested Cascade cells need a crop or canopy coefficient and a separate interception term, otherwise the result is no more physical than Hargreaves-Samani.
- Switching PET formula invalidates the existing bucket calibration and creates a step change at the hindcast-to-forecast transition (lead 0).
- TerraClimate PET is already Penman-Monteith-type.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Land-surface-modeling review confirms full **FAO-56 Penman-Monteith reference ET** is the preferred
formulation — this is also what the group's own agroseismology paper uses
([Shi et al. 2026, *Science* 392(6795):306-310](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aec0970), Eq. S9),
not a temperature-only proxy.

PET in this repo currently has two paths, neither of which is full Penman-Monteith:

- **TerraClimate path** (`fetch_terraclimate.py`) — takes TerraClimate's own `pet` product, which
  TerraClimate computes internally via a Penman-Monteith-type reference ET (Abatzoglou et al. 2018).
  Fine as an external product, but we don't control or verify its inputs.
- **PRISM path** (`fetch_prism_monthly.py` / `fetch_prism_daily.py`) — as of the Hargreaves-Samani
  fix (superseding the earlier Hamon implementation), computes ET from Tmax/Tmin/Tmean + latitude
  only. Hargreaves-Samani is FAO-56's own recommended substitute *when radiation, wind, and humidity
  are not measured* (Allen et al. 1998, Ch. 3) — a real improvement over Hamon, but still not full
  Penman-Monteith, because PRISM does not carry net radiation, soil heat flux, wind speed, or vapor
  pressure deficit.

## What's needed to swap in real Penman-Monteith

FAO-56 Eq. 6: `ET0 = [0.408*Δ*(Rn-G) + γ*(900/(T+273))*u2*(es-ea)] / [Δ + γ*(1+0.34*u2)]`
(daily form; see Shi et al. 2026 Eq. S9 for the sub-daily variant). Needs, gridded over the domain:

- [ ] **Net radiation** (Rn) — shortwave + longwave, or a proxy (cloud cover + solar angle) if direct
      radiation isn't available.
- [ ] **Wind speed** (u2, 2 m) — currently not ingested from any source.
- [ ] **Humidity / vapor pressure deficit** (es, ea) — currently not ingested from any source.
- [ ] **Soil heat flux** (G) — usually approximated as ~0 at daily timestep (FAO-56 convention);
      likely not a new data-ingestion item, just a modeling choice to make explicit.

Candidate sources for the three real gaps (radiation, wind, humidity), in rough order of fit:

1. **AI weather models via [earth2studio](https://github.com/NVIDIA/earth2studio)** (GraphCast/ACE2/
   StormCast) — already the target forcing interface for the forward-forecast path (#71), and these
   models output radiation/humidity/wind alongside precipitation, so this is the natural place to
   pick them up rather than a separate ingestion path.
2. **ERA5-Land reanalysis** — already used as an independent cross-check (#72); could double as a
   real-input source for hindcast-mode Penman-Monteith if AI-model fields aren't wanted for the
   observed/hindcast path.
3. A dedicated **met-station network** (e.g. AgWeatherNet, RAWS) if point-anchored radiation/wind/
   humidity is preferred over gridded reanalysis for the observed path — unexplored, flagging as an
   option rather than a plan.

## Scope / sequencing

This is a **later-stage enhancement**, not a blocker: Hargreaves-Samani is an honest, FAO-56-endorsed
stand-in for now. This naturally follows the forward-forcing work in #71 (which already needs an
earth2studio ingestion path for AI-model fields) — do the radiation/wind/humidity ingestion as an
extension of that same pipeline rather than a separate one, then swap PRISM's/the daily budget's PET
call from `hargreaves_samani_pet_mm`/`hargreaves_samani_pet_per_day_mm` to a new
`penman_monteith_pet_mm`, keeping Hargreaves-Samani as the fallback when the new inputs aren't
available for a given window (e.g. hindcast periods before an AI-model archive starts).

Relates: #71 (forward AI forcing), #72 (ERA5-Land cross-check), #39 (Earth2Studio scope). See
`docs/peer_review.md` §3.6 for the original review that flagged this.


</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Shrinks to rainfall-intensity (infiltration-excess) runoff on burned or impervious ground; moved to v0.6.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite-then-defer (verifier corrected: The claim 'already-daily bucket' is only half true. coupled_water_budget is daily-capable, but the SHIPPED 90 m SM product still uses the monthly-only total_water_bucket (soil_moisture.py:162-200, :292, :452), with no dt argument. So the daily-derivation residual is not done; it depends on the #177 m2 product decision. Restricting Hortonian runoff to burned/impervious cells is physically defensible, because PNW forest Ksat of 15-55 mm/hr exceeds typical AR rates (water_budget.py:41-44). Moving beta4 (the Stage-2 AR regression term, climate_response.py:12-13) to #8 (aquifer-type tau) is a mismatch. It belongs with the TFN work (#23) or AR validation (#59).)

### Specification

Close the daily-derivation part. Retitle the remainder 'sub-daily infiltration-excess for burned/impervious cells' and move it to v0.6 (wildfire disturbance). Move beta4 to #8.

### Problems found

- The body is stale. An agent would 're-derive' an already-daily bucket.
- It is mixed with Stage-2 beta4.

### Physics assessment

The daily derivation is done (water_budget.py:160-172, with drain_tau, cap and recession rates converted per step), and TFN is #23/#8. What remains is sub-daily infiltration-excess. That is physically minor in forested PNW soils: Ksat is 15-55 mm/hr (water_budget.py:41-44) against typical AR hourly intensities of about 5-15 mm/hr. It matters for burned (hydrophobic) or impervious surfaces. beta4 belongs to the statistical Stage-2 model.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

The monthly Thornthwaite-Mather bucket (monthly drainage/degree-day closures) cannot represent sub-daily flood forcing; re-derive at daily/hourly resolution with recomputed closures. Populate the AR term (beta4=0 today) or the TFN recharge kernel (Rung 2) so atmospheric rivers actually drive GWL. See `docs/peer_review.md` for the full reviews.

</details>

body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Effective stress with depth per geologic unit, drained or undrained response, and snow load.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Retitle: 'Saturated-branch parameters per hydrostratigraphic unit: σ'(z), the head variable sampled, and drained vs undrained loading'. Tasks: within the #198 operator, derive ΔVs/Vs(z) = n_HM·Δσ'(z)/σ'(z) with Δσ' = γ_w·Δh for a phreatic or confined head, add a loading term with B for surface loads, and give per-unit priors for the exponent and the unit boundaries. Use Sy/S only in the head↔storage conversion. AC: analytic check that the drained and confined cases give equal Δσ' per metre of head; a band-dependent sensitivity table; a unit-boundary test. Block on #198a. Remove 'Sy vs S' from the title.

### Problems found

- The physics premise (the Sy-vs-S partition controls dv/v per unit head) is wrong.
- 'Borehole calibration' needs co-located wells and seismic stations, a human data question; it is also a calibration target that must not double as validation.
- It belongs in the saturated branch of #198, not as a standalone scalar per unit.
- The Rainier leverage review (README:44,92) proposes using rainier3d hydrostratigraphy here, but its thresholds are m1_placeholder.

### Physics assessment

The physics is mis-framed. The dv/v-to-head sensitivity is set by Δσ'/Δh and the stress sensitivity of Vs at the depths the kernel samples. A drained water-table move and a confined head change both give |Δσ'| ≈ γ_w·Δh at the sampled depth (total stress is roughly constant in the confined case). Specific yield vs storativity (Sy ~0.1-0.3 vs S ~1e-5 to 1e-3) does not set dv/v per metre of head. It sets head per unit stored water, which matters when converting to storage or the water budget. Skempton B and undrained response matter for loading signals (rain, snow, barometric), where total stress changes and pore pressure follows only partly. The genuine 1-2 order variation in k_sat comes from depth and σ'(z): the probe gives 3e-4 to 2.8e-3 per metre across bands for a water table at 5 m. The body's '1-2 orders between drained unconfined and undrained confined' is attributed to the wrong cause. The #198 comment already requires that each band state which head it sees.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #198.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

dvv_to_wtd_change divides dv/v by a single scalar K_SAT=5e-4. The dv/v -> Delta-head sensitivity differs 1-2 orders between drained unconfined (specific yield) and undrained confined (storativity, Skempton B) responses. Make k_sat per-unit with an explicit Sy-vs-S partition and borehole calibration. See `docs/peer_review.md` for the full reviews.

</details>
title: Saturated-branch parameters per hydrostratigraphic unit: effective stress with depth, head sampled, drained vs undrained loading

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Show what each frequency band actually resolves, framed as a kernel-weighted integral over the vadose column (4-8 Hz senses the vadose zone).

> **PI note (2026-10-08):** dv/v sensitivity is band-dependent and never zero at shallow depth; 4-8 Hz senses the vadose zone (Illien et al., 2021). Frame this as what each observed band integrates over the vadose column, computed from kernels on a layered Vs0(z) (#247), not as 'seismic cannot see the vadose zone'.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Retitle: 'S_THETA=-1.0 on the depth-inverted shallow mean is unjustified: the 0.1-4 Hz inversion does not resolve the vadose zone'. Body: cite the probe numbers. Tasks: compute the resolution (averaging-kernel) matrix of invert_depth_profile for the default bands, which observability.averaging_kernel pattern can be reused for; report the recovered fraction and the deep leakage for the 'shallow' partition; correct the docstring at dvv.py:59-65; either restore S_THETA_BAND on that path or label the shallow partition non-identifiable. AC: a test asserting that recovered/true for a top-5 m perturbation is below 0.1 and that deep leakage is reported, and a docstring that matches the test. Close it once #198a retires the scalar gains.

### Problems found

- The original scope is done but the issue was not closed; the follow-on change partially regressed it on the basis of an unverified resolution claim.
- tests/test_dvv.py:73 checks only the magnitude of S_THETA_BAND; no test checks the inverted-profile path that S_THETA=-1.0 is meant to serve.
- It is batched in batch 28 with three unrelated dv/v issues.

### Physics assessment

The original bug was fixed in PR #61 (S_THETA → -0.08, comment 2026-07-07), and the Sept audit (roadmap-review.md:75) notes it is still open. Main has since changed the convention: S_THETA = S_MATERIAL_THETA = -1.0, applied to the depth-inverted shallow mean, with S_THETA_BAND=-0.08 kept for raw bands (dvv.py:54-69,81-93). That justification is physically false for this band set. In the probe with the repo's own kernels (Vs30=400 m/s, 4 bands), the shallowest node is 5 m, with nothing in the θ-active top 1 m. A -5% velocity change in the top 5 m yields inverted soil_moisture_dvv = -0.043%, about 1% recovery. A -5% change confined below 30 m leaks -3.5% into the 'shallow' mean. Dividing that mean by -1.0 therefore underestimates Δθ by roughly 100x and contaminates it with deep signal. The probe also gives the material sensitivity as -0.3 to -5.3 per unit θ across texture and θ, so -1.0 is not a constant.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #198.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

dvv.py `S_THETA=-2.0` (dv/v per unit volumetric theta) implies a 0.1 m3/m3 wetting -> 20% dv/v, whereas observed ambient-noise seasonal dv/v is ~0.1-1% - the nominal sensitivity looks 1-2 orders too large. Sanity-check against a Hertz-Mindlin + capillary derivation and against observed dv/v-theta amplitudes; recalibrate or document the intended forward vs inverse convention. See `docs/peer_review.md` for the full reviews.

</details>
title: S_THETA on the depth-inverted shallow mean: compute what each band resolves as a kernel-weighted vadose-column integral

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** GWL method members on the #187 contract.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Retitle it 'GWL structural (method) members for the #187 contract'.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Kriged, beta-map and TFN (#23) anomalies are emitted as labelled members on the #187 member dimension.
2. Held-out-well interval coverage (#186-corrected) is reported with and without the method members.
3. Spread is mapped against well density, and the claim that spread is larger in data-sparse uplands is tested.
4. Members are not added in quadrature to an existing sigma.

Add #186, #187 and #23 to BLOCKED_BY.

### Problems found

- Depends on the TFN prototype #23 (open) and the beta-map path; not stated as blockers.
- The acceptance criterion ('explicit ensemble-sigma component') is structural, not a test of calibration.
- Roadmap-review R8 notes it is mis-scoped relative to the meteorological members that #191 needs.
- Queued in batch 19, ahead of #187 and #186.

### Physics assessment

Method spread is legitimate as a measure of structural uncertainty. Adding it as one more quadrature sigma term is not: kriging, beta-map and TFN share the same wells and forcing, so they are neither independent nor a calibrated sample of structural error, and the spread is at best a lower bound. The 'kriging sigma' it would add to is itself wrong until #186 back-transforms Stage-3 variance.

The ensembled quantity is the DTW anomaly (Aug 2026 comment). In a probabilistic twin, method members should be carried as members (#187 contract), not collapsed into a sigma. src/models/gwl_dynamic.py still has a single kriging path (lines 49-118).

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

## Context
The soil-moisture state now carries a **forcing ensemble** (TerraClimate vs PRISM → a forcing-σ UQ term). The GWL dynamic component (`src/models/gwl_dynamic.py`) currently has a single path — ordinary kriging of monthly well anomalies. For UQ parity and robustness, give GWL an analogous ensemble across dynamic *methods/forcings*.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a GWL forcing/method-σ term to the DTW uncertainty budget (alongside static RF, dynamic kriging, downscaling).
- [ ] Report the ensemble spread and where methods disagree (e.g., data-sparse uplands).

## Acceptance

Refs: #18, #8 (Stage-2 τ), #23 (TFN prototype). Mirrors the PR #27 soil-moisture forcing ensemble.

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Score the existing downscalers on held-out data.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Rewrite: the downscalers exist. Remaining work: score twi/regression/ml against bilinear on sub-footprint held-out data (NISAR 200 m pixels from #197; SNOTEL point sites), with wet/dry stratification; fit or justify the TWI coefficient; update representativeness_sigma from the measured gain. Drop the poroelastic option.

### Problems found

- The task 'implement ≥1 non-trivial downscaler' is already done.
- Its acceptance cannot discriminate between methods.
- The representativeness-σ update is undefined until a fine-scale score exists.

### Physics assessment

The implementation is done: twi, regression and ml downscalers are registered (downscale.py:131-243). The acceptance is ill-posed. A mean-preserving downscaler upscaled back to the coarse grid reproduces the coarse field by construction (downscale.py:165-170, :203-210), so 'improvement at native-scale validation (#29)' cannot tell it apart from bilinear. Fine-scale skill must be scored against sub-footprint observations: in-situ probes, NISAR at 200 m, or wells for GWL. The TWI downscaler uses a fixed 0.035 m³/m³ per σ (:155) that is unconstrained. TWI control of θ is state-dependent: strong when wet, weak when dry (Grayson et al. 1997). 'Poroelastic head propagation for GWL' is not a downscaling mechanism.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Part of #18. Tracked for draft PR #27.

## Context
Downscaling is now **modular** (`src/models/downscale.py` — `register_downscaler` / `downscale(method=...)`), but the only implemented method is **`bilinear`**, which is *pure resampling*: it adds no new fine-scale information (the representativeness σ quantifies exactly that). The registry passes each downscaler the fine static **covariates** (envelope / terrain / baseline) so smarter methods can exploit them without touching call sites. This issue adds at least one.

## Tasks
- [ ] Implement ≥1 non-trivial downscaler, e.g.:
  - covariate regression of the coarse→fine residual on the fine static field (envelope, HAND, TWI);
  - ML super-resolution trained on high-resolution observations (e.g. SMAP-to-fine, NISAR);
  - physics-based redistribution — TWI/TOPMODEL wetness for θ, poroelastic head propagation for GWL.
- [ ] Register it and make it selectable via `soil_moisture_90m(downscaler=...)` / `gwl_dynamic_90m(downscaler=...)`.
- [ ] Quantify the fine-scale skill gain vs `bilinear` **at native-scale validation** (#29), and update the representativeness σ so the budget reflects the smarter method.

## Acceptance
- A registered, selectable non-bilinear downscaler with a measured improvement over the resampling baseline; representativeness σ updated accordingly.

Refs: #18, #29 (native-scale validation supplies the score).

</details>
title: Data-informed / model-driven downscaler beyond the bilinear resampling baseline

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Waits until the PI names the stations, frequency bands and dv/v product.

**Audit verdict:** hold-human

### Specification

Apply needs-human-decision until the PI names the stations, the band set and the product, then split. (30a, data plane, agent-ready after that decision): fetch and QC the real banded dv/v with processing-ensemble Cd (dvv.py:235-281) into the #189 observation-record schema, with station kernels from a local Vs0(z). (30b, blocked by #198c/#164/#189): estimate operator parameters with withheld wells and SNOTEL, using a spatial block holdout. Remove the 'third independent estimate' language. AC: posterior predictive dv/v residual whiteness and coverage on held-out epochs, and no fit to the same wells used for scoring.

### Problems found

- The data source is a human decision: which network/stations (PNSN, Rainier, DAS), which product (codameter/NoisePy), the reference convention, and data rights.
- The body references draft PR #27, which has since merged; the tracking text is stale.
- The 'third independent estimate' framing contradicts #198.
- Calibration and validation targets coincide.
- The S_sk·β·B formula in the body and in dvv_coupling.py:19 is not dimensionally specified (science-review S4).
- It sits unblocked in batch 28 with #45/#50/#51.

### Physics assessment

Ingesting real dv/v is the most important missing piece in the family; every 'cross-check against measured dv/v' AC elsewhere (#85, #121-123) is untestable without it. As written the issue is wrong in two places. (1) It asks to 'invert real dv/v → GWL & θ … as a third, independent estimate'. That contradicts #198 and the Aug-2026 audit (dv/v is H applied to the state, with covariance HBH^T+R, never an independent field). (2) It calibrates the poroelastic and van Genuchten parameters 'against boreholes', then quantifies agreement against the same well and SNOTEL estimates. Using calibration targets as validation is circular unless wells are held out (#189 holdouts). The probe also shows the current 0.1-4 Hz bands cannot see θ in the top 1 m at all (no kernel node shallower than 5 m; a top-5 m signal is recovered at about 1%), so 'invert real dv/v → θ' is physically unsupported without >~10-50 Hz data or DAS.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #198.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Part of #18, implements the observational input for #19. Tracked for draft PR #27.

## Context
`src/models/dvv_coupling.py` implements the forward (states → banded dv/v) and inverse (banded dv/v → GWL & θ) operators from the gaia-hazlab soil-hydromechanical memory framework, and a **demonstrative** closed loop recovers both states (r≈1) from *modelled* dv/v. It is not yet driven by real data. This issue promotes it to operational.

## Framework (already encoded)
- Superposition: `Δv_obs ≈ Δv_sat + Δv_vad`, depth kernel `Δv(r,t) ≈ ∫ K(z) Δv(r,z,t) dz`.
- Saturated / low band → head: `(dv/v)_sat = −S_sk·β·B·Δh` → `d_wt`.
- Vadose / high band → θ: `V_s=√(G/ρ_b)`, Hertz-Mindlin `G(P_e)=G_ref(P_e/P_ref)^{1/3}`, van Genuchten retention.

## Tasks
- [ ] Ingest measured ambient-noise dv/v in frequency bands (codameter / denolle-lab; https://denolle-lab.github.io/codameter/), mapped to the pilot grid.
- [ ] Define/apply the band→depth sensitivity kernel K(z) (regional network → depth-averaged; DAS → explicit V_s(z) if available).
- [ ] **Calibrate** the poroelastic (S_sk, β, B) and vadose (Hertz-Mindlin G_ref/n, van Genuchten α/n/m) parameters against boreholes / soil texture / lab (currently nominal, calibration-pending).
- [ ] Invert real dv/v → GWL & SM; assimilate as a **third, independent** estimate alongside the terrain/climate and SNOTEL/SMAP estimates.

## Acceptance
- Real dv/v inverted to GWL & θ on the pilot with calibrated parameters; agreement quantified vs the other estimates; feeds the soil-mechanics state (#19).

Refs: #18, #19 (dv/v soil mechanics), dvv-coupling-framework (https://mdenolle.github.io/dvv-coupling-framework), soil-memory (https://gaia-hazlab.github.io/book/soil-memory/).

</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Split into validation-only pieces per product.

**Audit verdict:** split

> **Agents:** implement one slice per PR, use `Refs #29` (never `Closes`), and leave this issue open until every slice is accepted.

### Specification

Split into: (a) run validate_smap.py on the v0.4 domain with quality and VWC masking and a depth caveat, then commit the JSON, as validation only; (b) NLDAS-v3 as an inter-model check; (c) GRACE: either drop it or require TWS compartment accounting at mascon scale over a larger region; (d) NISAR goes to #197. Remove 'calibrate against SMAP', or require a frozen time split.

### Problems found

- Omnibus issue spanning four products with different readiness.
- Its acceptance uses a product as both calibration and validation.
- GRACE is effectively out of scope at this domain size.
- It absorbed #110, but the roadmap review warns that the closure does not establish a delivered SMAP evaluation.

### Physics assessment

Upscale-then-compare is correct. Four physics defects. (1) Task 2 'calibrate/bias-correct θ against SMAP' turns the one independent check into a calibration target (audit S2); SMAP must be held out, or split by time. (2) SMAP is 0-5 cm against the model's root zone, and dense western-Cascades forest (VWC > ~5 kg/m²) degrades L-band retrievals; the quality flag must be applied. (3) GRACE senses total water storage, not groundwater (science-review S11), and one mascon (~300 km) exceeds the whole 141x170 km domain, so it carries essentially no spatial information here. (4) NISAR duplicates #197. The SMAP fetcher and validate_smap.py exist, but no smap_validation.json is committed.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Part of #18. Tracked for draft PR #27.

## Context
Calibration/assimilation against coarse remote-sensing products must happen at **the sensor's native spatial and temporal scale** — you upscale the 90 m model to the product grid (area-mean) and score there, never downscale the product to 90 m. The primitive exists (`src/models/downscale.py` → `upscale_to_grid`, `native_scale_comparison`); this issue wires real products through it.

Crucially, **SMAP gives the first genuinely *independent* θ validation** — it is outside the P&PET forcing chain, unlike the current TerraClimate `soil` cross-check (which shares forcing, so its r=0.98 is only a consistency check).

## Tasks
- [ ] **SMAP** L3/L4 soil moisture fetch (NASA Earthdata login required — document auth); upscale 90 m θ → SMAP grid; `native_scale_comparison` (bias/RMSE/corr) at native res + cadence.
- [ ] Calibrate/bias-correct θ against SMAP at native scale.
- [ ] **NLDAS-v3** soil moisture (independent LSM) as a second native-scale check.
- [ ] **GRACE**/GRACE-FO storage anomalies for the **GWL** side (basin-scale storage) at native (coarse) scale.
- [ ] Hooks for **NISAR** (upcoming, high-res InSAR soil moisture) so it drops in when data is available.

## Acceptance
- SMAP native-scale comparison reported (independent θ validation: r/bias/RMSE); at least one calibration/bias-correction applied at native scale; Earthdata auth documented.

Refs: #18 (epic), #20 (independent validation). Upscaling primitive landed in PR #27.

</details>
title: Native-scale calibration/validation vs SMAP, NISAR, NLDAS-v3, GRACE (upscale-then-compare)

### Specification

Split. (A) Agent, milestone v0.2, runs first: fetch DNR 100k geology for DOMAIN.bbox_4326; complete the crosswalk on the formation/unit-name field; drop the Miocene->CRBG age rule (key CRBG on Grande Ronde/Wanapum/Saddle Mountains names); add a lahar class; rasterize and build the domain raster on the v0.4 grid; commit per-domain cell and well counts. (B) needs-human-decision: geologist review of the crosswalk before any hazard run. Add BLOCKED_BY edges from #3/#6/#7/#10/#47 to (A).

### Problems found

- Mixes agent work (download the public DNR 1:100k data, list units, map, rasterize, count) with a human geologist sign-off.
- Makefile `domains` targets the legacy terrain_hand_90m.tif grid (Makefile:145-153), not DOMAIN western-cascades-v0.4.

### Physics assessment

This is the critical unblocker. data/processed/lithology_crosswalk.json is a STARTER (56 LITHOLOGY values). Its refine rule (GEOLOGIC_AGE contains 'miocene' -> class 3 CRBG) is wrong for this domain: the western Cascades are full of Miocene andesite and intrusive units, and CRBG is essentially absent from the v0.4 box. The body says lithology 'never affects GWL prediction', but it does gate validation and masking, so errors silently remove domains.

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Umbrella tracking issue for repositioning this repo from a groundwater-only product to
**gaia-soil-reanalysis**: a coupled subsurface-state estimator producing three state
variables — soil moisture, groundwater level (the mature module today), and soil
mechanical properties — each with a **static** and a **dynamic** source, feeding the
liquefaction / landslide / flood digital twins.

The differentiator vs. hydrology-only teams (HydroShare/HydroFrame) is the **dv/v** channel:
ambient-noise seismic velocity change as a dynamic observational constraint that jointly
informs the water table (saturated, poroelastic) and vadose-zone saturation.

| State variable | Static source | Dynamic source |
|---|---|---|
| Soil moisture | SOLUS100 / POLARIS | reanalysis / remote sensing |
| Groundwater level | obs-anchored RF baseline | climate-response / TFN |
| Soil mechanics | SOLUS / Vs30 (Sanger & Maurer) | **dv/v** |

References: soil-memory (https://gaia-hazlab.github.io/book/soil-memory/),
dv/v-coupling-framework (https://mdenolle.github.io/dvv-coupling-framework),
codameter (https://denolle-lab.github.io/codameter/).
