**Rescoped 2026-10-18 for the MODFLOW 6 groundwater core.** Plan and design record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-modflow-groundwater-core/plan.md` (#273); epic #274.

## Purpose
Lowland models that touch Puget Sound need a head-dependent coastal boundary.

## Deliverable
`src/features/coastal_boundary.py` and `data/processed/coastal_ghb_90m.parquet`: shoreline cells
on the 90 m ledger grid (aggregable to k x 90 m), boundary head = mean sea level converted to
NAVD88 from NOAA tide stations in the domain (Seattle 9447130, Tacoma 9446484) with the datum
offset source stated, a freshwater-equivalent head note, and a GHB conductance prior from
nearshore sediment thickness and K with its source.

## Inputs and conventions
Heads m NAVD88. Seawater intrusion is out of scope and stated as such.

## Acceptance
- Datum conversion checked against the published station datum sheet values (test).
- Shoreline cell count and length reported; no inland cell flagged.

## Hard blockers
Blocked by: none.

## Advisory follow-ups
Score near-coast wells once a coastal model runs.


<details><summary>Scope before the 2026-10-18 MODFLOW refactor (archived, not current)</summary>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Fix sea level at the shoreline only; score near-coast wells.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Rewrite as: impose head=MSL (NAVD88 offset, VDatum) on shoreline cells only, with a Dupuit/Ghyben-Herzberg inland profile as a soft prior; add a valley/riparian groundwater sink in water_budget (coordinate with #175); acceptance on held-out near-coast wells (bias and RMSE versus distance from shore), plus fraction of DTW<0 cells outside NWI wetlands/floodplain. Add BLOCKED_BY 10:[21].

### Problems found

- The acceptance 'coastal cells converge to sea level ± tidal range' is physically and quantitatively wrong.
- Targets only legacy Stage-1/3 files, not the water budget that drives the twin.
- Depends on the domain raster (#21) and the dist_coast raster (DataHub fetch_gaia dist_coast).
- 'DTW<0 only in floodplain/tidal (<0.1%)' conflicts with real valley-floor wetlands and artesian wells, which upstream QC currently deletes.

### Physics assessment

Partly wrong physics. The water table equals mean sea level only AT the shoreline. Inland it rises (Dupuit/Ghyben-Herzberg; tidal forcing also raises the mean inland head, cf. Nielsen 1990). A 2 km / HAND<=10 m 'coastal' cell therefore should NOT 'converge to sea level ± tidal range'. Puget Sound's ~3-4.5 m tidal range also makes that band nearly untestable. HAND already references the nearest drainage, so a HAND-based prior implicitly carries a stream-stage boundary, and sparse gauge stage adds little. The real defect is in the water budget: valley cells (HAND<=d0) have no groundwater sink (water_budget.py:193-196). No coastal or stage code exists anywhere in src/.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Part of #1. Depends on #2.

## Context
The field is interpolated without explicit hydrologic boundary conditions.

## Hydrologist rationale
The wells *see* boundary conditions the model must honor: at the shoreline the water table is
pinned near **sea level** (Puget Sound / coastal aquifers), and along streams the water table is
coupled to **stream stage**. Ignoring them lets the interpolant drift to non-physical heads near
the coast and rivers — exactly the low-lying, liquefaction-prone, road-bearing corridors.

## Tasks
- [ ] Impose a coastal Dirichlet-style constraint: head → mean sea level (with tidal/SLR offset)
      at the `coastal` boundary; do **not** smooth across it.
- [ ] Couple valley-floor cells to stream stage (NHD + gauge/stage where available) as a soft prior.
- [ ] Verify no over-land water table (DTW < 0) outside active floodplains/tidal zones.

## Acceptance
- Coastal cells converge to sea level ± tidal range; stream-adjacent cells track stage; DTW<0
  only in floodplain/tidal cells (<0.1%).

## Downstream relevance
- **Geotech/DOT:** coastal and river corridors carry the most road infrastructure and the
  highest liquefaction + lateral-spread + embankment-failure exposure.

Affected: `src/models/interpolate_residuals.py`, `src/models/baseline_regression.py`, paper §Stage 3.


</details>


</details>

body:
**Rescoped 2026-10-18 for the MODFLOW 6 groundwater core.** Plan and design record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-18-modflow-groundwater-core/plan.md` (#273); epic #274.

## Purpose
A well observes the head of its screened interval, not the water table unless the interval
brackets the phreatic surface (`src/features/well_hydrostratigraphy.measurement_target`). With
MODFLOW layers the operator must weight the layers the screen crosses.

## Deliverable
In `src/models/observability.py` (or `src/models/obs_wells.py`): `well_head_operator(well,
mf6_grid, framework)` returning layer weights (transmissivity-weighted over the screened
thickness) and the model cell, the measurement target (water table / semiconfined / confined),
and a representativeness variance. Wells with no screen data get an inflated variance from a
declared rule, or are refused for water-table use.

Time handling: discrete heads are the raw timestamped measurements, not the site-month medians
in `data/processed/nwis_gwlevels_domain_monthly.parquet`; the operator evaluates the model at
the measurement time (asynchronous). Where only monthly aggregates exist, the operator is the
monthly mean of daily model heads, and the median-vs-mean gap enters R.

## Inputs and conventions
Screens from #277; layers from #276. Heads m NAVD88. Vocabulary from
`src/models/hydro_state.py`.

## Acceptance
- A screen fully inside one layer gives weight 1 on that layer; a screen across two layers gives
  transmissivity weights summing to 1 (tests).
- A confined-unit well is never returned as a water-table observation.
- On continuous recorders, (monthly median minus the value on the assigned day) is compared with
  R and reported.

## Hard blockers
Blocked by: #276, #277.

## Advisory follow-ups
#47 per-domain error tables can reuse the measurement-target classes.


<details><summary>Scope before the 2026-10-18 MODFLOW refactor (archived, not current)</summary>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Single owner for sorting wells by screen depth and aquifer (#46 merged here), keeping water-table wells only.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Make #9 the single owner (close #46 into it). Tasks: (1) fetch site metadata (well depth, screen top/bottom, aqfr_type_cd, nat_aqfr_cd) for domain wells via the OGC monitoring-locations collection; (2) require measurement_target=='water_table' for the Stage-1/2/3 targets in both pipelines; (3) keep DTW<=0 and flowing wells as censored/flagged rows, not drops; (4) report counts and median DTW per target and per domain; (5) make lahar-capped areas a screening flag. Leave the operational DA records to #189.

### Problems found

- Duplicate of #46 (and overlaps #189); the roadmap review recommends consolidating #9/#46/#189.
- Stale premise: it says 'screen is depth-based', but a richer classifier now exists and is simply unused.
- The domain path has no site metadata to screen on.

### Physics assessment

Correct and high-value. The classifier exists: well_hydrostratigraphy.measurement_target (:129-197) uses flowing, aqfr_type_cd, screen and depth evidence, and qc_nwis.py:309 attaches it. But no training set uses it. baseline_regression.py:140-144 applies the depth-only watertable_wells, which keeps unknown-depth wells (:83-96). The v0.4 baseline_wt_domain.py:94-95 applies no screen at all, and its wells (download_nwis_domain) carry no metadata. Dropping DTW<=0 everywhere (baseline_regression.py:136, baseline_wt_domain.py:95, download_nwis_domain.py:104) biases valley fill deep and removes artesian evidence. 'Cross with confined_basalt' is nearly moot in western-Cascades-v0.4. The physically relevant confining units here are Qva below Vashon till and the Osceola/Electron lahar cap (rainier3d leverage R6c).

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Part of #1.

## Context
`src/data/qc_nwis.py` flags deep wells (`is_deep_well`), but the screen is depth-based.

## Hydrologist rationale
The product target is the **shallow, unconfined** water table. The NWIS network mixes water-table
wells with **confined/multi-aquifer** wells (Columbia Basin CRBG at 50–150+ m, heavily pumped with
10s of m of decline). A pure depth cutoff misclassifies shallow confined heads and deep unconfined
water tables. Screening must be **aquifer-aware** (well-construction + hydrogeologic unit), or those
heads corrupt the training target.

## Tasks
- [ ] Cross the `confined_basalt` / `volcanic_deep` domain (#2) and NWIS well-construction
      (screen depth, aquifer code) to flag confined / multi-aquifer wells.
- [ ] Exclude them from the shallow water-table training set; retain them in a separate table for QA.
- [ ] Document the screening decisions and counts per domain.

## Acceptance
- Training set is demonstrably shallow-unconfined; confined wells quarantined with reasons.

## Downstream relevance
- Prevents pumped confined declines from leaking into the shallow field both hazard models rely on.

Affected: `src/data/qc_nwis.py`, paper §Data.


</details>


</details>

body:
## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Sensor-noise (nugget) variance per geologic unit, applied after #186.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Rewrite: estimate τ² per domain with prior_calibration (REML, OOF residuals, physical m²) on time-pooled anomalies. Apply it in whichever Stage-3 is canonical (name it) after the #186 back-transform. Acceptance: held-out well standardized residual sd within [0.9, 1.1] per domain, and nugget CI reported. Add BLOCKED_BY 7:[186, 21].

### Problems found

- Premise 'default/zero nugget' is stale or incorrect.
- Must land after #186 (same function; #186 is P0 and needs-human-decision but is NOT held by the queue script).
- prior_calibration.py already implements a REML Matérn plus nugget on OOF residuals in physical units; the body does not mention reusing it.
- Which Stage-3 is operational is ambiguous: gwl_dynamic.py (kriged anomalies) or legacy interpolate_residuals.py.
- 'No spurious bullseyes' is not testable as written.

### Physics assessment

The concept is right: the nugget equals measurement plus representativeness variance. It is incomplete: aliasing a synoptic read into a monthly median, and screen/vertical mismatch, also belong in it. The stated premise is wrong: interpolate_residuals.py:85-91 lets PyKrige auto-fit an exponential variogram, nugget included, but in NORMAL-SCORE space (:77-83). The nugget is therefore dimensionless and cannot simply be 'set to 0.3-1 m²'. This is the same unit defect as P0 #186. A per-domain, per-month fit is infeasible with MIN_SITES_PER_MONTH=30 (:36); use a time-pooled variogram.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: #186.

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Part of #1. Depends on #2.

## Context
Stage 3 ordinary kriging of residuals currently uses default/zero-nugget variogram settings.

## Hydrologist rationale
"Stay close to the data while predicting between sensors" is a single deliberate knob: the
**nugget**. A zero-nugget exact interpolator *looks* faithful but overfits aliased, biased point
measurements and produces spurious bullseyes; an over-smoothed krige departs from the wells. The
nugget should equal the **representativeness variance** of the domain (a 90 m cell vs a point
well: ~0.3–1 m² in homogeneous fill, several m² in fractured rock), so each well is honored to
within what it actually represents and the field reverts to the physical prior between wells.

## Tasks
- [ ] Estimate representativeness variance per domain (short-lag variogram structure / co-located
      well pairs) and set the Stage 3 nugget from it (not 0, not default).
- [ ] Expose nugget + range as per-domain parameters in `interpolate_residuals.py`.
- [ ] Diagnostic: residual-at-well ≤ measurement + representativeness error after assimilation.

## Acceptance
- Nugget is data-derived per domain; no spurious near-well bullseyes; documented.

## Downstream relevance
- Controls whether the upland field LandLab ingests is faithful-but-noisy or smooth-but-biased.

Affected: `src/models/interpolate_residuals.py`, paper §Stage 3.


</details>

**In plain words:** Check water-table timing at continuous recorders once they are ingested (#235).

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Add a prerequisite issue for continuous-recorder ingestion (gap below). Require recorders held out from calibrate_fluxes/#137 fitting, with a frozen partition list. Score daily data: phase in days, KGE on anomaly, recession constant. Score synoptic wells like-season with an aliasing term. State explicitly that the amplitude/April-peak targets are calibration diagnostics. Add BLOCKED_BY 6:[recorder-ingest gap, 21].

### Problems found

- No continuous-recorder data path exists: download_nwis*.py pull only the OGC field-measurements collection (download_nwis_domain.py:35) and qc_nwis.py has no recorder flag.
- Unknown how many continuous recorders fall inside the v0.4 domain; the first task should count them.
- Overlaps #100 (April peak), #131 (storm delay validated against a continuous well) and #189 (holdouts).
- Needs the domain raster for per-domain tables.

### Physics assessment

Correct and important: separate spatial from temporal skill, and compare synoptic wells in like seasons. Three problems. Phase '±1 month' at monthly cadence is too coarse for the storm-timing landslide claim; it needs daily recorder data. The seasonal amplitude 1.06 m and the April peak are already CALIBRATION targets (notebooks/calibrate_fluxes.py:36 AMP_OBS; #100), so scoring them again on the same well population is circular (audit S2). Recession should be scored with a master-recession or episodic recession fit on well hydrographs.

### Order and dependencies

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Part of #1.

## Context
Validation is purely spatial. The well network is mostly **synoptic/periodic**; only a minority
are continuous transducer records.

## Hydrologist rationale
Two distinct skills must be measured separately: *spatial* (between wells) and *temporal* (does
the model capture the seasonal cycle, phase, and recession at a site?). Comparing a monthly model
value to an intermittent measurement also carries **seasonal aliasing** (PNW unconfined amplitude
~1–3 m), so comparisons must be like-season.

## Tasks
- [ ] Leave-one-recorder-out validation at continuous wells: seasonal amplitude error, **phase
      within ±1 month** of observed peak/trough, and recession-limb skill (KGE on the anomaly).
- [ ] Characterize per-domain seasonal amplitude from the continuous recorders; use it to bound
      the aliasing term when scoring synoptic wells.
- [ ] When validating against synoptic wells, compare **like-season only** (same month/season).

## Acceptance
- Temporal score table per domain; phase error and recession KGE reported; aliasing term
  quantified and applied to synoptic comparisons.

## Downstream relevance
- **Landslides:** storm-season **timing** of the shallow water table is the landslide trigger;
  a model right on average but wrong on phase is wrong for the DOT use case.

Affected: `src/evaluation/`, `src/data/qc_nwis.py` (recorder flag), paper §Validation.


</details>

## Revised scope — approved by the PI, 2026-10-08

**In plain words:** Run the per-domain error gates on the v0.4 grid with proper block cross-validation and confidence intervals.

**Audit verdict:** rewrite

### Specification

Retitle to 'Run + port per-domain gates to v0.4'. Tasks: (1) residual-variogram block sizing, reusing prior_calibration's OOF residuals; (2) per_domain_cv in baseline_wt_domain.py; (3) delete the 200 km default and make the --domain-absent path exit non-zero; (4) GroupKFold over unique blocks, plus a bootstrap CI on RMSE/bias; (5) align the pixi and Makefile tasks. Acceptance: committed per-domain JSON on the v0.4 grid with CIs. Add BLOCKED_BY 3:[21].

### Problems found

- Mostly implemented; the remaining work is running it and porting it, which the body does not describe.
- Never run on real data: the committed block_cv_metrics.json is the pooled 200 km fallback.
- Not ported to v0.4 baseline_wt_domain.py (:112-114 uses fixed 10 km GroupKFold).
- pixi `baseline` omits --domain (pixi.toml:95), so the gate is silently skipped.
- The committed folds 0 and 4 are identical (BlockShuffleSplit repeats with few blocks), so the 5-fold mean is effectively 4-fold.
- No n-dependent confidence interval on per-domain RMSE; with MIN_WELLS_FOR_CV=20 a pass/fail call is statistically weak.
- Cannot run until the lithology raster exists (#14/#21).

### Physics assessment

The code landed: domain_gates.py:27-34 has the gates table and :93-139 runs per_domain_cv with variogram blocks. Two physics flaws remain. (a) estimate_variogram_range is fit to raw DTW y (:116). Raw-DTW variance is dominated by topography (prior_calibration.py:8-14 says so explicitly), so the block size should come from the variogram of held-out residuals (Roberts et al. 2017). (b) The MIN_BLOCK_M=2 km clamp contradicts the body's 'sub-km in fractured rock'. The thresholds are reasonable targets. A 0.75 m RMSE on long-term median DTW is still coarser than the 0.1-0.2 m liquefaction sensitivity cited in #47.

### Order and dependencies

Blocked by: none (beyond the queue-guard PR, #231).

Audit record: `docs/reviews/2026-10-08-physics-backlog-audit/` (PR #229). New issues from the audit: #230–#271.

---

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

Part of #1. Depends on #2 (domain mask).

## Context
Current Stage 1 gate is `Spatial block CV RMSE < 8 m for PNW`
(docs/gwl_hybrid_framework.qmd, §Validation) with **200 km** CV blocks.

## Hydrologist rationale
An 8 m RMSE is meaningless for the application: in the Duwamish/Green/Puyallup valley fills
the *entire* seasonal + spatial DTW range is ~2–5 m and liquefaction triggering is sensitive
at the sub-meter level. 200 km blocks are larger than the whole Puget Lowland and pool all
settings, so the pooled score is dominated by the easy (lowland) regime and flatters the
product where it is weakest. Gates must be **stratified by domain** and CV blocks sized to the
**local variogram range**.

## Tasks
- [ ] Replace the global gate with per-domain RMSE / bias / coverage gates:
  | Domain | RMSE target | RMSE threshold | \|bias\| |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | unconsolidated_valley_fill | ≤ 0.75 m | ≤ 1.5 m | < 0.25 m |
  | unconsolidated_basin | ≤ 1.5 m | ≤ 2.5 m | < 0.5 m |
  | fractured_upland | report-only | mask if > range | report |
  | volcanic_deep / confined_basalt | n/a — masked (#4) | — | — |
  | coastal | ≤ 1.0 m (incl. boundary, #10) | ≤ 2.0 m | < 0.3 m |
- [ ] Spatial block CV with block size = empirical variogram range **per domain** (km in fill,
      sub-km in fractured rock), not a fixed 200 km.
- [ ] `src/evaluation/cross_validate.py`: report metrics per domain; emit `block_cv_metrics.json`
      keyed by domain; fail the gate per domain.

## Acceptance
- CI/validation reports a table by domain; pooled-only metrics are removed.
- Block size is documented and derived from the variogram, not hard-coded.

## Downstream relevance
- **Geotech/DOT:** the fractured_upland row is the landslide-relevant accuracy statement;
  being honest ("report-only / mask") is required before LandLab ingests it.

Affected: `src/evaluation/cross_validate.py`, paper §Validation Strategy (see #11).


</details>

<details><summary>Original issue body (kept for history)</summary>

## Context

A groundwater-hydrologist review (USGS / water-district perspective, PNW) of the GWL
space–time framework concluded that the current validation and uncertainty design is
**hydrogeologically naïve**: it uses a single global accuracy gate, region-spanning CV
blocks, and a fixed-radius confidence mask that ignore PNW flow systems and the
intermittent, spatially biased, shallow-only nature of the well network.

The governing principle from the review: **honor the wells (ground truth for shallow,
unconfined water), be honest between them, and never claim skill where neither dense
data nor the assumed physics hold — a hazard product is better silent than confidently
wrong.**

## Why this matters now — two downstream reviewers, two regimes

- **Liquefaction (Sanger & Maurer GLM):** needs the **valley floors** — well-dense,
  shallow, where the product can and must be accurate (sub-meter).
- **Landslides & roads (LandLab; incoming geotechnical / DOT reviewer):** needs the
  **hillslopes and fractured uplands** — exactly the regime the hydrologist flagged as
  weakest (sparse wells, fractured Cascade/Olympic rock, fast storm-driven pore-pressure
  response). Pore pressure is the proximate landslide trigger, so the LandLab coupling
  has a first-class stake in how we model and bound uncertainty in the uplands.

This epic tracks turning the review into concrete, testable work. Acceptance targets are
**stratified by hydrogeologic domain** rather than pooled.

## Sub-issues



## Acceptance for the epic
- The global `RMSE < 8 m` gate, 200 km CV blocks, and 50 km confidence mask are retired.
- Validation, masking, and uncertainty are all **per hydrogeologic domain** and
  **calibrated** (interval coverage verified).
- Upland/hillslope behavior is explicitly coordinated with the LandLab landslide study.
**Foundation**
- [ ] #2 — Hydrogeologic domain mask layer (everything below strata on this)

**Validation (retire the global gates)**
- [ ] #3 — Per-domain validation gates + variogram-sized CV blocks (retire `<8 m` / 200 km)
- [ ] #6 — Temporal validation at continuous recorders (phase, recession, aliasing)
- [ ] #11 — Rewrite the paper's Validation Strategy section to match

**Uncertainty (make σ trustworthy)**
- [ ] #4 — Variogram-driven confidence mask (retire fixed 50 km)
- [ ] #5 — Calibrated uncertainty: coverage / PIT / CRPS check

**Modeling fidelity (stay close to the data)**
- [ ] #7 — Stage 3 nugget = representativeness variance (stay-close-to-data knob)
- [ ] #8 — Stage 2 response time τ conditioned on aquifer type
- [ ] #9 — Aquifer-aware deep/confined well screening (shallow-only target)
- [ ] #10 — Coastal & stream boundary conditions (sea level, stream stage)

**Downstream coupling (geotech / DOT reviewer)**
- [ ] #12 — LandLab / geotech bridge: hillslope water table for landslide & road hazard


</details>
